category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Retrying only failed items in a batch
prompt: A Lambda function receives 10 messages from a standard SQS queue, catches a format error for one message, and saves the other 9. Without calling the queue's delete API from Lambda, you want to treat the successful items as complete and retry only the failed item until it reaches the DLQ. What should you do?

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and return the failed message ID
choices.explanation: This lets Lambda identify the individual item that failed.

choices.text: Reduce the batch size and batching window
choices.explanation: This reduces the impact of a failure on other items, but the response still does not distinguish successful and failed items.

choices.text: Throw an unhandled exception for the one failed item
choices.explanation: The entire batch is treated as failed.

choices.text: Shorten the visibility timeout
choices.explanation: This does not report item-level success or failure, and can cause duplicates if the timeout is shorter than the processing time.

source.label: LambdaのSQSエラー処理

learning.reason: This lets Lambda identify the individual item that failed.
learning.concept: A partial batch failure response does not make SQS exactly-once. Design writes to be idempotent.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Reverting to the previous version
prompt: Multiple clients refer to the same Lambda alias ARN. After changing a library, you want to send only part of the traffic to the new code and be able to revert manually to the previous version immediately. How should you do this without adding another router or release service?

choices.text: Set the Lambda reserved concurrency
choices.explanation: This controls concurrency, not the traffic split between versions.

choices.text: Overwrite the function's $LATEST code each time
choices.explanation: This cannot represent partial routing to the previous version or calls pinned to a version.

choices.text: Create a function URL for each version and route requests in the clients
choices.explanation: This requires routing changes in the clients and cannot preserve the same ARN.

choices.text: Publish versions and configure weighted routing on the alias
choices.explanation: The alias can manage traffic distribution between two published versions.

source.label: Lambdaエイリアスの重み付きルーティング

learning.reason: The alias can manage traffic distribution between two published versions.
learning.concept: With CodeDeploy, you can automate a canary shift of the alias and roll back based on alarms.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Conditional registration
prompt: Payment callbacks may send the same order ID concurrently. Register the initial state in DynamoDB only the first time, and prevent later retries from overwriting the state of an order that has already been processed. How can you do this without using an additional lock table?

choices.text: Set an attribute_not_exists condition on PutItem
choices.explanation: The condition check and write are performed as one operation.

choices.text: Use UpdateItem to unconditionally set the state to its initial value
choices.explanation: A retry would overwrite the existing state.

choices.text: Use GetItem to check whether the item exists, then call PutItem without a condition
choices.explanation: Another process can register the item between the check and the write.

choices.text: Run a strongly consistent Scan first
choices.explanation: Even a read of the latest state does not prevent a race with a subsequent write.

source.label: DynamoDB PutItem

learning.reason: The condition check and write are performed as one operation.
learning.concept: Evaluating the uniqueness condition as part of the data store write avoids relying on a preliminary application-side check.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Direct browser uploads
prompt: An API accepts product images. Its backend identifies the member and selects a single destination key for each upload. The browser should PUT directly using a signed request, without obtaining credentials, and its upload permission should expire after 10 minutes.

choices.text: Allow everyone to use PutObject through the bucket policy
choices.explanation: This would allow unauthenticated users to upload objects, including to keys other than the designated key.

choices.text: Change only the S3 CORS rules
choices.explanation: This controls browser origin restrictions, but does not authorize S3 API requests.

choices.text: Have the backend issue a presigned PUT URL for the specified key
choices.explanation: This delegates the specified operation for a limited time.

choices.text: Issue a presigned GET URL with an expiration
choices.explanation: A signature is tied to an HTTP operation and does not grant PUT permission.

source.label: S3署名付きURLでのアップロード

learning.reason: This delegates the specified operation for a limited time.
learning.concept: Anyone who receives a presigned URL can use it while it is valid. Limit the recipient, key, and expiration.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: SDK permissions
prompt: A payment Fargate task in a cluster can write to DynamoDB, but a separate analytics task must not be able to write. Both tasks can already pull the same private ECR image. Without configuring static keys in the SDK, where should the new write permission be granted?

choices.text: Add DynamoDB permissions to the application's task role
choices.explanation: This controls the credentials available to the application running in the task.

choices.text: Inject static access keys into the task as environment variables
choices.explanation: The application could use them, but this does not meet the requirement to use the task's temporary credentials.

choices.text: Change the ECR repository policy
choices.explanation: This controls access to the image, not writes to DynamoDB.

choices.text: Change only the task execution role
choices.explanation: This role is primarily for startup operations by the ECS agent; it does not grant permissions to the application in the task.

source.label: ECSのタスクIAMロール

learning.reason: This controls the credentials available to the application running in the task.
learning.concept: Separate the permissions used to start a task from those used by its application after startup.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Retries and duplicate payments
prompt: The payment provider treats requests with the same key and the same payload as the same operation. The payment succeeds, but the response is lost; the worker should retry even if it restarts. The initial request and the retry may be sent by separate processes.

choices.text: Save only a processed flag after receiving the response
choices.explanation: If the response is lost after the payment succeeds, the flag is never set.

choices.text: Delete the SQS message before calling the payment provider
choices.explanation: This reduces duplicate processing, but if the call fails, the business operation is lost.

choices.text: Reuse the same idempotency key on retries for each order
choices.explanation: The payment provider can recognize the requests as the same operation.

choices.text: Assign a new idempotency key to every request
choices.explanation: The payment provider will see each request as a separate operation.

source.label: 変更操作の冪等性

learning.reason: The payment provider can recognize the requests as the same operation.
learning.concept: A timeout from an external API does not prove that the operation failed. Preserve request identity when retrying.

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Resuming from the failed record
prompt: A Lambda function reading from Kinesis processes a batch in order. If the fourth record fails, it should be possible to retry starting at least from the fourth record. Avoid reprocessing the first three records that succeeded.

choices.text: Catch the error and return success
choices.explanation: This advances the checkpoint past the failed record as well.

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and return the sequence number of the failed record
choices.explanation: Stream processing uses the lowest failed sequence number as the restart position.

choices.text: Fail the entire batch
choices.explanation: The retry starts from the beginning, which does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Return the SQS message ID in the failure response
choices.explanation: Kinesis requires the record's sequence number.

source.label: LambdaのKinesis部分バッチ応答

learning.reason: Stream processing uses the lowest failed sequence number as the restart position.
learning.concept: SQS and Kinesis differ in the identifiers used for partial batch failure responses and in the scope of retries.

sourceLabel: Lambda partial batch responses for Kinesis

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
title: Writing an Order and Publishing an Event
prompt: An order service writes orders to DynamoDB and delivers events to downstream services. It must prevent an event from being lost if the process crashes immediately after the write, and reduce duplicate processing by consumers.

choices.text: Send a notification from the same application after the write, and delete the order if the notification fails
choices.explanation: If the process stops, the compensating action might never run.

choices.text: Use DynamoDB Streams to capture changes after they are committed, and make consumers idempotent
choices.explanation: The committed change is tied to an event source, and consumers can handle redelivery.

choices.text: Resend the results of a Scan in full every minute
choices.explanation: This cannot distinguish change events and requires resending every item.

choices.text: Publish the event first, then write the order
choices.explanation: If the write fails, an event is delivered for an order that does not exist.

source.label: DynamoDB Streamsの変更データキャプチャ

learning.reason: The committed change is tied to an event source, and consumers can handle redelivery.
learning.concept: With a dual write, only one of the two operations may succeed. Even when consumers read committed changes, they still need to be idempotent.

sourceLabel: Change Data Capture with DynamoDB Streams

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Isolating Overall Latency and API Call Delays
prompt: Only p99 latency is worsening for an order API that spans multiple services, including Lambda. You need to identify slow segments for the same sampled request, from the response at the entry point through downstream SDK calls.

choices.text: Instrument each service, propagate trace context, and inspect the traces in X-Ray
choices.explanation: You can trace the timing of an individual request by service and downstream-call segment.

choices.text: Inspect only CloudTrail management events
choices.explanation: They do not record application processing time by segment.

choices.text: Compare the average Duration of all functions
choices.explanation: This does not track outliers or causal relationships across requests.

choices.text: Compare only the times when alarms were triggered by each function
choices.explanation: This cannot connect the path taken by the same request.

source.label: AWS X-Rayのトレースとセグメント

learning.reason: You can trace the timing of an individual request by service and downstream-call segment.
learning.concept: Metrics help identify impact and timing; distributed tracing helps locate bottlenecks for an individual request.

examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化

category: アプリ開発、デプロイ、デバッグ
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Detecting Conflicts with Optimistic Locking
prompt: Two editors read the same DynamoDB item, modify it, and save it. You need to prevent the person who saves last from silently overwriting the earlier change and prompt the user to reload when a conflict occurs.

choices.text: Condition the update on the version number that was read, then update to the latest version number
choices.explanation: The condition check and update are performed atomically.

choices.text: Read the version number after updating and notify the user if it differs
choices.explanation: Once the overwrite has happened, the earlier edit is no longer protected.

choices.text: Extend the item's TTL before writing
choices.explanation: An expiration time does not control the order of edits.

choices.text: Read with strong consistency, then update unconditionally
choices.explanation: Another update can occur after the read.

source.label: DynamoDBの楽観的ロック

learning.reason: The condition check and update are performed atomically.
learning.concept: A conditional write can be used either to ensure a new unique registration or to detect conflicts by comparing the version of an existing item.

title: A Result Page Empty After Filtering
prompt: An order search uses the DynamoDB Query operation with the customer ID and uses a FilterExpression to keep only shipped orders. As it reads from newest to oldest, one page has an empty Items result but returns a LastEvaluatedKey. There may still be orders to display in the UI. What should the process receiving this page do?

choices.text: Keep the first LastEvaluatedKey received and hide all later pages because the result is empty.
choices.explanation: While LastEvaluatedKey is present, unread candidates may remain. An empty Items result alone does not indicate that the query is finished.

choices.text: Use that LastEvaluatedKey as ExclusiveStartKey in the next Query, and continue fetching pages until no key is returned.
choices.explanation: The filter is applied after each page is read. Even when the result is empty, the next read position is valid.

choices.text: Set ExclusiveStartKey to the key of the last order displayed on the screen and start again from there.
choices.explanation: The last displayed position differs from the last evaluated position. This can cause already-filtered pages to be read again.

choices.text: Set ConsistentRead on the same Query and stop paging if Items is empty.
choices.explanation: Strong consistency affects how up-to-date the data is. It does not change the read limit or when the filter is applied.

source.label: DynamoDB Query

learning.reason: Pass the read position from before filtering out candidates to the next request.
learning.concept: Handling the displayed row count separately from the data scan position prevents a search from stopping at an empty page.

title: Validation gaps across media types
prompt: An API Gateway REST API accepts multiple Content-Types that use the same JSON format. A request with a missing required field returns 400 for application/json, but the same invalid body reaches Lambda when sent with a new media type. The API must apply the same body validation to JSON media types added in the future. Which setting should be added to the existing body validator?

choices.text: Configure the same body mapping template for each Content-Type and accept the input if it can be transformed.
choices.explanation: Mapping changes the format sent to the backend. It does not provide method request model validation.

choices.text: Make the Content-Type header a required request parameter and enable parameter validation only.
choices.explanation: Parameter validation checks whether the header is present, but it does not validate the JSON body.

choices.text: Add a JSON schema for the input as the default model for the Lambda integration response.
choices.explanation: The integration response is processed after the integration and is not a control point before the request body is passed to Lambda.

choices.text: Associate the method request model with the $default Content-Type.
choices.explanation: This setting uses the same model regardless of Content-Type, so body validation also applies to JSON types without an individual model assignment.

source.label: API Gateway REST APIのリクエスト検証

learning.reason: Enabling a body validator also requires an input model to be applied.
learning.concept: Selecting a model based on a header and validating a body against a JSON schema are separate steps.

sourceLabel: API Gateway REST API request validation

title: HTTP success and business failure in synchronous execution
prompt: An order API calculates a quote using a synchronous Express workflow. The API treats a request as successful even when the state machine fails because the payment requirements are not met, although the SDK's StartSyncExecution call returns HTTP 200. The workflow definition and synchronous contract must remain unchanged. Which fix is appropriate?

choices.text: Check the status in the SDK response and treat output as a successful result only when the status is SUCCEEDED.
choices.explanation: HTTP success indicates that the synchronous execution API call was processed. The workflow's outcome is reported in status.

choices.text: Treat the request as successful unless the SDK throws an exception, and return an empty quote if output is missing.
choices.explanation: The same misclassification remains because an execution can fail while the API returns HTTP 200.

choices.text: Get the executionArn from the response and determine the synchronous Express execution's outcome using DescribeExecution alone.
choices.explanation: This method is not needed to determine the outcome of a normal Express execution; the synchronous response already includes status.

choices.text: Switch to the asynchronous StartExecution API and return a successful quote as soon as an ARN is received.
choices.explanation: Acceptance of the start request does not mean the calculation is complete, and this does not meet the requirement to return the business result synchronously.

source.label: Step Functions StartSyncExecution

learning.reason: Transport-level success and success of the work performed have separate statuses.
learning.concept: The caller should build its response based on the workflow's business outcome.

title: Job events that confirm batch inference completion
prompt: An application processes input records in S3 using Amazon Bedrock batch inference. Multiple jobs write to the same bucket, and S3 creates multiple files for each job. The application must run the finalization step exactly once for a job when the entire job reaches Completed, rather than on individual files. Which design avoids additional polling and duplicate processing when events are redelivered?

choices.text: Receive any S3 output-file creation event and treat the job as complete based on the first object alone.
choices.explanation: The presence of one file does not indicate that the entire job has finished, and it does not identify the job's status.

choices.text: Use EventBridge to receive Bedrock Batch Inference Job State Change events, select only events where detail.status is Completed, and use the job ARN as the unique key for the finalization result.
choices.explanation: This starts processing in response to the state change for the entire job and makes the finalization idempotent if the same completion notification is delivered again.

choices.text: Treat the job as complete as soon as CreateModelInvocationJob returns a job ARN, and use the last ARN received as the output destination for all jobs.
choices.explanation: Receiving a job ARN indicates that job creation was accepted; it does not indicate that output files have finished being generated.

choices.text: Subscribe to every Bedrock state change and use the EventBridge event ID from the first notification to run the finalization step once.
choices.explanation: An event ID does not select the final state for a job. This also receives notifications for job start and in-progress states.

source.label: BedrockのEventBridgeジョブ状態通知

learning.reason: Distinguish notifications for output objects from completion notifications for the jobs that produce them.
learning.concept: Combining the target job's identifier with the state that must be finalized lets the application process events for multiple jobs independently.

title: Scope of SDK throttling control
prompt: An AWS SDK that supports retry modes runs in a single process. A background migration job makes many updates to a DynamoDB table, while a membership API reads a different table with low latency. For the migration job, the initial request rate must also be adjusted automatically in response to throttling, without allowing that adjustment to delay the membership API's initial requests. How should the clients be configured?

choices.text: Share a single adaptive client across the process and set the API's maximum number of attempts to 1.
choices.explanation: An adaptive client shares initial-request rate limiting, which cannot be isolated by changing the number of retries.

choices.text: Use standard mode for the migration job, increase the maximum number of attempts, and apply client-side rate limiting to initial requests as well.
choices.explanation: Standard mode uses backoff for retries but does not apply adaptive mode's initial-request rate control.

choices.text: Use an adaptive client dedicated to the migration table and a separate standard client for the membership API.
choices.explanation: Separating the clients isolates adaptive request-rate adjustments and prevents them from affecting the membership API's rate control.

choices.text: Use different timeouts for the migration job and API, and configure two timers on a single adaptive client.
choices.explanation: Different timeouts do not change the shared request-rate control within the client.

source.label: AWS SDKの再試行モード

learning.reason: Adaptive rate adjustment operates at the SDK client level.
learning.concept: Throttling can occur on a per-resource basis, so the scope of client sharing determines the scope of its effects.

title: Preserving order within each customer while processing concurrently
prompt: A FIFO queue receives events for creating, updating, and canceling customer contracts. Events for each customer must remain ordered, but one slow customer's processing must not make other customers wait. Workers also process messages in group order within a received batch. How should the keys be specified when sending messages?

choices.text: Use one shared MessageGroupId for all customers and a different MessageDeduplicationId for each event.
choices.explanation: Even if duplicate events are suppressed, all customers still belong to a single ordering group.

choices.text: Use the customer ID as the MessageGroupId, and use the same unique event ID as the MessageDeduplicationId when resending that event.
choices.explanation: Ordering is managed per customer, so other customer groups can be delivered independently. Resent events can also be identified.

choices.text: Use a separate MessageGroupId for each event ID, and always assign the same MessageDeduplicationId to a given customer.
choices.explanation: A customer's events would be split across groups, breaking their order, and legitimate successive events could be treated as duplicates.

choices.text: Set the operation type as the MessageGroupId, and record the customer ID and sequence number in the payload.
choices.explanation: A customer's create, update, and cancel events would span multiple groups, so the queue could not preserve their order.

source.label: SQSのMessageGroupId

learning.reason: Assign the same group to a series of events that must be ordered relative to one another.
learning.concept: Design the ordering unit and the deduplication unit separately.

title: Diagnosing failures in asynchronous functions
prompt: A billing PDF generation Lambda is invoked asynchronously by another service. Only when it ultimately fails, the input event and response information from the failure must be sent to an existing standard SQS queue used for investigations. The function code cannot be changed to collect failed events. Which configuration should be selected?

choices.text: Set a standard SQS queue as the function's dead-letter queue and read the function's response information from the message body.
choices.explanation: A Lambda dead-letter queue receives the original event. It does not include the invocation's response payload.

choices.text: Set a standard SQS queue as the destination for successful invocations, and have the consumer retrieve only failed completions.
choices.explanation: Invocations that fail after retries are not sent to the destination for successful invocations.

choices.text: Have the invoking SDK send the Invoke API response it receives to the queue and treat that result as the final failure.
choices.explanation: The acknowledgment for an asynchronous invocation does not contain the final result of the function's later execution.

choices.text: Set a standard SQS queue as the OnFailure destination for asynchronous invocations and process the invocation record.
choices.explanation: For a final failure, the invocation record includes the original request and the function's response information.

source.label: Lambda非同期呼び出しの保持レコード

learning.reason: Retaining only the original event and keeping a diagnostic record containing both the invocation request and response serve different purposes.
learning.concept: The available failure-handling mechanisms depend on the invocation mode. This configuration applies to asynchronous Lambda invocations.

title: Maintaining consistency when retrying a multipart upload
prompt: An application uses an S3 multipart upload to transfer a large file in parallel. Part 3 succeeded on the first attempt, but the application determined that it was corrupted and reuploaded the correct data using the same UploadId and PartNumber. The application uses consecutive part numbers starting at 1, and the SDK retains the latest part responses. The upload must be completed without any additional lookups. What should the client do?

choices.text: Keep only the ETag from the reuploaded part 3, then send a completion request with each part number and its corresponding ETag in number order.
choices.explanation: Uploading the same part number replaces the previous part. Use the latest part and its corresponding ETag when completing the upload.

choices.text: List both the original and corrected part 3, placing the entry with the newer ETag last.
choices.explanation: Parts are identified by number; the upload does not combine two parts listed under the same part number.

choices.text: Assign the corrected part 3 a different number and expect S3 to restore the original logical order from the ETags.
choices.explanation: S3 combines parts in the specified number order. It does not infer their logical placement from ETags.

choices.text: Pass only the UploadId in the completion request and have S3 assemble the latest ETag list.
choices.explanation: The client must provide the list of part numbers and their corresponding ETags in the completion request.

source.label: S3マルチパートアップロード

learning.reason: The part list used at completion is the client's record, updated with the result of any resend.
learning.concept: Tracking the upload ID, part numbers, and latest ETags separately supports retries using the same part number.

title: Checking and updating the same inventory item in a transaction
prompt: To finalize an order, an application must check and decrement the remaining quantity in a DynamoDB inventory item and add a separate order item. Neither change may succeed without the other. A prototype TransactWriteItems request failed because it included both a ConditionCheck and an Update for the same inventory item. How should it be restructured?

choices.text: Keep the inventory condition in ConditionCheck and perform the update to the same inventory item before the transaction.
choices.explanation: If adding the order fails, the inventory change remains, so the two changes are not atomic.

choices.text: Only reverse the order of ConditionCheck and Update for the same inventory item.
choices.explanation: Regardless of action order, a transaction cannot target the same item with two actions.

choices.text: Put a ConditionExpression that checks the remaining quantity directly on the inventory Update, and include it in the same TransactWriteItems request as the order Put.
choices.explanation: There is only one action for the inventory item, and the entire transaction is rolled back if its condition fails.

choices.text: Combine the inventory update and order addition with BatchWriteItem, then resend only the failed items.
choices.explanation: BatchWriteItem does not provide a conditional Update for an item or atomicity across the entire operation.

source.label: DynamoDBのトランザクションAPI

learning.reason: Combine the update condition into a single action on the target item.
learning.concept: You can specify a condition for each item while making writes across multiple items atomic.

title: Hide expired items during the TTL deletion delay
prompt: A DynamoDB screen searches for valid quotes by customer ID. Each item has an expiration time in epoch seconds, and TTL is used to delete old quotes. You want expired quotes excluded from search results without waiting for TTL to physically delete them. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Use a FilterExpression in Query to keep only items whose expiration time is later than the current time.
choices.explanation: TTL physical deletion can be delayed, but expired items can be excluded with a condition applied after the read.

choices.text: Change Query to ConsistentRead so that TTL deletion is visible as soon as the expiration time is reached.
choices.explanation: Strong consistency reads writes and deletes that have completed. It cannot anticipate a TTL deletion that has not yet occurred.

choices.text: Use ProjectionExpression for each item to exclude the expiration attribute from the selection.
choices.explanation: Omitting an attribute from the returned data does not exclude the entire item based on its expiration time.

choices.text: Change the TTL attribute on existing items to milliseconds so that the deletion process can evaluate the expiration time more precisely.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB TTL interprets values as epoch seconds. Changing them to milliseconds does not improve deletion precision.

source.label: DynamoDBの期限切れ項目の扱い

learning.reason: Include the availability-window check in the read, independently of physical deletion.
learning.concept: Asynchronous deletion can help manage storage costs, but enforcing a strict expiration boundary for users requires a separate check.

title: What to reuse across warm invocations
prompt: A Lambda function processes API requests from multiple tenants in sequence. You want to reduce the overhead of creating a new HTTPS connection for every request, but tenant-specific headers and authorization results must not carry over to the next request. The SDK client can accept per-request headers as arguments. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Place the SDK client and the previous tenant's headers outside the handler, then reuse the previous values in the same environment.
choices.explanation: Because the execution environment is reused, tenant-specific values would also remain for the next request.

choices.text: Create the client inside the handler and create a new connection pool on every invocation.
choices.explanation: Request-specific state would not persist, but this would not meet the requirement to reduce initialization costs through connection reuse.

choices.text: Establish the first connection outside the handler and always use the same socket without accounting for the possibility that it may be closed.
choices.explanation: An idle connection can be closed, so a reusable client must also be able to reconnect.

choices.text: Initialize a request-independent SDK client outside the handler, enable connection reuse, and generate headers inside the handler for each request.
choices.explanation: Only the client is reused; tenant-specific state, including authorization results, remains scoped to the lifetime of each request.

source.label: Lambda実行環境再利用のベストプラクティス

learning.reason: Distinguish settings reused with the execution environment from state that must be recreated for every request.
learning.concept: Reducing initialization costs does not justify sharing state across tenant boundaries.

sourceLabel: Lambda execution environment reuse best practices

title: Automatically clean up one-time schedules
prompt: An application creates an EventBridge Scheduler schedule for each reservation to send a notification once. Many completed schedules remain and consume schedule quotas. The schedule group must remain in use, and Scheduler retries on failure must remain enabled. How can you automatically delete only the schedule after it completes, without introducing a separate deletion job?

choices.text: Use a one-time expression and leave the default setting for completion behavior.
choices.explanation: Not firing again after execution is different from deleting the schedule resource.

choices.text: Set ActionAfterCompletion to DELETE when creating the schedule.
choices.explanation: Scheduler deletes the schedule after its final execution. No separate periodic cleanup is needed.

choices.text: Shorten the asynchronous event expiration for the Lambda target.
choices.explanation: How an event passed to the target is handled does not change the lifetime of the Scheduler resource.

choices.text: Enable automatic deletion at the end of execution by removing DeleteSchedule permission from the role that invokes the target.
choices.explanation: Changing the target's execution permissions does not configure the action to take after completion.

source.label: EventBridge Schedulerのスケジュール削除

learning.reason: Specify at creation time that the schedule itself should be deleted after its final execution.
learning.concept: Even a one-time schedule consumes quota as a created resource unless it is deleted.

title: Pass the raw body only when no mapping is defined
prompt: A REST API in API Gateway uses a non-proxy integration. Before migration, there are no templates, so the existing request body is passed through unchanged. After migration, you add one template for application/json and want Content-Type values without a matching definition to receive a 415 instead of being passed to the backend. Which single integration setting works for both stages?

choices.text: Set PassthroughBehavior to WHEN_NO_TEMPLATES.
choices.explanation: When there are no templates, the body is passed through; when a template exists, an unmatched media type is rejected.

choices.text: Set PassthroughBehavior to WHEN_NO_MATCH.
choices.explanation: The body is passed through when no template matches the media type, so unmatched requests would still reach the backend after migration.

choices.text: Set PassthroughBehavior to NEVER and create no templates before migration.
choices.explanation: Requests without an existing mapping would not pass through, so the raw body would also be rejected before migration.

choices.text: Require the Content-Type header with a request validator and leave the body passthrough setting at its default.
choices.explanation: Checking that the header exists does not determine whether a mapping for that media type exists.

source.label: API Gatewayの本文パススルー設定

learning.reason: Distinguish passing through unmatched requests from passing through only when no templates exist.
learning.concept: Method settings that validate the shape of a request body differ from integration settings that transform and pass the body.

title: Filter subscriptions by JSON body without changing the publisher
prompt: The SNS publisher puts the event type in `event.kind` in the JSON body and sends no message attributes. You want to send notifications with `kind` set to `shipment` only to a new SQS subscription, without affecting other subscriptions to the same topic. The consumer should not have to retrieve and discard unwanted messages. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Add a condition to the SQS queue policy that evaluates `event.kind` in the JSON body.
choices.explanation: A queue policy is used to authorize calls. It does not configure SNS to choose delivery destinations based on values in the message body.

choices.text: Attach the same filter policy to the subscription and leave its scope as `MessageAttributes`.
choices.explanation: Because the value is not in a message attribute, this cannot evaluate the desired JSON body.

choices.text: Set `FilterPolicyScope` to `MessageBody` for that subscription only, and configure a body filter that matches `event.kind` to `shipment`.
choices.explanation: SNS can evaluate the JSON body and filter delivery to this subscription. Policies for other subscriptions are independent.

choices.text: Use the topic access policy to reject bodies whose `kind` is not `shipment`.
choices.explanation: This cannot select deliveries per subscription and would also affect existing publishers or subscriptions.

source.label: SNS購読のフィルターポリシースコープ

learning.reason: Set the subscription filter's evaluation scope to the location where the event type is actually stored.
learning.concept: Even when the publisher represents an attribute in the body, choosing the subscription scope lets you filter messages without changing the publishing code.

title: Read only the file you inspected
prompt: A process overwrites a delivery configuration at a single S3 key. After inspecting the object with `HeadObject`, the application records its ETag and wants to call `GetObject` only for the content associated with the ETag it inspected. If the object changes before the GET and the condition no longer matches, the application must not download the object and must start the inspection over. Versioning is disabled. Which condition should it use?

choices.text: Pass the recorded ETag to `If-None-Match` and have the object returned when it matches.
choices.explanation: `If-None-Match` is used to retrieve content when the current value does not match, which is the opposite of the required behavior.

choices.text: Set `If-Match` on `GetObject` to the ETag from the inspection, and start the inspection over if the condition fails.
choices.explanation: S3 checks the ETag at the time of the GET and can prevent the content from being retrieved by returning 412 when it does not match.

choices.text: Download the latest content with `GetObject` and compare it with the saved ETag after receiving it.
choices.explanation: This can detect a change, but it does not meet the requirement to avoid downloading content that fails the condition.

choices.text: Call `HeadObject` again and, if the result is the same, call `GetObject` without a condition.
choices.explanation: The object could still change between the second check and the GET.

source.label: S3の条件付き読み取り

learning.reason: When inspection and retrieval are separate calls, put the validation condition on the retrieval itself.
learning.concept: Here, the ETag is used as a value for S3 to compare; you do not need to assume that it is always an MD5 hash of the entire file.

title: Distinguish tokens from the same issuer by their purpose
prompt: An HTTP API uses tokens from the same Cognito user pool, and its existing JWT authorizer validates the issuer and app client. You want read-only access tokens and ID tokens to be unable to call the order cancellation route. Cognito issues `orders/cancel` only to access tokens from a client that has cancellation permission. Which setting should you add?

choices.text: Change the JWT authorizer's audience from the app client ID to `orders/cancel`.
choices.explanation: The audience identifies the client; scopes represent the operations required by a route.

choices.text: Require an `Authorization` header only on the cancellation route.
choices.explanation: The presence of a header does not distinguish a read-only token from a cancellation token.

choices.text: Set `orders/cancel` as an authorization scope on the cancellation route and apply the same JWT authorizer.
choices.explanation: API Gateway compares the validated token's `scope` or `scp` claim with the route's authorization scopes. It can reject tokens without the cancellation scope.

choices.text: Shorten the cancellation route's cache duration to allow only short-lived ID tokens.
choices.explanation: Token lifetime and cache duration are separate from whether the token grants permission to perform the operation.

source.label: API GatewayのJWTオーソライザー

learning.reason: Validate both that the token was issued correctly and that it grants permission for the operation.
learning.concept: A route-specific authorization scope can limit operations even for tokens from the same issuer.

title: Bind ciphertext to a customer ID
prompt: An order service calls `Encrypt` with a symmetric KMS key and stores ciphertext separately for each customer. The service must use a shared key and detect a customer mismatch during decryption if ciphertext for another customer is accidentally retrieved. The caller's authorized customer ID is available. Which implementation should it choose?

choices.text: Include the customer ID in the `EncryptionContext` when encrypting, and construct the same entry from the authorized customer ID when decrypting.
choices.explanation: The `EncryptionContext` is additional authenticated data. Decryption fails unless its keys and values match those used during encryption.

choices.text: Store the ciphertext and customer ID in the same database record, and use the customer ID read from that record to decide whether to decrypt.
choices.explanation: If the ciphertext and its metadata are retrieved together by mistake, this cannot detect a mismatch with the customer who is authorized to access the data.

choices.text: Add the customer ID to a shared alias for the key during encryption, and specify only the current alias during decryption.
choices.explanation: An alias for a key is a reference to the shared key; it does not cryptographically bind the ciphertext to an individual customer ID.

choices.text: Specify the same shared key for encryption and decryption, and put the customer ID in the `GrantToken`.
choices.explanation: A `GrantToken` references a KMS grant; it is not additional authenticated data for the ciphertext.

source.label: KMS Encryption Context

learning.reason: Reconstruct the decryption context from the trusted customer ID.
learning.concept: An `EncryptionContext` is not a place to store secrets; it authenticates nonsecret context associated with the ciphertext. Access control is still required.

title: Short-Term Access to Multiple Private Files
prompt: A company distributes member-only training through CloudFront. Each training course consists of a manifest and many video segments, and during playback the player fetches the existing URLs on the same host as they are. Allow each member to access only the path for a specified course for 30 minutes, without changing any file URLs. The existing S3 origin is restricted to access through OAC. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Issue a CloudFront signed URL for only the manifest during member login.
choices.explanation: Signing the manifest URL does not automatically authorize video segments that have different URLs.

choices.text: Set the CloudFront cache TTL to 30 minutes for each course and invalidate the cache when a member logs in.
choices.explanation: Cache duration does not authorize viewers or restrict access to a course path.

choices.text: Generate S3 presigned GET URLs for each video segment and rewrite the manifest references each time.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirements to keep the URLs unchanged and deliver content through CloudFront.

choices.text: Issue CloudFront signed cookies with a custom policy that specifies the course path and expiration, and configure a trusted key group on the applicable cache behavior.
choices.explanation: The same signed cookie can authorize multiple related URLs, so the client-side URLs do not need to change.

source.label: CloudFrontの署名付きURLとCookie

learning.reason: Separate access rights from the URLs and limit the custom policy to the course path.
learning.concept: Restricting access to the origin and authorizing viewers in CloudFront serve different purposes.

title: Model Inference Without Internet Connectivity
prompt: Workers in a private subnet send inference requests to an existing model in Amazon Bedrock in the same Region. You cannot add a NAT gateway or an internet egress path to the VPC. In addition to the existing IAM permissions, which two settings are needed to use the SDK's standard regional endpoint unchanged?

choices.text: Create only an interface endpoint for the bedrock control plane.
choices.explanation: The endpoint for model management does not provide the runtime API used for inference.

choices.text: Create an interface endpoint for bedrock-runtime, and enable DNS resolution and DNS hostnames in the VPC as well as private DNS for the endpoint.
choices.explanation: This lets the standard runtime hostname resolve to the endpoint's private addresses inside the VPC.

choices.text: Create a gateway endpoint for Bedrock and add it to the workers' route table.
choices.explanation: Use an interface endpoint for a PrivateLink connection to Bedrock.

choices.text: Use the IAM InvokeModel permission to replace network access to the endpoint.
choices.explanation: Permission to perform an API action is separate from establishing an HTTPS connection over the network.

choices.text: Allow HTTPS from the workers in the endpoint's security group.
choices.explanation: Even when the hostname resolves to a private IP, the endpoint must allow TCP port 443 connections.

source.label: Amazon BedrockのPrivateLink

learning.reason: Model management APIs and inference APIs have different private endpoints.
learning.concept: IAM and endpoint policies control API operations, while DNS and security groups establish the network connection.

title: Inspect Model Output Outside the Model Call
prompt: An internal chat application is designed to allow the model provider to be changed, and the API for its current inference provider does not accept Bedrock guardrails. Keep the current inference provider, inspect only the model output with the organization's Bedrock guardrail before displaying it, and have the application return a different message if the guardrail intervenes. Which implementation is appropriate?

choices.text: Send the guardrail identifier to the current inference provider and display responses that do not recognize the identifier as is.
choices.explanation: The inference provider does not support this feature, so passing the identifier will not inspect the output.

choices.text: Pass the output text to ApplyGuardrail before displaying it, set source to OUTPUT, and handle any intervention.
choices.explanation: ApplyGuardrail can be used independently of a model invocation. Setting source to OUTPUT applies the policies for model output.

choices.text: Pass the output to ApplyGuardrail but always set source to INPUT, then use the result to decide whether the output passes the output policies.
choices.explanation: INPUT specifies that user input is being evaluated; OUTPUT is the value used to apply policies configured for model output.

choices.text: Send the same question to another Bedrock model and treat its new response with a guardrail as the inspection result for the original model output.
choices.explanation: Inspecting another model's response does not inspect the original output that will actually be returned to the user.

source.label: Bedrock ApplyGuardrail API

learning.reason: Run inference and inspection as separate calls, and branch on the inspection result before showing the output to the user.
learning.concept: When guardrails are used independently, the application is responsible for incorporating inspection into its control flow.

title: Restricting a Temporary Session That Uses a Shared Role
prompt: The role assumed by a report-generation service with AssumeRole is shared with existing processes and allows reads across all department prefixes. A single new job must be temporarily restricted to retrieving S3 objects for its assigned department. Do not change the role's existing permissions or trust relationship, and assume that the target bucket has no policy that grants permissions directly to the session. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Change the role's trust policy to the ARN of the target S3 objects.
choices.explanation: A trust policy specifies which principals can assume a role. It does not define the scope of a job's individual S3 operations.

choices.text: Put the department prefix in the AssumeRole RoleSessionName and use the role without changing its permissions.
choices.explanation: The session name itself does not restrict permissions.

choices.text: Use a consistent prefix in S3 GET requests and leave the original S3 permissions in place.
choices.explanation: Application conventions alone do not prevent credentials from being used to request a different key.

choices.text: Use a session policy with AssumeRole that allows only s3:GetObject on objects for the assigned department.
choices.explanation: The intersection with the session policy further restricts the permissions the role has for that session.

source.label: IAMのセッションポリシー

learning.reason: You can reduce the permissions of each session even when temporary credentials are issued from the same role.
learning.concept: A session policy does not add permissions to those held by the role.

title: Restricting Batch Reads to a Tenant’s Partition
prompt: In DynamoDB, the tenant ID is the partition key and the order ID is the sort key. Each tenant’s temporary role is tagged with a tenantId that the authentication process has authorized. You need to allow BatchGetItem with a least-privilege role and restrict every specified key to that tenant. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: For the BatchGetItem permission, specify dynamodb:LeadingKeys with ForAllValues:StringEquals and compare its value with the principal’s tenantId. Also require LeadingKeys to be present.
choices.explanation: Each requested key is evaluated, and the request is denied if even one key belongs to another tenant’s partition.

choices.text: Use dynamodb:LeadingKeys with ForAnyValue:StringEquals to check whether the batch contains a key for that tenant.
choices.explanation: This does not reject a mixed batch in which only some keys match.

choices.text: Allow only scans and attribute projections, omitting the partition key from the returned attributes.
choices.explanation: Restricting which attributes are displayed does not restrict reads of items belonging to other tenants.

choices.text: Add every tenant ID as a resource tag and use tag matching on the table as the sole basis for authorization.
choices.explanation: A table tag is a resource-level attribute and cannot restrict reads by individual item key.

source.label: DynamoDBの詳細なIAMアクセス制御

learning.reason: When a batch contains multiple keys, every key must be checked against the authorization condition.
learning.concept: ForAllValues can evaluate as true even when the condition key is absent. Combine it with a condition that requires the key to be present.

sourceLabel: Fine-grained IAM access control for DynamoDB

title: Authorizing an Encrypted Multipart Upload
prompt: An existing application role is allowed the required S3 object operations and kms:GenerateDataKey on the target KMS key. PutObject for a small file succeeds with bucket SSE-KMS, but a multipart upload to the same prefix using the same key fails midway with a KMS access-denied error. What is the minimum additional permission required?

choices.text: Add kms:DescribeKey for the target key.
choices.explanation: Allowing the role to read key configuration does not authorize the internal processing of encrypted parts.

choices.text: Add kms:Encrypt for the target key.
choices.explanation: S3 SSE-KMS multipart processing requires the combination of GenerateDataKey and Decrypt.

choices.text: Add kms:Decrypt for the target key to the role performing the upload.
choices.explanation: For multipart uploads, S3 reads the encrypted parts, so it requires Decrypt in addition to GenerateDataKey.

choices.text: Add only kms:ReEncryptFrom for the target key.
choices.explanation: Allowing re-encryption from another key does not replace the required Decrypt permission.

source.label: S3のSSE-KMSに必要な権限

learning.reason: Even with the same SSE-KMS settings, a single PUT and a multipart upload involve different S3 internal processing and key operations.
learning.concept: When only one part of an operation fails, compare the KMS operations required by the successful and failing paths.

title: Refreshing a Credential Cache Immediately After Rotation
prompt: An application caches Secrets Manager connection credentials in memory and uses them for new database connections. During operations, the AWSCURRENT version switches to a new password. Refresh the cache only when a new connection is found to fail with the old credentials, and do not rerun business operations that have already been submitted. Which implementation is appropriate?

choices.text: Call GetSecretValue again using the previously read VersionId, then reconnect with that value.
choices.explanation: Pinning the VersionId continues to retrieve the same old version after rotation.

choices.text: Read AWSCURRENT again with GetSecretValue, update the cache, and retry the new connection once.
choices.explanation: This retrieves the version pointed to by the current stage. Retry only connection establishment that has not yet handed off the operation.

choices.text: Always prefer AWSPREVIOUS and treat a failed connection with the old credentials as confirmation that the new password has been applied.
choices.explanation: AWSPREVIOUS is not the current version and may return a password that is already invalid.

choices.text: Use Secrets Manager ListSecretVersionIds to get the latest version ID and keep using the previously cached secret value.
choices.explanation: Updating version metadata alone does not change the password sent to the database.

source.label: Secrets Manager GetSecretValue

learning.reason: Retrieve the secret through the stage that identifies the current version instead of pinning a specific version.
learning.concept: If you use a cache, decide when to invalidate values that become stale after rotation.

title: Permissions for Routine Monitoring and Approved Unmasking
prompt: Some access logs that will be ingested into CloudWatch Logs contain identifying information that operations cannot immediately omit. Keep it masked during routine log viewing, and allow only an approved investigation role to read the unmasked data when needed. Which log group configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Encrypt the log group with KMS and add only kms:Decrypt to the investigation role.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest does not mask individual fields shown in Logs Insights based on the viewer.

choices.text: Completely remove the identifying information at ingestion and let investigators recover the original values with logs:Unmask.
choices.explanation: Values removed from the original data cannot be restored by CloudWatch’s unmask operation.

choices.text: Create an alarm for sensitive data monitoring and let the routine role inspect the relevant logs.
choices.explanation: An alert that data was detected does not hide the content later shown in searches or subscription filters.

choices.text: Mask the relevant data identifiers with a log group data protection policy, and grant logs:Unmask only to the investigation role when needed.
choices.explanation: Detected values are masked by default, and only the investigation role receives the permission needed to unmask them.

source.label: CloudWatch Logsの機密データマスキング

learning.reason: Distinguish masking data for users after ingestion from removing it before ingestion.
learning.concept: A data protection policy applies to events ingested afterward. Do not assume it has the same effect on existing logs.

sourceLabel: Sensitive data masking in CloudWatch Logs

title: Restricting KMS Use to a Specific Service
prompt: An application role reads and writes encrypted objects in S3 in ap-northeast-1. The application role only needs to use the target KMS key through S3; direct KMS API calls by the role and use through other services must not be allowed. No key operations are granted by any other allow statement. Which condition should be added to the key-use permission?

choices.text: Match kms:ViaService to s3.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com.
choices.explanation: This applies the permission only to KMS key operations performed by the specified service on the caller’s behalf.

choices.text: Match aws:RequestedRegion to ap-northeast-1.
choices.explanation: This can restrict the Region, but it does not distinguish direct KMS calls from calls made through S3 in the same Region.

choices.text: Match kms:CallerAccount to the application’s account ID.
choices.explanation: Even if the caller’s account matches, this condition does not identify the service used for the request.

choices.text: Use kms:EncryptionAlgorithm to specify only symmetric algorithms.
choices.explanation: Restricting the algorithm does not limit whether the call is made through S3.

source.label: KMSのViaService条件

learning.reason: Specify the permitted service path as a condition, in addition to the identity that uses the key.
learning.concept: Distinguish conditions used for KMS calls through a service from conditions that also apply to direct requests.

title: Restricting Read Access to Your Own Distribution
prompt: A private S3 bucket is used as a CloudFront REST origin, with requests signed by OAC. S3 Block Public Access is enabled, and the read permission granted to CloudFront must be restricted to one distribution. Which permission should the bucket policy specify?

choices.text: Set the AWS account root as the Principal so that all CloudFront configurations in the account can read the bucket.
choices.explanation: Trusting the entire account neither grants the required permission to the CloudFront service principal nor restricts access to an individual distribution.

choices.text: Grant object access to cloudfront.amazonaws.com and broaden the condition to include every distribution ARN in the account.
choices.explanation: Even within the same account, this expands the permission to every distribution.

choices.text: Grant cloudfront.amazonaws.com s3:GetObject on the target objects, and restrict AWS:SourceArn to the specified distribution ARN.
choices.explanation: The condition restricts the CloudFront service principal that accesses S3 through OAC to the intended distribution.

choices.text: Grant s3:GetObject to the session role of CloudFront viewers and do not apply bucket controls to OAC.
choices.explanation: CloudFront does not use viewers’ AWS roles to retrieve objects from S3.

source.label: CloudFrontのS3オリジンアクセス制御

learning.reason: Restrict permission for the service mediating delivery to the specific distribution that should be allowed.
learning.concept: Viewer permissions and the permission CloudFront uses to read from the origin are separate.

title: Scoping a Contractor’s Customer Engagement in a Role Trust Policy
prompt: An external monitoring service uses the same contractor IAM principal to assume roles for multiple customers. You want your role to be assumable only when the contractor is running a monitoring job for your organization. The contractor can assign a unique identifier to each customer. Which two options should be combined?

choices.text: Ask the contractor to set RoleSessionName to the customer name and audit that name in CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This can support auditing after the role is assumed, but it does not make engagement-specific authorization a requirement in the trust policy.

choices.text: Allow the contractor principal in the trust policy and require sts:ExternalId to match the value assigned to your organization.
choices.explanation: In addition to the principal, this verifies which customer the contractor is acting for when assuming the role.

choices.text: Require sts:ExternalId to match in the role’s permissions policy and put only the principal in the trust policy.
choices.explanation: The target role’s trust policy specifies the conditions for accepting an AssumeRole request.

choices.text: Share the same ExternalId with your organization and other customers, and have the contractor send that value for each monitoring task.
choices.explanation: A shared value cannot identify which customer engagement the target role is being assumed for.

choices.text: Have the contractor manage the value assigned to each customer and include that value as ExternalId in AssumeRole requests for your organization.
choices.explanation: The value that satisfies the trust policy condition must be sent independently for each customer.

source.label: IAMの委託先アクセスとExternalId

learning.reason: When trusting a contractor principal shared across customers, also set a condition that identifies the customer engagement at the time of role assumption.
learning.concept: ExternalId is not a substitute for long-term credentials; it is a context value assigned by the contractor for each customer.

title: Returning Existing Document Matches Without Generating an Answer
prompt: Add a feature to an internal search API that returns candidate documents from an existing Bedrock Knowledge Base. A separate service role handles ingestion and configuration changes, and the search API does not generate answers. Add only the permissions the application execution role needs to read from one knowledge base. Which permission should you grant?

choices.text: Allow bedrock:InvokeModel on the target model and include the knowledge base ID in the model input.
choices.explanation: Invoking a model does not grant permission to retrieve relevant documents from a knowledge base.

choices.text: Allow bedrock:Retrieve on the target knowledge base ARN.
choices.explanation: This permits only the retrieval API for the specified knowledge base.

choices.text: Allow bedrock:RetrieveAndGenerate and have the application discard the generated response text.
choices.explanation: Even if the response is unused, this operation performs generation in addition to retrieval.

choices.text: Allow bedrock:StartIngestionJob to start an ingestion process each time a search is performed.
choices.explanation: Updating a data index is not the operation used to retrieve candidate documents from existing content.

source.label: Bedrock Knowledge BasesのIAMアクセス許可

learning.reason: Grant the application role only the scope needed for the API operation it uses.
learning.concept: Separating retrieval, answer generation, and data ingestion in permissions makes it clear who can perform each operation.

title: Require TLS while preserving service integrations
prompt: Add a setting to an S3 bucket that denies HTTP access from clients. In an existing integration, some network conditions may be removed from the request context for calls made by AWS service principals. Which configuration enforces TLS for ordinary clients without breaking AWS service integrations through this policy’s Deny?

choices.text: Add an Allow that applies only when aws:SecureTransport is true, and keep all existing Allows.
choices.explanation: Adding an Allow does not deny a non-TLS path if an existing permission allows it.

choices.text: Deny all principals when aws:SecureTransport is false, then add a separate Allow for AWS service principals.
choices.explanation: A separate Allow cannot override an explicit Deny that applies to the request.

choices.text: Deny all requests from principals for which aws:PrincipalIsAWSService is false, regardless of whether they use TLS.
choices.explanation: This also denies legitimate HTTPS access by non-service principals.

choices.text: Apply an explicit Deny only when both aws:SecureTransport and aws:PrincipalIsAWSService are false.
choices.explanation: This denies non-TLS requests from ordinary clients while excluding AWS service principals from this Deny.

source.label: S3のポリシー条件キーの例

learning.reason: When a network-based Deny needs to exclude AWS services, scope the Deny through its conditions.
learning.concept: Conditions on Allows cannot cancel an explicit Deny, even when the conditions are distributed across separate statements.

title: A reusable development tag and immutable release tags
prompt: A single ECR repository stores dev-latest, which validation overwrites each time, and tags beginning with release-, which are used for reproducible releases. Developers and the production pipeline can both push to the same repository, but ECR must prevent an already-created release tag from being overwritten through either publishing path. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Make all tags mutable and use a lifecycle policy that retains release tags longer than development tags.
choices.explanation: Retention rules control when images expire. They do not prevent a push from reusing an existing release tag.

choices.text: Set IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION and use dev-latest as the exclusion filter that allows overwrites.
choices.explanation: Tags are immutable by default, with the single development tag as an exception that can be updated.

choices.text: Make all tags immutable and have the development pipeline overwrite dev-latest under the same name each time.
choices.explanation: Without an exclusion, overwriting dev-latest is also rejected.

choices.text: Set MUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION and specify only dev-latest in the exclusion filter.
choices.explanation: With mutability as the default, the exclusion makes matching tags immutable. That is the opposite of the requirement.

source.label: ECRイメージタグの変更可否

learning.reason: Define the repository’s default tag mutability and the exclusions that receive the opposite treatment.
learning.concept: Tag retention and tag overwrite controls are separate settings.

title: A configuration failure just after full deployment
prompt: An API’s configuration changes are deployed gradually with AWS AppConfig. The request failure rate rises several minutes after deployment to all targets, once normal traffic hits the change. Without adding monitoring logic to the application code or pipeline, you want a CloudWatch alarm to automatically roll back to the previous configuration for 15 minutes after the change reaches 100% of targets. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Extend the deployment strategy’s Deployment duration to 15 minutes and set Bake time to 0 minutes.
choices.explanation: Extending the deployment duration does not add a separate monitoring period after deployment reaches 100%.

choices.text: Set only the CloudWatch alarm’s evaluation period to 15 minutes, and let the AppConfig deployment complete when it reaches all targets.
choices.explanation: Once the deployment is considered complete, the alarm’s evaluation period alone does not provide automatic rollback during an AppConfig deployment.

choices.text: Register the alarm as a monitor for the AppConfig environment, configure a monitoring role, and set the deployment strategy’s Bake time to 15 minutes.
choices.explanation: During the bake time, the deployment remains incomplete even after reaching 100%, allowing automatic rollback based on the monitor.

choices.text: Register a configuration validator with AppConfig and set its timeout to 15 minutes, until the failure rate rises.
choices.explanation: A configuration validator checks whether the value being deployed is valid. It does not replace live monitoring or a post-deployment observation period.

source.label: AppConfig配布ストラテジー

learning.reason: Distinguish the point when a configuration reaches all targets from the point when the deployment is considered successful.
learning.concept: Deployment duration controls how quickly changes spread; Bake time controls the observation period after full deployment, when automatic rollback is still available.

title: An initial deployment with no rollback target
prompt: The ECS rolling update deployment circuit breaker and automatic rollback are enabled. The new tasks in a service created for the first time fail to start and reach the failure threshold. Task definition revisions from earlier exist, but this service has no completed deployment yet. What will ECS do?

choices.text: Find the immediately preceding task definition revision and redeploy the service with it.
choices.explanation: The rollback target is selected based on a completed deployment for that service, not on the revision number.

choices.text: Find the last task that transitioned to RUNNING and use that version, even if it did not pass health checks.
choices.explanation: A task’s transient individual state does not represent a completed deployment that can serve as a rollback target.

choices.text: Because this is the first deployment, rollback is unavailable, so the circuit breaker records the failure but continues starting new tasks in the same deployment.
choices.explanation: ECS stops starting new tasks for a deployment that has been marked as failed.

choices.text: Mark the deployment as failed and stop without starting new tasks because there is no COMPLETED deployment to roll back to.
choices.explanation: Automatic rollback requires a completed deployment for the same service.

source.label: ECSのデプロイサーキットブレーカー

learning.reason: Even with automatic rollback enabled, a completed deployment is needed as the recovery target.
learning.concept: The existence of a task definition revision does not mean the service has successfully deployed that revision.

title: A repushed image is not reflected in the function
prompt: A test Lambda function uses a container image created from the ECR `test` tag. The build successfully pushed a fixed image to the same `test` tag, but invoking `$LATEST` still returns the result from before the fix. No invocation uses an alias. Which procedure is required?

choices.text: Run Lambda `UpdateFunctionCode` with the same image URI, then verify after the update completes.
choices.explanation: Lambda resolves a tag to a digest when the function code is updated. Moving the tag in ECR alone does not update the function's code.

choices.text: Save the Lambda environment variables again and wait for a new execution environment to be used.
choices.explanation: Creating a new execution environment does not change the digest of the function image it references; a code update is required.

choices.text: Rescan the ECR image referenced by `test` and invoke the function after the scan completes.
choices.explanation: An image scan result does not update the Lambda function's code reference.

choices.text: Publish a version from the existing `$LATEST` only; this will pick up the latest `test` image in ECR.
choices.explanation: Publishing a version freezes the current function configuration. A separate code update is needed to retrieve the new digest from ECR.

source.label: Lambdaのコンテナイメージ更新

learning.reason: The content a Lambda function runs when it references a tagged image is determined by the resolved digest.
learning.concept: Complete publishing an image and deploying the application that uses it as separate steps.

title: Fast iteration during development with real services
prompt: A developer is testing a SAM application that includes an SQS event source mapping. The developer wants to verify real event delivery in a dedicated AWS stack while applying local code changes quickly whenever they are saved. Production deployments must continue through the existing pipeline. Which procedure should the developer use during development?

choices.text: Run `sam local invoke` in watch mode with the SAM CLI and automatically register the local function with the real event source mapping.
choices.explanation: Local invocation can simulate event input, but it does not let the real AWS-side mapping invoke a local function.

choices.text: Start `sam sync --watch` for both the development and production stacks, and use production pipeline approval only to notify the team of the result.
choices.explanation: This would apply local changes directly to production, which does not meet the requirement to manage production through its pipeline.

choices.text: Run `sam sync --watch` against the dedicated development stack and verify the integration behavior using the function deployed in AWS.
choices.explanation: Watch mode detects local changes and syncs them to the AWS development environment. This keeps development separate from the existing production deployment process.

choices.text: Since the template has not changed, repeatedly run `sam build` and wait for AWS to detect the built artifacts.
choices.explanation: `sam build` prepares artifacts; it does not automatically update the AWS development stack.

source.label: AWS SAMのクラウド同期

learning.reason: Choose between local execution and syncing to a cloud environment based on the scope of integration you need to verify.
learning.concept: Use watch-based rapid updates in an isolated development environment, while keeping production approval and deployment in the existing process.

title: Keep a snapshot of a database before replacement
prompt: A CloudFormation change set shows that an RDS DB instance will be replaced because of a configuration change. The update will proceed, but you want to retain a snapshot before the old DB is deleted as part of the replacement. The new DB must remain managed by the stack. Which attribute should you set in the template?

choices.text: Set only `DeletionPolicy: Snapshot` on the old DB resource.
choices.explanation: `DeletionPolicy` applies when a stack is deleted or a resource is removed from the template. A different attribute governs a change to the physical resource through replacement.

choices.text: Set `UpdateReplacePolicy: Snapshot` on the DB resource that will be replaced.
choices.explanation: For the supported DB resource, CloudFormation creates a snapshot of the old physical DB before deleting it during replacement, then manages the new physical DB as that logical resource.

choices.text: Use a stack policy to deny `Update:Replace` for the DB resource.
choices.explanation: This would prevent the replacement, but it would also prevent the required update to the new DB.

choices.text: Set `UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain` on the DB resource and treat retaining the old DB as creating a snapshot.
choices.explanation: `Retain` preserves the old physical resource itself. It does not specify creating a snapshot and then deleting the old DB during replacement.

source.label: CloudFormation UpdateReplacePolicy属性

learning.reason: A change set reveals whether replacement will occur in advance, allowing you to specify what happens to the old physical resource.
learning.concept: Different attributes apply when an update carries a logical resource forward and when a resource is removed from the template.

title: Validate a new Lambda version before shifting traffic
prompt: CodeDeploy will gradually shift a Lambda alias to a new version. Before any end-user traffic is sent to the new version, you want to run a synthetic request against that version. Treat a test failure as a deployment failure. Which two procedures should you use?

choices.text: Configure the synthetic test in an `AfterAllowTraffic` hook.
choices.explanation: This test runs after traffic has been shifted.

choices.text: Register a validation Lambda in the AppSpec `BeforeAllowTraffic` hook and invoke the version using its qualified ARN.
choices.explanation: This runs validation before the shift and lets you test the new version itself while the alias still points to the old version.

choices.text: In `BeforeAllowTraffic`, invoke only the production alias and treat its successful response as validation of the new version.
choices.explanation: Before the shift, the alias response does not validate the new version.

choices.text: On completion, use the deployment ID and hook execution ID with `PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus` to return `Succeeded` or `Failed`.
choices.explanation: CodeDeploy can use the hook validation result to decide whether to continue the deployment or fail it.

choices.text: Have the hook output the result and let CodeDeploy automatically score whether the hook Lambda completed successfully.
choices.explanation: The hook must report the validation result to CodeDeploy.

source.label: CodeDeployのAppSpecライフサイクルフック

learning.reason: Predeployment validation requires both selecting the version under test and reporting the result to the deployment.
learning.concept: The timing of the production alias shift and the timing of direct validation of an individual version can be separate.

title: Reviewing each pending release in order
prompt: A V2 CodePipeline pipeline uses a shared validation environment. Release candidates arrive in quick succession. Even if a running candidate is waiting for approval, candidates already in the queue must not be replaced by later arrivals; they must enter the review stage in arrival order. Parallel execution of candidates within a stage must also be avoided. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Set the execution mode to QUEUED so executions that pass through a stage are processed in queue order.
choices.explanation: Later executions do not overtake earlier ones; they wait in order at the entrance to a locked stage.

choices.text: Set the execution mode to SUPERSEDED and advance the newest candidate whenever an action for an older candidate finishes.
choices.explanation: A waiting execution can be replaced by a later one, so this does not meet the requirement to review every candidate.

choices.text: Set the execution mode to PARALLEL and rely only on manual approval decisions to prevent simultaneous entry into the shared validation stage.
choices.explanation: With PARALLEL, each execution proceeds independently. It is not a mode that makes later candidates wait in order at the stage level.

choices.text: Keep the execution mode as SUPERSEDED and add each candidate's commit SHA to the artifact name.
choices.explanation: Artifact names can help identify candidates, but they do not affect how stages allow candidates to overtake one another.

source.label: CodePipelineの実行モード

learning.reason: The execution mode determines whether a pipeline processes all waiting executions or prioritizes the latest one.
learning.concept: QUEUED processes waiting release candidates in order while limiting contention for a shared stage.

title: Emitting diagnostics when tests fail
prompt: Run integration tests in the build phase of CodeBuild. A nonzero exit from the test command must fail the pipeline, but a diagnostic summary must still be emitted from the same phase and retained in CloudWatch Logs. Which approach avoids handling the test exit code in a custom wrapper?

choices.text: Put the diagnostic commands after the tests in the same commands block and expect subsequent commands to run after a failure.
choices.explanation: Normally, when a command fails, later commands in the same commands block are skipped.

choices.text: Always turn test failures into shell success with a condition and emit diagnostics on the next line of the same commands block.
choices.explanation: This can run the diagnostics, but CodeBuild does not receive the test failure and therefore cannot fail the pipeline.

choices.text: Keep the tests in commands and put the diagnostic commands in the finally block of the same phase.
