choices.explanation: finally runs whether commands succeed or fail, while a preceding test failure remains a phase failure.

choices.text: Put diagnostics in an action in the next stage and rely on the failed build's output being passed through the normal path.
choices.explanation: The pipeline stops when the build fails, so the next stage cannot be relied on to run.

source.label: CodeBuildのbuildspecリファレンス

learning.reason: Place errors that should stop the work and diagnostic actions that must run after a failure in separate blocks.
learning.concept: CodeBuild's finally block ensures commands run; it does not turn failures into successes.

title: Resources temporarily skipped during rollback
prompt: A CloudFormation stack entered UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED. You continued the rollback by specifying only the resources that could not be restored through the normal procedure, and the stack reached UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE. What should you do with the skipped resources before the next application update?

choices.text: Inspect the actual resources and bring them into alignment with the state expected by the stack template before proceeding with the next update.
choices.explanation: Even if a skipped resource is displayed as complete, its actual configuration may not have been restored to match the template.

choices.text: Treat every resource shown as UPDATE_COMPLETE as repaired and run the next change set as is.
choices.explanation: That status does not indicate that CloudFormation restored the skipped resource's actual configuration to its previous state.

choices.text: Run drift detection only; it will automatically synchronize the actual resources with the template.
choices.explanation: Drift detection reports differences. Correcting them is a separate task.

choices.text: Disable update rollback in the next build and proceed with the update while leaving the differences in place.
choices.explanation: Changing how a failure is handled does not resolve inconsistencies between the template and actual resources.

source.label: CloudFormationの更新ロールバック継続

learning.reason: Check the actual state of the affected resources instead of relying only on the rollback status.
learning.concept: Skipping a resource is an exception that lets recovery proceed; afterward, the actual resource and the stack's recorded state must be reconciled.

title: Promoting a validated API snapshot
prompt: A single API Gateway REST API has test and prod stages. test points to a deployment ID whose changes have been validated. The API's editable definition already includes unvalidated changes for the next release. How can you promote exactly the API definition and mappings validated in test while preserving the prod URL and stage settings?

choices.text: Create a deployment from the current API definition and associate both prod and test with it.
choices.explanation: This would also include the unvalidated changes in the editable API definition in the new snapshot.

choices.text: Copy the test stage variables to prod and keep prod's current deployment ID.
choices.explanation: Stage variables alone do not change the deployed version of the methods and mappings used by the stage.

choices.text: Edit the definition of prod's existing deployment directly to match the test snapshot.
choices.explanation: Treat a deployment as a snapshot of the API definition and switch which deployment an existing stage references.

choices.text: Update the prod stage's deploymentId to the ID that was validated in test.
choices.explanation: This associates the existing snapshot in the same API with prod, so the validated definition can be used without creating another deployment.

source.label: API Gateway UpdateStage

learning.reason: Treat the API being edited separately from the deployment referenced by a stage.
learning.concept: Promoting the validated artifact as is avoids incorporating unvalidated changes when generating a new deployment.

title: Validate the relationship between two values
prompt: An AppConfig freeform JSON configuration specifies start and end times as integer minutes within the same day. Existing schema validation checks each value's type and range, but you want to verify that the start is earlier than the end before deployment begins, without changing the JSON body. Existing monitoring with CloudWatch alarms must remain in place separately. What should you add to the configuration profile?

choices.text: Set the same minimum and maximum for the start and end values, and treat their ordering as validated too.
choices.explanation: Even when each value is within its valid range, the relationship between the start and end values might still be invalid.

choices.text: Register a Lambda validator that reads the two values in the configuration body and raises an exception if their order is invalid.
choices.explanation: A Lambda validator can check business rules derived from the content of a freeform configuration before deployment.

choices.text: Extend the AppConfig bake time and wait for an alarm caused by invalid times after deployment.
choices.explanation: This can help detect a problem after deployment, but it does not validate the configuration before deployment.

choices.text: Add checks only to the consumers that read AppConfig, and evaluate the values when the first request arrives.
choices.explanation: Consumers can guard against invalid values, but this does not let AppConfig reject the configuration before deployment begins.

source.label: AWS AppConfigのバリデーター

learning.reason: Check the types and the relationship between configuration values before applying the configuration.
learning.concept: A validator that rejects invalid configuration before deployment and an alarm that monitors behavior after deployment address different failure modes.

title: Show the build-determined version on the approval screen
prompt: A CodeBuild action in CodePipeline calculates the artifact's RELEASE_VERSION, and you want to display that value in the description of the next manual approval action. You want to reference the value from the same pipeline execution without adding log or artifact parsing steps to the approval action. Which two steps are required?

choices.text: Specify RELEASE_VERSION in exported-variables in the CodeBuild buildspec, and set its value during the build.
choices.explanation: This makes the variable determined during that execution available as an output variable from the CodeBuild action.

choices.text: Print a value with the same name to standard output in CodeBuild, and have the pipeline convert each line into a variable.
choices.explanation: Normal build log output is not automatically made available as an action output variable.

choices.text: Set a namespace for the CodeBuild action, and reference the namespace-qualified variable in the approval action's custom information.
choices.explanation: A downstream action's configuration can reference variables output by an upstream action in the same execution.

choices.text: Enter the same artifact name as the CodeBuild result in the approval action, and have it extract the version number automatically at runtime.
choices.explanation: An artifact name is separate from a variable, and the approval information setting does not read values from files.

choices.text: Fix RELEASE_VERSION as a pipeline-level input variable before starting the pipeline.
choices.explanation: Because this version is determined inside the build, a value supplied when the pipeline starts cannot reference the resulting version.

source.label: CodePipelineのアクション出力変数

learning.reason: Pass a value calculated during execution from an upstream action to the configuration of a downstream action.
learning.concept: Setting an output-variable namespace makes it possible to distinguish variable names used by multiple actions.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Lambda throttles despite apparent headroom
prompt: You operate multiple Lambda functions in the same Region. A function without a reserved concurrency setting suddenly starts throttling, but ConcurrentExecutions for all functions is below the Region quota. Other functions have large reserved concurrency allocations. Which metric should you inspect directly to determine whether you have reached the limit, including capacity unavailable for on-demand invocations?

choices.text: View Duration for the affected function using Maximum to determine the capacity allocated to the function.
choices.explanation: Duration measures execution time and does not include the account's reserved capacity allocations.

choices.text: View only UnreservedConcurrentExecutions for the Region using Maximum.
choices.explanation: This is the number of currently running executions using unreserved capacity; it does not include reserved capacity that is allocated but idle.

choices.text: Sum ProvisionedConcurrentExecutions across all functions.
choices.explanation: This is the number of executions currently being handled by preinitialized environments; it does not show all capacity that reserved concurrency makes unavailable to other functions.

choices.text: View ClaimedAccountConcurrency for the Region using Maximum, and compare it with the account concurrency quota.
choices.explanation: It represents concurrency unavailable for on-demand allocation, combining capacity allocated through reservations and executions using unreserved capacity.

source.label: Lambda同時実行数のモニタリング

learning.reason: Account for capacity reserved for other functions, not just the number of executions observed.
learning.concept: The number of currently running concurrent executions can differ from the capacity available for new on-demand invocations.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Aggregate metrics while keeping request IDs searchable
prompt: An application sends processing-time metrics in CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format. The Operations team monitors percentiles by service and environment, and during an incident it looks up requestId in the same logs. New custom metrics are being created for each requestId, increasing operating costs. Which two changes should you make?

choices.text: Limit the dimension set to service and environment to aggregate measurements for the same service and environment.
choices.explanation: The combination of dimensions used to identify a metric should match the granularity you want to monitor.

choices.text: Keep requestId as a dimension and aggregate statistics in a CloudWatch dashboard.
choices.explanation: Aggregating the display in a dashboard does not prevent ingestion from creating individual metrics.

choices.text: Record requestId as the metric value and average it instead of processing time.
choices.explanation: Averages of IDs do not provide processing-time percentiles or help identify a request.

choices.text: Keep requestId as a regular property in the structured log.
choices.explanation: Without requestId as an EMF dimension, it does not create additional time series and can still be searched in the log.

choices.text: Hash requestId as a dimension and use the hash to search the logs.
choices.explanation: Replacing each ID with a one-to-one hash does not materially change the number of metrics for distinct IDs.

source.label: CloudWatch埋め込みメトリクス形式

learning.reason: Use separate keys for aggregation and for investigating an individual request.
learning.concept: A time series is created for each combination of dimension values. Identifiers are better suited to searchable log fields.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Confirming updates immediately with DAX caching
prompt: The product list uses DynamoDB Query through DAX. Immediately after an administrator registers a product, it does not appear in the cached list. Keep the existing cache for public users, but have only the administrator's registration confirmation read the committed update. The confirmation uses Query on the base table, not a GSI. What is the smallest change?

choices.text: Route only the administrator's writes through DAX, and treat the same cached Query result as strongly consistent.
choices.explanation: A write through DAX updates the item cache, but does not invalidate existing query-cache entries.

choices.text: Set ConsistentRead to true on the confirmation Query and leave the normal list's existing settings unchanged.
choices.explanation: DAX forwards a Query that requests strong consistency to DynamoDB and does not cache the result.

choices.text: Shorten the cache lifetime for all queries, including those for public users, so changed values appear soon afterward.
choices.explanation: Shortening the lifetime does not rule out stale results within that lifetime or eventual consistency, and it changes the cache settings for every screen.

choices.text: Send the confirmation Query to a different DAX node without changing its key condition.
choices.explanation: Selecting a different node does not itself request strong consistency.

source.label: DAXとDynamoDBの整合性

learning.reason: Request strong consistency only for the read that must reflect the most recent committed write.
learning.concept: Distinguishing the item cache from the query-result cache helps determine what a write updates.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Set independent concurrency limits for two queues
prompt: One Lambda function processes two standard SQS queues using event source mappings in the default mode. Due to downstream constraints, messages from queue A may use at most 12 concurrent executions, and messages from queue B may use at most 20. Even if both queues are busy, they should be able to use up to 32 executions in total without throttling caused by a configured function-wide limit. There are no other invocations, and the Region has sufficient capacity. Which settings should you choose?

choices.text: Set the function's reserved concurrency to 32 and leave each mapping's concurrency unlimited.
choices.explanation: This limits the function as a whole, but does not prevent either queue alone from exceeding 12 or 20.

choices.text: Set MaximumConcurrency to 12 and 20 on the respective mappings, and set the function's reserved concurrency to 20.
choices.explanation: This satisfies each mapping's limit, but when both process at their maximum, they conflict with the function-wide limit of 20.

choices.text: Set MaximumConcurrency to 12 and 20 on the respective mappings, and set the function's reserved concurrency to 32.
choices.explanation: This configures both the per-queue limits and the function-wide capacity to accommodate the sum of the two limits.

choices.text: Set the batch sizes to 12 and 20, and set the function's reserved concurrency to 32.
choices.explanation: Batch size is the number of messages passed to one invocation; it does not limit the number of function invocations running concurrently.

source.label: LambdaのSQSイベントソース拡張

learning.reason: Align the maximum concurrency for each source with the concurrency available to the function as a whole.
learning.concept: When one function processes multiple sources, estimate the function's capacity by adding the per-source limits.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Isolate the delayed segment from API response times
prompt: For the same REST API stage with caching disabled, one-minute aggregates from a normal period and a delayed period were compared. The request counts and response sizes were similar. CloudWatch Average Latency increased from 120 ms to 420 ms, while IntegrationLatency remained around 95 ms. Which segment should you investigate first based on this observation?

choices.text: Investigate API Gateway processing before and after the integration call, and compare the timing with changes in authorization or request and response processing.
choices.explanation: Latency measures the full time from when API Gateway receives a request until it responds; IntegrationLatency measures the backend integration segment. The increase cannot be explained by integration time.

choices.text: Conclude that the integrated Lambda's processing time increased by 300 ms and raise the function's memory.
choices.explanation: Because the average integration duration did not change, these two metrics do not identify an increase in Lambda processing time.

choices.text: Conclude that the external network between the client and API Gateway added 300 ms.
choices.explanation: Latency measurement begins when API Gateway receives the request. External delay before arrival does not directly appear as this difference.

choices.text: Assume IntegrationLatency always includes cache hits, and use only changes in Count to determine whether integration increased.
choices.explanation: Count is the number of requests; it does not indicate how long the API takes to call the integration and receive its response.

source.label: API Gatewayのメトリクスとディメンション

learning.reason: Compare total time with integration time over the same granularity and period, and start investigating the segment that increased.
learning.concept: Knowing where each measurement starts and ends helps avoid leaping from a single average to a specific cause.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Search many log groups for an exact ID
prompt: In CloudWatch Logs Insights, find log events that exactly match a known requestId across Standard-class log groups used by multiple teams. The logs being analyzed are from after the field index was created; log groups for other purposes that do not have a requestId index may be excluded. Search log groups that share a name prefix, and use a query that restricts reads to groups where the index can be used. Which query should you use?

choices.text: Extract requestId with parse and use a partial-match like condition on requestId.
choices.explanation: A partial match is not a condition for using an index to restrict the search to groups for exact matches.

choices.text: First run stats count() by requestId over all logs, then restrict the output by ID.
choices.explanation: This does not narrow the group or event search before aggregation, and it does not return the original log events as-is.

choices.text: Use the same name as the index and apply filterIndex requestId = target-ID first.
choices.explanation: filterIndex restricts the search to log groups that have an index for the specified field, and can find events with the specified value.

choices.text: Use a regular filter to select rows where requestId equals the target ID.
choices.explanation: An indexed log group can use its index, but groups without the index remain in the scan.

source.label: CloudWatch Logsのフィールド索引

learning.reason: For repeated searches by key, indexing that key can narrow the scan.
learning.concept: filterIndex excludes logs without the relevant field index from the search. The same assumption does not hold if you need to include older data.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Comparing memory settings against a duration limit
prompt: The same Lambda architecture was benchmarked with four configurations. The results were a billed duration of 1,000 ms at 256 MB, 400 ms at 512 MB, 270 ms at 1,024 MB, and 230 ms at 1,536 MB. The comparison is for the same single invocation, and charges other than compute time are the same. Which configuration keeps the billed duration within 500 ms while minimizing GB-seconds, calculated from the allocated memory and billed duration?

choices.text: Use 256 MB.
choices.explanation: This has the smallest memory allocation, but the measured duration of 1,000 ms exceeds the time limit.

choices.text: Use 512 MB.
choices.explanation: 0.5 GB × 0.4 seconds is 0.20 GB-seconds, the lowest value among the configurations within the limit.

choices.text: Use 1,024 MB.
choices.explanation: This is within 500 ms, but 1 GB × 0.27 seconds, or 0.27 GB-seconds, is more than the 512 MB configuration.

choices.text: Use 1,536 MB.
choices.explanation: This has the shortest measured duration, but 1.5 GB × 0.23 seconds is 0.345 GB-seconds.

source.label: Lambdaメモリと性能の設定

learning.reason: For configurations that meet the constraint, compare the product of memory and duration.
learning.concept: CPU allocation increases with memory. When benchmark results are available, do not judge by memory or duration alone.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: ECS tasks are replaced too soon while starting up
prompt: A new version of an ECS service takes about 55 seconds after startup to warm its local cache. By design, it returns 503 to the ALB health check until it is ready, but ECS replaces the new task too soon using the steady-state check settings, so the task does not remain running long enough to become ready. Which setting grants a grace period for replacement only just after startup, without slowing failure detection after the service is steady?

choices.text: Set the ECS service's healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds to a value that covers the usual startup time.
choices.explanation: This gives the scheduler a grace period just after task startup before it uses failed health checks to decide whether to replace the task.

choices.text: Extend the ALB's steady-state health check interval and use the same setting as a startup grace period.
choices.explanation: Extending the health check interval also delays failure detection during steady-state operation.

choices.text: Only extend the container health check's startPeriod and let ALB results trigger replacement immediately.
choices.explanation: A startup grace period for container checks alone does not give ECS a grace period for failures reported by the ALB.

choices.text: Extend the ALB deregistration delay so the new task can wait for its first health check to pass.
choices.explanation: Deregistration delay concerns connection handling when a target is removed. It does not control when startup failures are used to replace a task.

source.label: ECSサービスのヘルスチェック猶予

learning.reason: Grant a grace period only for replacement decisions during startup, while keeping the steady-state health check settings unchanged.
learning.concept: This grace period affects ECS replacement decisions. It does not change the health check results the ALB reports for targets.

sourceLabel: ECS service health check grace period

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Writes to the base table are blocked by a hot GSI key
prompt: Writes to an orders table are receiving ThrottlingException errors. ThrottlingReasons includes IndexWriteKeyRangeThroughputExceeded and the ARN of a GSI that aggregates items by status. The table's overall write volume is about normal, but the status of most new orders is PENDING. Which cause should be investigated first?

choices.text: The base table's partition key is skewed, and the GSI ARN identifies the item that failed.
choices.explanation: The reason begins with Index, and the indicated resource is a GSI. The index should be investigated separately from the table.

choices.text: Writes are concentrated on the GSI's PENDING key, and the index has reached its processing limit for that key range.
choices.explanation: IndexWriteKeyRangeThroughputExceeded indicates excessive writes to a partition within the specified index. Backpressure from the GSI can affect writes to the base table.

choices.text: The account has reached its regional limit on the number of tables, preventing writes to existing GSIs.
choices.explanation: The reason indicates a key-range limit on write processing, not a resource-count quota.

choices.text: The GSI read specified ConsistentRead, throttling the write operations.
choices.explanation: Strong consistency for GSI reads is a separate read configuration issue and does not fit the reported write throttling reason.

source.label: DynamoDBのスロットリング診断

learning.reason: Use the exception type, reason code, and resource ARN together to locate where the constraint is occurring.
learning.concept: Looking only at total base-table usage can miss load concentrated on a small part of a GSI.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Count executions spilling over from provisioned capacity
prompt: Provisioned Concurrency is configured for a Lambda function's prod alias. Latency worsened during a brief load increase, but there were no throttles. Which metric should be used to find the number of invocations that actually ran on standard concurrency after all provisioned capacity was in use?

choices.text: Sum ProvisionedConcurrencyInvocations.
choices.explanation: This counts invocations that used provisioned capacity, not executions that spilled over from it.

choices.text: Use the maximum ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization as the invocation count.
choices.explanation: Utilization shows the proportion of capacity in use; it does not count spillover invocations.

choices.text: Sum Throttles and treat that as the number routed to standard concurrency.
choices.explanation: Invocations that could be handled by standard concurrency were not rejected, so they are not included in Throttles.

choices.text: Sum ProvisionedConcurrencySpilloverInvocations for the prod alias.
choices.explanation: This metric counts invocations actually handled by standard concurrency when all provisioned capacity was in use.

source.label: Lambdaのメトリクス種別

learning.reason: Approaching the limit, handling by overflow capacity, and rejection are separate observations.
learning.concept: When measuring the effect of provisioned environments, monitor invocations that succeeded but ran on standard capacity as well.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Treat periods without errors as healthy
prompt: An application publishes a custom metric to CloudWatch only when a processing error occurs. A separate heartbeat alarm monitors for missing telemetry. When the error alarm must fill in missing data, it should treat evaluation periods with no errors as within the threshold. Which missing-data setting should it use?

choices.text: Specify notBreaching.
choices.explanation: When missing evaluation points are filled in, they can be treated as data within the threshold.

choices.text: Specify ignore.
choices.explanation: When data is insufficient, this keeps the current alarm state. It does not return a previous ALARM state to normal.

choices.text: Specify breaching.
choices.explanation: This treats missing points as breaching the threshold, so even a period with no errors could be considered breaching.

choices.text: Specify missing.
choices.explanation: If there are no points available to evaluate, the alarm enters INSUFFICIENT_DATA. This setting does not fill in missing data as healthy.

source.label: CloudWatchアラームの欠落データ処理

learning.reason: Interpret periods with no reported values based on the conditions under which the metric is published.
learning.concept: Missing data has different meanings for a metric published only when an error occurs and for a heartbeat that checks telemetry-path health.

sourceLabel: CloudWatch alarm handling of missing data

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Cache connections after adding shards
prompt: A cache has been migrated to ElastiCache for Valkey in cluster mode enabled. Existing clients connect only to one node endpoint and treat MOVED responses for some keys as errors. Which configuration lets the client find the write destination without requiring the application to rewrite its node list every time shards are added or removed?

choices.text: Point the existing client to the endpoint of the primary node in another shard.
choices.explanation: Connecting to a different fixed node still does not let the client find the node responsible for every hash slot.

choices.text: Connect a cluster-aware client to the configuration endpoint and have it discover shard and slot information.
choices.explanation: The client can recognize the cluster configuration and send each request to the node responsible for its key.

choices.text: List read-replica endpoints as connection targets and choose among them for writes as well.
choices.explanation: Listing read replicas does not provide a way to select the primary responsible for a key when writing.

choices.text: Shorten only the DNS cache lifetime of the existing client and keep using the same fixed node.
choices.explanation: Refreshing DNS information and discovering which node owns a key's slot are separate operations.

source.label: ElastiCacheのクラスターエンドポイント

learning.reason: Check both the initial connection address and whether the client itself supports cluster discovery.
learning.concept: In cluster mode enabled, key ownership is distributed. A connection configured for a single node cannot track the other destinations.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Tenant-specific SQL prevents connection reuse
prompt: Connections to Aurora MySQL go through RDS Proxy. For each request, the application stores the user's tenant in SET @tenant_id and uses it to filter subsequent SQL statements. DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned is increasing, and connection multiplexing is ineffective. The driver can bind values without creating server-side prepared statements. Which change removes the cause while preserving the filter?

choices.text: Set the tenant ID once in the proxy's common initialization query and use the same value for all connections.
choices.explanation: The tenant ID varies by request, so using the same initial value for every connection would not preserve the filter.

choices.text: Keep reading the session variable and configure the proxy to exclude this SET operation from pinning.
choices.explanation: Statements executed later might run on a connection without the same session variable. Excluding the operation from pinning can break that assumption.

choices.text: Pass the authorized tenant ID as a bind value in each SQL statement and remove the writes to and reads from the session variable.
choices.explanation: Each statement receives its filter value even if it runs on a different connection, so session state does not need to be maintained.

choices.text: Extend the proxy's idle timeout to retain pinned connections for longer.
choices.explanation: A longer timeout does not let other clients reuse a connection while it is pinned.

source.label: RDS Proxyのセッションピン留め

learning.reason: Move the state that prevents connection reuse into the inputs to each SQL statement.
learning.concept: When a request does not depend on state written to a connection by a previous request, the proxy can assign another connection without changing the result.

title: Return multiple cookies with a login response
prompt: An HTTP API invokes Lambda using proxy integration with payload format version 2.0. The API must return two cookies with different paths to an existing client, each in its own Set-Cookie header. How should the response be constructed?

choices.text: Define two Set-Cookie keys in headers.
choices.explanation: headers maps names to values and cannot retain the same key twice.

choices.text: Add each cookie as a separate item in the response's cookies array.
choices.explanation: In format 2.0, each item in cookies becomes a separate Set-Cookie header.

choices.text: Put both values in multiValueHeaders and leave payloadFormatVersion unchanged.
choices.explanation: multiValueHeaders is the representation for format 1.0; format 2.0 uses cookies.

choices.text: Put both values in a cookie field in the response JSON body.
choices.explanation: A cookie in the application body does not become an HTTP Set-Cookie header interpreted by the browser.

source.label: HTTP APIのLambdaプロキシ統合

learning.reason: Where duplicate header names are represented depends on the integration payload format.
learning.concept: In format 2.0, cookies are carried in a dedicated response array.

title: Process a large input list in parallel without passing it to Lambda
prompt: A CSV file in S3 contains hundreds of thousands of records. Each row must be processed independently by an existing workflow. You need to avoid passing the entire CSV to the parent execution, explicitly limit concurrency, and keep a separate history for each child execution. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Convert the CSV into an array with Lambda and pass it to an Inline Map in the parent state machine.
choices.explanation: The parent has input-size and execution-history limits, and this does not separate history for each child execution.

choices.text: Define one branch in a Parallel state for each CSV row.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a way to enumerate a dataset whose row count varies at runtime.

choices.text: Use a Distributed Map in a Standard parent workflow, specify the S3 CSV as the ItemReader input, and set MaxConcurrency.
choices.explanation: The dataset can be read from S3, with a child execution created for each record and concurrency limited.

choices.text: Pass the CSV key to a single Express execution and process all records sequentially with Lambda.
choices.explanation: Processing all records in a single call does not provide child execution histories or a concurrency limit.

source.label: Step Functions Distributed Map

learning.reason: Separate a large dataset and child execution histories from the parent’s input and history.
learning.concept: Define the unit of input processing and the concurrency limit in the workflow.

title: Distinguish unprocessed items from nonexistent items in a batch read
prompt: You pass keys to DynamoDB BatchGetItem in the order they should appear on the screen, but the response items arrive in a different order and some keys remain in UnprocessedKeys. Nonexistent items should be displayed as empty, and items the service has not yet read must be retried before returning results in the original order. Which two steps are required?

choices.text: Retry only UnprocessedKeys, using backoff.
choices.explanation: The unread keys are identified, so there is no need to request keys that have already been processed again.

choices.text: Treat the order of the Responses array as the positions in the input array.
choices.explanation: BatchGetItem does not guarantee that items are returned in the order specified in the request.

choices.text: Treat every key missing from the initial response as nonexistent, whether or not it appears in UnprocessedKeys.
choices.explanation: An unprocessed key may return an item in a subsequent request.

choices.text: Resend all initial keys without a delay until a timeout occurs.
choices.explanation: This rereads keys that were already processed and may worsen throttling.

choices.text: If using a projection, include the primary key and sort the returned items into input order by primary key.
choices.explanation: This identifies which key each returned item belongs to, without relying on response order.

source.label: DynamoDB BatchGetItem

learning.reason: Handle retrying unprocessed keys separately from reconstructing the display order of retrieved items.
learning.concept: For batch read APIs, you may need to identify the processing result for each key.

title: Return the value written by your update
prompt: Multiple workers update the same DynamoDB counter. Immediately after an operation that increments the units succeeds, you want to return the value written by your UpdateItem at the time of that write, even if another worker changes the value afterward, without an additional read. You need only the attributes that changed. How should you configure the operation?

choices.text: Set ReturnValues to ALL_OLD and treat the returned value as the value after the update.
choices.explanation: This returns the item before the update, so it does not show the result of that call.

choices.text: After the update, call GetItem with ConsistentRead and return that value.
choices.explanation: This can include a subsequent update that has already committed by the time of the read, so it may not be the result of your update.

choices.text: Set ReturnValues to UPDATED_NEW on UpdateItem.
choices.explanation: The response includes the changed attributes with their values after this update.

choices.text: Set ReturnValues to UPDATED_OLD and infer the new values merely from the fact that values for the updated attributes were returned.
choices.explanation: This narrows the returned attributes, but they are the values from before the update.

source.label: DynamoDB UpdateItem

learning.reason: Returning values in the same operation avoids a race with a later read.
learning.concept: ReturnValues specifies both which attributes to return and whether their values are from before or after the update.

title: Required attributes are not returned from a secondary index
prompt: An internal application uses Query to search a DynamoDB GSI by status. The GSI uses KEYS_ONLY, and shipmentDate, which the screen must display, is not a key. The existing GSI definition cannot be changed. The application must obtain the latest date for each item found by the search from the base table record and return it to the screen. Which approach works?

choices.text: Specify shipmentDate in a ProjectionExpression for the GSI Query so that it is retrieved from the base table.
choices.explanation: A ProjectionExpression selects attributes that the GSI contains. A GSI does not supplement non-projected attributes from the base table.

choices.text: Set ConsistentRead:true on the GSI Query.
choices.explanation: GSIs do not provide strongly consistent reads, and this does not change the attribute projection configuration.

choices.text: Specify Select:ALL_ATTRIBUTES for the GSI so that base-table attributes are also retrieved, as with an LSI.
choices.explanation: This differs from an LSI, which can read additional non-projected attributes from the base table.

choices.text: Retrieve the base table primary key from the GSI, then perform BatchGetItem against the base table with ConsistentRead enabled using that key.
choices.explanation: A GSI automatically projects the base table primary key. A second read from the base table can retrieve the required attributes.

source.label: DynamoDBグローバルセカンダリインデックス

learning.reason: Separate the condition used to search the GSI from the display attributes retrieved from the base table.
learning.concept: A GSI does not automatically retrieve non-projected attributes from the base table during a query.

title: Read only the end of a large object
prompt: A binary file several GB in size is stored in S3. An inspection Lambda must first read a fixed-length footer at the end of the file and retrieve the body only if corruption is suspected. How can it retrieve the footer without downloading the entire object?

choices.text: Call HeadObject and read the final byte sequence from the response body.
choices.explanation: HeadObject returns metadata and does not return object bytes.

choices.text: Retrieve the object with GetObject, then extract the end locally.
choices.explanation: Even if only the needed portion is selected afterward, the entire object is transferred first.

choices.text: Specify a Range representing the footer length in GetObject.
choices.explanation: S3 can return only the single requested byte range.

choices.text: Pass an offset to ListParts and read the end of the completed file.
choices.explanation: ListParts is for listing parts of an in-progress multipart upload.

source.label: S3 GetObjectのRange指定

learning.reason: Pass the required byte range in the retrieval request.
learning.concept: Selecting a range before transfer and extracting content in the application after transfer have different costs.

title: Processing file events for names containing spaces or plus signs
prompt: A Lambda that receives S3 object creation notifications passes the key in the event directly to GetObject. Retrieval fails only for names containing spaces or plus signs. Which change correctly reads the intended object using the bucket and key in the event?

choices.text: Decode s3.object.key exactly once using form URL encoding rules before passing it to GetObject.
choices.explanation: In an event key, spaces become +, while a literal + is encoded separately. One appropriate decode preserves the original key.

choices.text: Only replace every + in s3.object.key with a space.
choices.explanation: Characters encoded with % are not decoded, so the original key cannot be fully restored.

choices.text: Decode the key using a percent-encoding-only decoder and leave + unchanged.
choices.explanation: This can restore URL percent notation but leaves +, which represents a space in form encoding.

choices.text: If s3.object.key is not found, repeat decoding until it produces no further changes.
choices.explanation: If the original key contains %, repeated decoding changes the name.

source.label: S3通知イベントの構造

learning.reason: Distinguish the event representation from the object key passed to the SDK.
learning.concept: Normalize the key representation exactly once so that the original name is not changed accidentally.

title: Fix a target input format without changing the event source
prompt: An EventBridge order event contains multiple fields. An existing receiving Lambda needs only a top-level orderId and a fixed processing type. Other targets must receive the original event. Without modifying the sender or Lambda code, pass a new input only to this target. What should be changed?

choices.text: Make the event pattern a structure containing only orderId and the processing type.
choices.explanation: An event pattern filters events. It does not reshape the received event.

choices.text: Pass a constant input containing the same JSON to the target every time.
choices.explanation: This can pass a fixed type, but cannot incorporate the order ID that varies for each source event.

choices.text: Use InputPath to pass only detail.orderId to the target.
choices.explanation: This can select the order ID, but cannot combine it with a fixed value or generate JSON with named fields.

choices.text: Use an Input Transformer only for the target, extract the order ID with a JSON path, and place it with a fixed value in the same template.
choices.explanation: It can extract part of the original event and shape it into the required format for each target.

source.label: EventBridge入力変換

learning.reason: Use event filtering, partial extraction, and transformation for their respective purposes.
learning.concept: Configuring input transformation per target avoids affecting other consumers of the same event.

title: Extend visibility only for a message being processed
prompt: A custom worker reads an SQS standard queue. Processing usually takes a few seconds, but an external operation can sometimes take longer than the visibility timeout set when a message is received. You want to keep the default duration short for all messages while continuing to hide only the message being processed from other workers. What should you do?

choices.text: Call DeleteMessage as soon as processing starts, and send a new message if processing fails.
choices.explanation: If the worker stops partway through, the message cannot be redelivered, making recovery difficult.

choices.text: Before the timeout expires, call ChangeMessageVisibility with the current ReceiptHandle, then delete the message after processing succeeds.
choices.explanation: This extends the invisibility period for an individual message being processed. You still need to account separately for duplicate delivery in a standard queue.

choices.text: Increase WaitTimeSeconds in ReceiveMessage so other workers wait until processing is complete.
choices.explanation: This setting controls how long to wait to receive a message; it does not change the invisibility period after receipt.

choices.text: Set the timeout to 0 with ChangeMessageVisibility and let the same worker continue processing.
choices.explanation: Setting it to 0 makes the message available to other workers again, so they may process it concurrently.

source.label: SQS可視性タイムアウト

learning.reason: Maintain the lease on the individual message while processing, then delete it after completion.
learning.concept: Extending the invisibility period reduces duplicate processing but does not change the delivery model of a standard queue.

title: A setting for frequent empty responses during short polling
prompt: Several workers read an SQS standard queue. With the default short polling, they can continue to receive empty responses even when messages are visible. You want to reduce receive requests and avoid waiting until the wait period expires when data arrives. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Set the visibility timeout to 20 seconds so receive requests do not return early.
choices.explanation: Visibility controls how long a received message stays hidden; it does not control how long to wait for a message.

choices.text: Set a positive WaitTimeSeconds value in ReceiveMessage, and make the HTTP response timeout longer than that value.
choices.explanation: Long polling returns early when messages are available. It can reduce empty responses, including those caused by sampling only some servers.

choices.text: Only increase the client's HTTP timeout.
choices.explanation: This does not change how SQS receives messages; a short-polling response is still returned as is.

choices.text: Set MaxNumberOfMessages to 10 so the receive request remains open until it collects 10 messages.
choices.explanation: This sets the maximum number of messages; it does not make the request wait until that number is available.

source.label: SQSの短いポーリングと長いポーリング

learning.reason: Let the service handle the receive wait, and ensure the client's timeout does not expire first.
learning.concept: Long polling sets how long the request can wait; it does not hold an available message until the wait period expires.

title: Keep existing read capacity as subscribers are added
prompt: The same Kinesis Data Streams data is sent to real-time analytics and auditing. After auditing was added, the consumers began competing for the shards' shared read capacity, delaying analytics. How can you isolate read capacity for auditing without changing the writer or the number of shards?

choices.text: Increase the maximum number of records retrieved by GetRecords in the auditing process, and call it more frequently.
choices.explanation: As a standard consumer, the auditing process still shares the read capacity.

choices.text: Change only the auditing process's initial shard iterator to LATEST.
choices.explanation: This changes where reading starts, but contention for shared read bandwidth remains.

choices.text: Register a consumer for auditing and read with SubscribeToShard using enhanced fan-out.
choices.explanation: Enhanced fan-out consumers use dedicated read throughput for each shard.

choices.text: Specify a different partition key for auditing and read the same stream with GetRecords.
choices.explanation: A partition key can affect how records are distributed, but it cannot move existing data into a separate dedicated read capacity.

source.label: Kinesisの拡張ファンアウト

learning.reason: When all subscribers need to read the same records, treat write distribution and subscriber read capacity as separate concerns.
learning.concept: Enhanced fan-out provides dedicated read capacity for each subscriber.

title: Fix insufficient scratch space during extraction
prompt: A Lambda function downloads a compressed file from S3, extracts it, and processes it with a library that requires a local file it can seek through. Memory and execution time are sufficient, but the function lacks the 8 GB of scratch space needed only during extraction. The file does not need to be shared across execution environments or invocations. What is the smallest change?

choices.text: Increase only the Lambda memory setting to 10 GB so that /tmp has that capacity.
choices.explanation: Memory and /tmp capacity are configured separately.

choices.text: Add an 8 GB writable directory to the container image and extract the file under the function's root directory.
choices.explanation: The container's root file system is read-only in the Lambda execution environment.

choices.text: Increase the Lambda timeout and wait for the /tmp write limit to be lifted.
choices.explanation: Execution time does not change the write capacity.

choices.text: Set Lambda ephemeral storage to a value that provides 8 GB plus working headroom, and continue extracting to /tmp.
choices.explanation: /tmp can be increased by configuration from 512 MB to 10,240 MB and can be used for temporary files in each execution environment.

source.label: Lambda一時ストレージ

learning.reason: Identify whether the constrained resource is CPU, memory, or disk before changing a setting.
learning.concept: The storage needed for scratch files in one execution environment differs from storage needed to share files across environments.

title: Return product search tool results to the model
prompt: In a guidance app using Bedrock Converse, the model selected a product inventory tool. The response contains a toolUse block and a toolUseId, and only the app can retrieve inventory data. What should the app do to include actual inventory in the final answer?

choices.text: Run the inventory tool authorized by the app, add a toolResult with the same toolUseId to the conversation, and call Converse again.
choices.explanation: With client-side tools, the app performs the operation. The identifier pairs the request with its result when returning it to the model.

choices.text: After the model responds, wait for Bedrock to find an app function with the same name and append its result automatically.
choices.explanation: A client-side tool is not executed just because the model selected it.

choices.text: Send the actual inventory as a new system instruction and remove the original toolUse block from the conversation.
choices.explanation: The request and its corresponding result would no longer be represented together in the conversation.

choices.text: Create a new toolUseId and send an empty toolResult, then retrieve the inventory after the next response.
choices.explanation: An ID that does not match the request cannot associate the result with the call, and no actual inventory is provided.

source.label: Bedrockのクライアント側ツール使用

learning.reason: Receive the model's tool request, run it in the app, and return the result with the same identifier.
learning.concept: Clearly distinguish an operation selected by the model from one the app authorizes and executes.

title: Replay archived events only to the failed destination
prompt: An EventBridge event bus has rules for billing and analytics, and only analytics was down. Replay events from the outage period in the archive to the same bus. Which configuration keeps existing live events flowing to both rules while preventing the replayed historical events from restarting billing?

choices.text: Replay to all rules and exclude live events from the billing rule's event pattern.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to keep processing live events.

choices.text: Specify the replay time range and select only the analytics rule on the same event bus as the replay destination.
choices.explanation: The replay can be limited to the selected rule without changing the rules that receive normal event delivery.

choices.text: Delete the analytics rule, replay to all rules, and restore the analytics rule after the replay finishes.
choices.explanation: The events would not be replayed to analytics, and the billing rule could receive historical events.

choices.text: Change the archive retention period to match the outage duration so the analytics target catches up automatically.
choices.explanation: Changing the retention period does not start a replay.

source.label: EventBridgeアーカイブのリプレイ

learning.reason: Limit historical event delivery by both time range and rule.
learning.concept: An archive determines which events are retained; a replay determines where retained events are sent.

title: Compare before-and-after values using only the event
prompt: Start downstream processing only when a member's plan changes in DynamoDB. By the time a Stream record is processed, the item might have been updated again. You need to compare the old and new plans for that specific change using only the change event. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Set KEYS_ONLY and call GetItem during processing to infer the previous value as well.
choices.explanation: The current item alone cannot establish the old value for that specific change.

choices.text: Set NEW_IMAGE and treat the last value read as the current value before the change.
choices.explanation: The Stream event does not include the before image, so the correct pair may not be available when processing is delayed.

choices.text: Set StreamViewType to NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES and compare OldImage with NewImage in the record.
choices.explanation: Each event contains the item images before and after its change, so the change can be inspected even if the item is read after a subsequent update.

choices.text: Use OLD_IMAGE and calculate the value immediately after the change from the Stream sequence number.
choices.explanation: A sequence number identifies a position in the stream; it does not represent the value after the change.

source.label: DynamoDB StreamSpecification

learning.reason: Use the before-and-after state from when the event occurred instead of substituting the current state read later.
learning.concept: StreamViewType lets you choose the item images needed by downstream processing.

title: Store large reports and a searchable index
prompt: Search is needed only for a report's status and generation time, but each report's JSON body is around 600 KB and its compression ratio varies. Which design supports retrieving the entire report when needed and avoids exceeding DynamoDB's item size limit?

choices.text: Store the body in S3 and the searchable attributes and S3 object identifier in DynamoDB. Also provide a consistency process for cases where only one of the two writes succeeds.
choices.explanation: The searchable item can stay within DynamoDB's 400 KB limit. Writes spanning S3 and DynamoDB do not automatically form a single transaction.

choices.text: Base64-encode the body and store it in the same item as the searchable attributes.
choices.explanation: A reversible encoding does not bypass DynamoDB's item size limit, and Base64 increases the size.

choices.text: Create a GSI for search to raise DynamoDB's item size limit, including the body.
choices.explanation: Creating an index does not change the item size limit of the base table.

choices.text: Always compress each report into a single item and increase write capacity to allow items larger than 600 KB.
choices.explanation: Throughput capacity does not change the item size limit. Compression is not guaranteed to reduce the item below that limit.

source.label: DynamoDBで大きな項目を扱う方法

learning.reason: Choose storage locations for the searchable attributes and large body based on the access pattern.
learning.concept: When writing to separate services, account for cases where writes to one or both services fail.

title: Wait for the reviewer to finish
prompt: In a Standard workflow review step, you send a request to SQS and want the workflow to resume with the saved result after a review service in the same AWS account finishes. You want to avoid repeatedly polling the status and specify a timeout. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Send the message with a regular SQS SendMessage call and treat a successful send response as the review result.
choices.explanation: A successful send does not mean the review service has processed the request.

choices.text: Set the SQS visibility timeout to the same value as the workflow timeout and advance to the next state when the message is consumed.
choices.explanation: The queue's visibility setting does not provide a way to return a business result to Step Functions.

choices.text: Switch to an Express workflow and wait indefinitely on the same SQS task.
choices.explanation: The callback task-token pattern is not available in Express workflows, and it does not wait indefinitely.

choices.text: Use the SQS waitForTaskToken integration to include a token in the message, then have the review service call SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure when it finishes.
choices.explanation: The task waits for a result associated with the token or for the configured timeout.

source.label: Step Functionsのサービス統合パターン

learning.reason: Request acceptance and business completion happen at different times.
learning.concept: A callback token associates a later result with the execution that is waiting for it.

title: SNS delivery format changes the attribute limit
prompt: You deliver messages from SNS to SQS. After enabling Raw Message Delivery for the subscription, only messages with 11 attributes stopped arriving. You must preserve all attributes and cannot change the publisher or the number of attributes. You can add envelope parsing to the receiving application. Which change should you choose?

choices.text: Keep raw delivery and move the eleventh attribute to a different MessageAttribute in the same subscription.
choices.explanation: Renaming an attribute does not increase the number of attributes SNS can deliver to a raw SQS subscription.

choices.text: Request all attributes when receiving from SQS to retrieve messages that were lost with raw delivery.
choices.explanation: The receiver's attribute selection cannot recover messages that were not delivered because of the attribute limit.

choices.text: Disable raw delivery for the subscription and have the receiver read the original message and attributes from the SNS notification JSON.
choices.explanation: This avoids the 10-attribute limit for raw SQS delivery and allows the receiver to process the SNS envelope.

choices.text: Only increase the SQS queue's maximum message size and keep raw delivery enabled.
choices.explanation: Changing the maximum SQS message body size does not change the attribute limit for raw delivery.

source.label: SNS Raw Message Delivery

learning.reason: A delivery option can affect more than whether a wrapper is present, so check the attribute limits at the destination as well.
learning.concept: When the publisher's representation must remain unchanged, the receiver can be made capable of parsing the service's message format.

title: Have S3 verify a hash before upload
prompt: Before transfer, the application receives the expected SHA-256 value for the data through a separate channel. You want to upload the data with a single PutObject call and prevent the write from succeeding if the content S3 receives differs from that value. Which method should you choose?

choices.text: Store the expected value in custom metadata and have S3 compare it with the body.
choices.explanation: User metadata is stored, but it does not instruct S3 to verify the content's integrity.

choices.text: Pass the expected value to PutObject as a Base64-encoded ChecksumSHA256.
choices.explanation: S3 calculates a checksum for the received data and rejects the write if it does not match the supplied value.

choices.text: After a successful upload, always treat the ETag as the SHA-256 of the original data.
choices.explanation: An ETag does not mean SHA-256. Comparing it after success also does not reject the data when it is received.

choices.text: Call HeadObject after saving the object and assume the hash matches if ContentLength equals the expected length.
choices.explanation: The content can differ even when the length is the same.

source.label: S3アップロード時のデータ整合性

learning.reason: Distinguish between recording a hash and having the service verify a checksum when it receives the data.
learning.concept: Passing the expected digest to the upload API lets the destination determine whether the content is intact.

title: Update agreed conditions before implementation
prompt: A development team is implementing a billing feature with Kiro's requirements-first Spec. After generating the design and work items, the team changes how billing across business days is handled. They want the updated agreement to inform future regeneration and reviews and to prevent conflicts between the current design and implementation items. What should they update first?

choices.text: Add the updated condition to the owner's chat and regenerate the implementation using the existing Spec.
choices.explanation: The shared specification would still contain the old requirement even if a separate conversation includes the updated condition.

choices.text: Only clear the completed marks in the previous tasks.md and redo the implementation using the old requirement.
choices.explanation: Resetting the work status does not make the requirement change explicit.

choices.text: Record the updated acceptance criteria in the Spec's requirements.md, then update and review the design and implementation tasks against those criteria.
choices.explanation: Putting the changed expected behavior at the source of the specification keeps the subsequent design and work items aligned.

choices.text: Only change the internal interfaces in the design and keep the previous acceptance criteria for reference.
choices.explanation: The criteria for what the implementation and tests must satisfy would remain outdated.

source.label: KiroのSpec機能

learning.reason: Reflect a user-facing change in the acceptance criteria, not only in implementation notes.
learning.concept: When requirements, design, and work items correspond, generated code can be checked against the intended behavior.

title: Allowing a function to be invoked by one S3 bucket only
prompt: Invoke a Lambda function from S3 creation notifications. Allow only the specified bucket name, and do not allow invocations from another account if that name is reused there in the future. The execution role used by the application to read S3 is configured separately. Which permission should you add?

choices.text: Add s3:GetObject to the Lambda execution role so the bucket can invoke the function.
choices.explanation: This grants the running function permission to read from S3; it is separate from permission for S3 to invoke the function.

choices.text: In the function's resource-based policy, allow the S3 service to call InvokeFunction and specify SourceArn and SourceAccount.
choices.explanation: This restricts access to both the original bucket name and its owning account. The S3 bucket ARN itself does not contain an account ID.

choices.text: In the function's resource-based policy, allow the S3 service and use only the bucket name in SourceArn as a condition.
choices.explanation: This restricts the bucket name but not the owner of a bucket created with the same name after the original bucket is deleted.

choices.text: Add the Lambda execution role to the bucket policy to restrict the account allowed to invoke the function.
choices.explanation: Object permissions on the bucket cannot control whether the function resource accepts InvokeFunction.

source.label: Lambdaを呼ぶAWSサービスへの許可

learning.reason: Permissions for invoking the function are configured in the function's policy.
learning.concept: Restricting both the bucket name and the account prevents the permission from extending to a reused name.

sourceLabel: Permissions for AWS services that invoke Lambda

title: A signed-in mobile app accesses S3 directly
prompt: A mobile app signs in users with a Cognito user pool and can obtain an ID token. Only after sign-in, it must access S3 directly with the AWS SDK without embedding long-term keys in the app. Do not add API Gateway or a server that issues presigned URLs for this operation. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Use the user pool as an identity provider for a Cognito identity pool, then obtain temporary AWS credentials through an IAM role for authenticated users.
choices.explanation: The user-pool token can be used for authentication, and the identity pool can provide short-lived credentials for AWS services.

choices.text: Set the user-pool ID token in the AWS SDK's secret access key field.
choices.explanation: An ID token is not a component of an AWS access key.

choices.text: Use the user-pool app client secret to sign S3 API calls.
choices.explanation: A Cognito client secret cannot replace credentials from an IAM role.

choices.text: Distribute the access key of a shared IAM user to every user in the app's user pool.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to use temporary credentials and shares a key among users.

source.label: Amazon Cognito IDプール

learning.reason: Distinguish the token used to sign in to the app from the credentials obtained before signing AWS API requests.
learning.concept: An appropriate IAM role can grant signed-in users permission to perform AWS operations.

title: API signing fails after switching to temporary credentials
prompt: A custom HTTP client calls an API Gateway API that uses IAM authentication. Signing worked with a test long-term key. After replacing only the access key ID and secret with those returned by AssumeRole, authentication fails with the same permissions on the temporary role. Without adding an SDK, what is needed to sign with temporary credentials?

choices.text: Put the role ARN in the Authorization header as a Bearer token.
choices.explanation: An ARN is not a credential and does not provide the signature required by IAM authentication.

choices.text: Add the AssumeRole ExternalId to the API authentication header.
choices.explanation: ExternalId is part of the request context for assuming a role, not the session token for subsequent AWS API requests.

choices.text: Also use the session token returned by AssumeRole and include X-Amz-Security-Token in the request as required by the signing rules for the target service.
choices.explanation: Temporary credentials consist of an access key ID, a secret access key, and a session token.

choices.text: Combine only the temporary role's access key ID with a signature made using the existing long-term key.
choices.explanation: Mixing components from different credential sets cannot be validated as a temporary session.

source.label: AWS APIリクエストの署名

learning.reason: Use the complete set of temporary credentials returned by AssumeRole.
learning.concept: A temporary credential's session token does not replace the access-key signature.

title: Decrypting just one encrypted configuration value
prompt: A Lambda function reads one SecureString from Parameter Store. The parameter is encrypted with an application-specific customer managed KMS key. The function does not need to read any other values under the path and must obtain the plaintext value. Which two permissions or settings are required?

choices.text: Allow ssm:GetParameter on the target parameter ARN and call the operation with WithDecryption enabled.
choices.explanation: This permits reading the required parameter and specifies that it should be returned decrypted.

choices.text: Allow only ssm:DescribeParameters and obtain the plaintext from the parameter description.
choices.explanation: An operation that lists or describes parameters does not retrieve their values.

choices.text: Configure the key and IAM permissions so the Lambda execution role can use kms:Decrypt with the target KMS key.
choices.explanation: Decrypt permission on the key is needed to decrypt a value encrypted with a customer managed key.

choices.text: Allow ssm:GetParametersByPath on all parameters and select the correct value inside Lambda.
choices.explanation: Only one parameter is needed, so permission to read other values is unnecessary.

choices.text: Grant only kms:GenerateDataKey on the target key.
choices.explanation: This does not replace permission to decrypt an existing value.

source.label: Parameter Store SecureStringのKMS暗号化

learning.reason: Scope the permission to read the value and the permission to decrypt it to the required resource.
learning.concept: WithDecryption requests decryption; it does not grant permission to use the KMS key.

sourceLabel: KMS encryption for Parameter Store SecureString

title: Read an existing secret from another account
prompt: A Lambda execution role in a consumer team reads an API key directly from AWS Secrets Manager in a shared services account, using its own credentials. The secret is not copied, and no role in the shared account is assumed. Which two configurations are required?

choices.text: Keep the shared account's AWS managed key, aws/secretsmanager, and change only the secret's resource policy in the shared account.
choices.explanation: An AWS managed key cannot be used for direct cross-account reads.

choices.text: Allow GetSecretValue for the secret in both its resource policy and the consumer role's IAM policy.
choices.explanation: Cross-account access requires permission from the shared account and authorization for the principal in the consumer account.

choices.text: Rely on the consumer role's Secrets Manager permissions; no resource policy is needed in the shared account.
choices.explanation: This does not provide the shared account's permission for access to its existing secret from another account.

choices.text: Encrypt the secret with a customer managed key in the shared account, and allow the consumer role to perform the required Decrypt operation in both the key policy and the consumer IAM policy.
choices.explanation: Retrieving an encrypted value across accounts requires permission to decrypt with the key, in addition to permission to read the secret.

choices.text: Grant kms:Decrypt to the consumer role and require no permission to read the secret from Secrets Manager.
choices.explanation: Permission to use the KMS key does not replace the policies that authorize retrieval of the secret.

source.label: Secrets Managerのクロスアカウントアクセス

learning.reason: Access is evaluated both for the service that stores the secret and for the key that encrypts it.
learning.concept: For direct cross-account use of a resource, authorization must be granted on both the caller's side and the resource owner's side.

title: When an established SQL connection lasts longer than 15 minutes
prompt: An application uses IAM database authentication to connect to RDS for PostgreSQL. A batch job runs SQL for about 40 minutes after establishing a connection. When should the connection pool obtain a token to account for the token's expiration?

choices.text: Disconnect every established connection every 15 minutes and resubmit any SQL in progress.
choices.explanation: Token expiration does not invalidate an existing database session. The work does not need to be interrupted.

choices.text: Use a valid token when establishing each new physical database connection, and do not disconnect an authenticated connection solely because the token expires.
choices.explanation: The token is validated during connection authentication; it is not used to maintain an established session.

choices.text: After the first connection succeeds, reuse its token for other connections even after it expires.
choices.explanation: An expired token cannot be used to authenticate a new connection.

choices.text: Pass a separate token as a parameter for every SQL query on an existing connection.
choices.explanation: The IAM token is used to authenticate the database connection. It does not need to be included in each SQL query's parameters.

source.label: RDS IAMデータベース認証

learning.reason: The lifetime of a credential and the lifetime of an already established connection are separate.
learning.concept: A connection pool needs valid credentials when it creates a physical connection.

title: Permissions for a deployer to pass an execution role
prompt: A deployment IAM role can create Lambda functions, but attaching a specified execution role to a function fails. The execution role is in the same account and trusts the Lambda service. The deployer does not need to assume that role and should not be able to pass arbitrary roles. What should be added?

choices.text: Add the deployment role to the execution role's trust policy and allow sts:AssumeRole.
choices.explanation: This would let the deployer use the execution role in its own session; it does not authorize passing the role to a service.

choices.text: Add iam:PassRole to the Lambda function's execution role.
choices.explanation: The deployment role is performing this operation. Changing the function's execution role does not solve the problem.

choices.text: Grant the deployment role iam:PassRole only for the specified execution role ARN, and restrict it to Lambda with iam:PassedToService.
choices.explanation: This limits the operation to associating the specified role with the specified AWS service.

choices.text: Grant the deployment role only iam:GetRole.
choices.explanation: Permission to read role details does not authorize passing the role to a service.

source.label: IAM PassRoleの制御

learning.reason: Assuming a role and assigning a role to an AWS service are different operations.
learning.concept: Give the deployment principal permission only for the required role and the service receiving it.

title: Removing an ACL from uploads to another account's bucket
prompt: A shared S3 bucket has Object Ownership set to Bucket owner enforced, and its policy allows uploads from another account. An existing SDK sends public-read ACLs with PutObject, which results in AccessControlListNotSupported. Which change preserves object ownership and public access restrictions?

choices.text: Remove the ACL from the upload request and rely on the existing IAM and bucket policies for authorization.
choices.explanation: With Bucket owner enforced, ACLs are disabled and writes without an ACL are accepted. The bucket owner owns the objects.

choices.text: Change public-read to a private ACL and continue sending the ACL header.
choices.explanation: A private ACL is still an ACL and is not a generally accepted ACL under this setting.

choices.text: Add PutObjectAcl to the application role to enable individual ACLs that are disabled.
choices.explanation: Adding a policy permission does not undo the bucket's ACL-disabled setting.

choices.text: Change Object Ownership back to Object writer and rely on Block Public Access alone to preserve the current ownership requirement.
choices.explanation: Block Public Access does not make the bucket owner the owner of uploaded objects.

source.label: S3 Object OwnershipとACL無効化

learning.reason: Remove the client-side ACL so the upload matches a bucket that uses policies for access control.
learning.concept: Bucket ownership and permission to read an object are separate concepts.

sourceLabel: S3 Object Ownership and ACL disabling

title: Encrypting large data for later decryption
prompt: An application must encrypt a large confidential artifact before storing it. The KMS key must never leave KMS, each file must use a different symmetric data key, and an authorized process must be able to decrypt the file later. Which two steps should be combined?

choices.text: Pass the entire file to a single KMS Encrypt call and do not generate a data key.
choices.explanation: Symmetric KMS Encrypt has a plaintext size limit, so it is not intended for passing an entire large file directly.

choices.text: Use KMS GenerateDataKey and encrypt the file in the application with the returned plaintext data key.
choices.explanation: Large data can be encrypted locally, and the plaintext key can be held only as long as needed for encryption.

choices.text: Use the byte string of the encrypted data key returned by GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext directly as the key for local encryption.
choices.explanation: Using an encrypted key for encryption would not meet the requirement to control decryption of the stored key through KMS permissions.

choices.text: Store the plaintext data key in a separate private file for a long time.
choices.explanation: Even if the encrypted data is protected, storing its key in plaintext leaves it unprotected if the key is exposed.

choices.text: Store the encrypted data key with the ciphertext, then decrypt the data key with KMS later. Discard the plaintext key after the cryptographic operation.
choices.explanation: This lets KMS permissions control decryption of the key while allowing the data key needed to decrypt the file to be recovered.

source.label: KMSデータキー

learning.reason: Separate the temporary key used to encrypt the data from the KMS key that protects that temporary key.
learning.concept: An encrypted data key can be stored with the data. Handle the plaintext key only for as long as the cryptographic operation requires.

title: Expose an API with certificate required at a single entry point
prompt: An HTTP API is being exposed to devices. A custom domain that validates client certificates and an S3 trust store are already configured. Calls must use this domain, and the default endpoint automatically attached to the API must not accept requests. Which additional setting is required?

choices.text: Also set the trust store URL as a stage variable.
choices.explanation: The trust store is used in the custom domain's mTLS configuration. Adding a stage variable does not disable the default endpoint.

choices.text: Set the API mapping key to empty and publish the stage at the custom domain root.
choices.explanation: This changes the path on the custom domain, but the default API endpoint remains available.

choices.text: Enable CloudWatch access logs for the default endpoint.
choices.explanation: Recording usage does not reject requests to the default route.

choices.text: Disable the HTTP API's default execute-api endpoint.
choices.explanation: This restricts access to the intended custom-domain path and makes the automatically provisioned API entry point unavailable.

source.label: API Gateway HTTP APIの相互TLS

learning.reason: Make only the entry point with the required authentication method available.
learning.concept: Custom-domain configuration and the setting that enables a service's default endpoint are independent.

sourceLabel: API Gateway HTTP API mutual TLS

title: Authorize the same user separately for each route
prompt: An HTTP API uses the same Lambda authorizer across multiple routes and caches simple responses in format 2.0. The current identity source is only Authorization, but authorization decisions differ by route. Which setting prevents a decision from being shared across routes while preserving caching within the same route?

choices.text: Add $context.routeKey to the identity sources and use the token-route pair as the cache key.
choices.explanation: The authorizer cache uses identity-source values, which lets it distinguish different routes.

choices.text: Keep only Authorization as the identity source and shorten the cache duration for the same token.
choices.explanation: Even with a shorter expiration, the same cache entry is used across routes during that interval.

choices.text: Add a route identifier to the business request body passed to Lambda, and leave the authorizer identity source unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the body passed to the integration does not change the authorization cache key.

choices.text: Include the current time in the response alongside true or false to divide the authorization cache by time.
