choices.explanation: Contextual information in the response does not change how API Gateway constructs the cache key.

source.label: HTTP APIのLambdaオーソライザー

learning.reason: Include inputs that can change an authorization decision among the cache identity sources.
learning.concept: If access can differ by route for the same token, reuse the result at the route level.

title: Align the expiration of build package tokens
prompt: A CI job assumes a short-lived IAM role to retrieve CodeArtifact packages. The role session time remaining when the build starts varies from run to run. What should be specified when issuing the CodeArtifact authentication token to prevent it from remaining valid after the role session ends?

choices.text: Shorten the role's MaxSessionDuration and leave the CodeArtifact token setting at its default.
choices.explanation: By default, the CodeArtifact token lifetime is not tied to the remaining time in the role session.

choices.text: Retrieve the CodeArtifact token using the assumed role and set duration-seconds to 0.
choices.explanation: Zero does not mean immediate expiration; it makes the token lifetime equal to the remaining time in the assumed role's current session.

choices.text: Specify the same fixed duration-seconds value each time as at the start of the session.
choices.explanation: If issuance is delayed, the token could remain valid beyond the original session's expiration.

choices.text: Set the session name to the current time and omit the token lifetime when issuing it.
choices.explanation: The session name does not control the lifetime of a CodeArtifact token.

source.label: CodeArtifactの認証トークン

learning.reason: Explicitly tie the expiration of a secondary token to the role when issuing it.
learning.concept: When temporary credentials expire, a separate service token issued from them does not necessarily expire automatically.

title: Keep operational metrics without storing future request and response content
prompt: Model invocation logging is enabled for Bedrock inference, collecting the contents of requests and responses. The requirements have changed: going forward, the content must not be sent to the log destination, and the application should record only the number of items processed, latency, and whether each operation succeeded. Past logs are covered by a separate retention procedure. What should you do?

choices.text: Set the CloudWatch Logs retention period to one day and leave content logging enabled.
choices.explanation: Shortening the retention period does not stop new content from being sent to the logs.

choices.text: Encrypt the current log destination and use IAM to prevent access to the content.
choices.explanation: Restricting decryption access does not stop the content from being sent and stored.

choices.text: Disable model invocation logging that collects content, and have the application record operational metrics that exclude content.
choices.explanation: This stops future content from being transferred and records only the required numbers through a separate path.

choices.text: Reduce the token limit for model output and keep the current logging configuration.
choices.explanation: Even shorter output would still be included in the logs. This would not affect storage of the input.

source.label: Bedrockのモデル呼び出しログ

learning.reason: Distinguish protecting access to the log destination from choosing not to collect the content in the first place.
learning.concept: When inference content is not needed for monitoring, record only the required outcomes and latency.

title: Match permitted Regions to a geographic inference profile
prompt: An application uses a Bedrock geographic cross-Region inference profile. The profile has multiple destination Regions within its geography, and an organization SCP explicitly denies model invocation in one of them. The invocation role has the required IAM Allow. Region controls must remain in place. What is the appropriate response?

choices.text: Keep using the same profile and add the denied Region to the invocation role's IAM Allow.
choices.explanation: An IAM Allow cannot override an SCP deny.

choices.text: Use any profile in that geography and assume Bedrock will always automatically skip the denied Region.
choices.explanation: You must verify that every destination of a geographic profile is permitted by the SCP.

choices.text: Switch to a global cross-Region profile and treat it as limited to the current geography.
choices.explanation: A global profile is not a way to limit processing to the original geography.

choices.text: Switch to a supported profile whose destinations are all within the organization's permitted scope. If none is available, choose a supported inference method within permitted Regions.
choices.explanation: Choosing an invocation method that matches the available permitted routes preserves the Region controls.

source.label: Bedrockのクロスリージョン推論

learning.reason: Compare the invocation's permitted Regions with the Regions to which the profile can actually route requests.
learning.concept: Geographic and global profiles handle Region restrictions differently, so confirm which type of profile is in use.

title: Require the classification tag at write time
prompt: Objects uploaded to an S3 ingestion prefix must be tagged Classification=Internal at the same time they are created. A specific upload role is allowed to write to the prefix, and no other path grants that permission. Which condition should you configure?

choices.text: Check the bucket's Classification resource tag, without evaluating the tag on the object being written.
choices.explanation: The bucket tag alone does not reveal the value of the tag requested when the object is created.

choices.text: Allow a new PutObject when s3:ExistingObjectTag/Classification is Internal.
choices.explanation: A tag on a new write is not an existing-object tag. Use a request tag to control tags supplied with PutObject.

choices.text: Add a condition requiring s3:RequestObjectTag/Classification to equal Internal to the permissions required to upload the object.
choices.explanation: This limits writes to requests that include the tag with the required value.

choices.text: Use s3:RequestObjectTagKeys to check only whether the key Classification is present.
choices.explanation: Checking the allowed key name does not restrict the value to Internal.

source.label: S3のタグとアクセスポリシー

learning.reason: Check the classification information on the new request when the resource is created.
learning.concept: Use different conditions to check which tag keys are allowed and whether a required tag has the required value.

title: Set an upper bound on permissions for created roles
prompt: Developers can attach policies to application roles in their assigned environments. The management team wants to ensure that future AttachRolePolicy calls cannot give application roles permissions beyond the scope delegated to developers. Each role receiving permissions will also have separate permissions that grant actual access, and no external resource policy grants access directly. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Require a permissions boundary defined by the management team on every new role, and prevent developers from removing the boundary.
choices.explanation: The boundary limits the actions allowed by the role's identity policies to those included in the boundary. The boundary alone does not grant access.

choices.text: Add the assigned team to the role's trust policy and treat it as an upper bound on permissions.
choices.explanation: A trust policy specifies who can assume the role. It does not cap the permissions available after the role is assumed.

choices.text: Treat permissions as bounded whenever an attached IAM policy has an approved prefix in its name, regardless of its contents.
choices.explanation: A name alone does not set an upper bound on the actions and resources actually allowed.

choices.text: Use a restrictive session policy for only some sessions and leave the remaining sessions without a specific upper bound.
choices.explanation: This does not consistently impose an upper bound on all roles in scope.

source.label: IAMアクセス許可の境界

learning.reason: Manage the maximum permissions separately from the access actually granted to the application.
learning.concept: Operational controls must also ensure that delegated administrators cannot remove the boundary.

title: OAuth authorization for a client that cannot keep a secret
prompt: A native app distributed to users signs in with Cognito. You must not embed a shared client secret in the installation, and only the requester that received an authorization code should be able to exchange that code for tokens. Which method should you choose?

choices.text: Include a client secret in the app, obfuscate it, and use it to exchange the authorization code.
choices.explanation: A shared secret cannot be kept confidential in a distributed public client.

choices.text: Use the authorization code flow with PKCE S256 in a public client without a secret, and send the original code_verifier when exchanging the code.
choices.explanation: This binds the issued code to the verification value held by the client that initiated the authorization request.

choices.text: Send the same code_challenge in the authorization request and token exchange, and do not retain the code_verifier in the app.
choices.explanation: The token exchange requires the code_verifier used to calculate the challenge; the same challenge value cannot perform the verification.

choices.text: Check only that the OAuth state values match, and send no verification value when exchanging the code.
choices.explanation: state and PKCE serve different purposes. Checking state does not bind the code to the requester at the token endpoint.

source.label: Cognitoでの認可コードとPKCE

learning.reason: Instead of placing a fixed secret in a distributed app, create proof for each authorization and code exchange.
learning.concept: Continue to validate state and verify the client during the code exchange; they serve different purposes.

sourceLabel: Authorization Code Flow and PKCE in Cognito

title: Pin the build runtime for reproducibility
prompt: The AWS managed image used by CodeBuild includes several Python runtimes. You want to specify the version used by a build in the project repository and keep that same version selected even if the corresponding image's default changes. Where should you configure it?

choices.text: Add the Python version name to the artifact produced by CodeBuild.
choices.explanation: The artifact name is an identifier; it does not select which Python runtime the build invokes.

choices.text: Specify an image-supported Python version under runtime-versions in the buildspec install phase.
choices.explanation: On supported images, this selects the runtime version to use when the build starts.

choices.text: Specify only the Runtime for the function deployed to Lambda.
choices.explanation: The runtime specified for a deployed function does not change the CodeBuild toolchain.

choices.text: Record the Python version only in the package dependency lockfile.
choices.explanation: Package versions and the interpreter selected by CodeBuild are managed separately.

source.label: CodeBuildで選べるランタイムバージョン

learning.reason: Make the build environment choice explicit in a setting that can be managed in source control.
learning.concept: The runtime combinations you can specify vary by managed image.

title: Retain test results for audits beyond 30 days
prompt: CodeBuild registers JUnit-format results in an existing report group. Auditors also need to inspect details of failed test cases from 90 days ago. While continuing to use standard CodeBuild reports, which setting lets you retrieve the original test results after 30 days?

choices.text: Extend the retention period for CodeBuild CloudWatch Logs to 90 days.
choices.explanation: Extending log retention does not change the report expiration or retain the JUnit files.

choices.text: Add 90days to the report group name and use the same name for every build.
choices.explanation: The name identifies the group; it does not change the test report expiration.

choices.text: Configure the report group to export the original test result files to S3, and set the required retention period on the bucket.
choices.explanation: Standard reports expire after 30 days, but you can manage retention for raw data exported to S3.

choices.text: Retain the CodePipeline source artifact for 90 days.
choices.explanation: The source artifact does not automatically include test results produced after the build runs.

source.label: CodeBuildのテストレポート

learning.reason: Configure the report expiration and the location for retaining the original files separately.
learning.concept: Exporting from a report group lets you retain the test tool's output format for later reference.

title: Test every combination of SDK and feature settings in parallel
prompt: Validate a package against every combination of two selected SDK versions and three feature settings. You need to inspect each combination's test logs and result independently, and adding another setting value should not require writing additional build definitions. Which method is appropriate?

choices.text: Define the SDK version and feature setting as dynamic properties in CodeBuild batch build-matrix.
choices.explanation: This creates an independent build for each specified combination of values and can run them in parallel.

choices.text: Use build-graph with one node for the SDK and another for the feature setting, and add a dependency.
choices.explanation: This can express dependencies between two tasks, but it does not expand tasks for each combination.

choices.text: Use build-fanout to start multiple copies of the same environment configuration.
choices.explanation: This creates copies of the same configuration; it does not expand all combinations of different values.

choices.text: Run every combination sequentially in one standard build and inspect only CodeBuild's final status.
choices.explanation: Even if every configuration is tested, this does not provide an independent build result for each combination.

source.label: CodeBuildのバッチビルドbuildspec

learning.reason: List the test configurations as sets of values and let the build tool expand them.
learning.concept: Dependency order, splitting the same configuration, and combining different configurations are distinct use cases.

title: Build only when the target directory in a shared repository changes
prompt: Several applications share a Git repository. A V2 pipeline using a connected source must start only when a push to main changes files under services/orders/, and must not start when the only change in that directory is an update to Markdown files. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Create separate push-filter entries for pushes to main and for the order service path.
choices.explanation: If separate entries are evaluated as OR conditions, the pipeline could start when only the branch or only the path matches.

choices.text: Use one push filter that includes main and configure Markdown files as the only included paths.
choices.explanation: This includes only the files you want to exclude, reversing which changes start the pipeline.

choices.text: Set main as a build environment variable, start the pipeline on every push, and check the branch during the build.
choices.explanation: This does not limit pipeline starts and causes runs that do not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Use one push filter with main and the order service path in the include conditions, and specify Markdown files in the path exclude conditions.
choices.explanation: The branch and file path conditions in the same filter must both match, and matching excluded paths take precedence.

source.label: CodePipelineのGitトリガーフィルター

learning.reason: Use one filter to require both the branch and the target path to match.
learning.concept: Distinguish the OR logic between multiple filters from the AND logic among conditions within the same filter.

title: Apply the approved change set in the same execution
prompt: CodePipeline updates a production CloudFormation stack. The approver must review the resource differences in the change set that was created, then approve it, and the same change set must be executed after approval. Production resources must not be changed before review. In what order should the actions be configured?

choices.text: Run CREATE_UPDATE, then manually approve the updated stack and accept the result.
choices.explanation: CREATE_UPDATE updates production resources first, so they change before approval.

choices.text: Use CHANGE_SET_REPLACE to create a change set with a unique name for each execution, then, after manual approval, run CHANGE_SET_EXECUTE with the same stack name and change set name.
choices.explanation: This separates the proposed changes from applying them, so the reviewed plan is executed after approval.

choices.text: Create change sets with different names before and after manual approval, then execute the newly created one.
choices.explanation: This does not ensure that the change set reviewed during approval is the one actually applied.

choices.text: Run CHANGE_SET_EXECUTE first, then use CHANGE_SET_REPLACE to create the change set for review.
choices.explanation: Applying the change first does not provide a review of the differences beforehand.

source.label: CodePipelineのCloudFormationアクション

learning.reason: Separate the action that plans production changes from the action that applies the plan.
learning.concept: Match the change set that was reviewed during approval to the name of the change set that is actually used.

title: Prepare native dependencies for the Lambda runtime
prompt: A SAM ZIP-based Lambda function developed on macOS uses a Python package with a C extension. When the regular build is run on macOS, the library cannot be loaded by Lambda. The function's execution architecture and Python version are already defined in the template. Which build method should you use while retaining the ZIP package format?

choices.text: Copy macOS site-packages into the ZIP as is, then recompile them in Lambda after deployment.
choices.explanation: Build tools for the target environment may not be available when Lambda starts, and macOS binaries cannot be loaded.

choices.text: Change only the ZIP file extension when sam deploy transfers the artifact to S3.
choices.explanation: Uploading the artifact does not change the platform of the binaries inside the package.

choices.text: Run sam build --use-container using a build image compatible with the runtime and architecture.
choices.explanation: Dependencies can be prepared in an environment compatible with Lambda, and the build can still produce a ZIP package.

choices.text: Move the existing Python binaries into a Lambda layer while keeping the build environment on macOS.
choices.explanation: Changing where the package is stored does not change binary compatibility.

source.label: AWS SAMのビルド

learning.reason: Build native dependencies in an environment compatible with the target runtime, rather than the local environment.
learning.concept: A container can be used for the build even when the package format is ZIP.

title: Choose how to update the service that consumes a shared dependency
prompt: Several Lambda functions use version 7 of a layer containing the same library. You want to validate a fixed version in one test function first, then roll it out to the other functions later. What should you change while allowing the other functions to continue using the old library?

choices.text: Publish the fix as a new layer version and update only the test function to use the ARN with the new version.
choices.explanation: Each function is associated with the layer version it specifies. The configurations of the other functions remain unchanged.

choices.text: Overwrite the contents of layer version 7 and change only the test function's alias.
choices.explanation: A published layer version cannot be changed, and a function alias does not update the layer itself.

choices.text: Remove the layer from all functions and let each function resolve the latest version without specifying a layer version.
choices.explanation: A layer is associated using a versioned ARN. This does not create a workflow in which the latest version is selected automatically.

choices.text: Add permission to view the layer to the test function's role, but leave the function configuration on the old version.
choices.explanation: Granting permission to use the layer does not switch the version used by the function.

source.label: Lambdaレイヤーの依存管理

learning.reason: Separate publishing the dependency library from changing the reference on the consuming side.
learning.concept: Numbered layer versions support staged updates per function and reproducible configurations.

title: Restart ECS tasks with a new secret
prompt: An ECS service task definition injects a Secrets Manager secret as an environment variable. Rotation succeeded, but existing tasks still use the old value. How can you run the existing service with the new value while keeping the reference to the current version and the task definition unchanged?

choices.text: Save the same secret again and wait for the environment variables in running tasks to update.
choices.explanation: Environment variables are injected when a task starts; they are not updated automatically while it is running.

choices.text: Force a new deployment of the ECS service to replace its tasks.
choices.explanation: At startup, the tasks retrieve the current secret value through the same reference.

choices.text: Only add GetSecretValue to the task role to switch existing environment variables to the current version.
choices.explanation: Unless the application is changed to call the retrieval API, adding permission alone does not change existing environment variables.

choices.text: Save the new value to a file in each existing container and have the secret environment variable automatically reference that file.
choices.explanation: Changing a file does not automatically update the environment variables of an already running process.

source.label: ECSのシークレット環境変数

learning.reason: With startup-time value injection, rotating the secret must be paired with replacing the running containers.
learning.concept: Even if the reference stays the same, newly started tasks can read the value available at that time.

title: Import an existing bucket into a stack while preserving its data
prompt: You want to place a manually created S3 bucket under CloudFormation stack management while preserving its current objects and physical bucket name. The bucket must remain if the stack is deleted. The resource type supports resource import. Which two steps are required?

choices.text: Add an AWS::S3::Bucket definition matching the existing configuration to the template and set DeletionPolicy to Retain.
choices.explanation: Provide the resource definition required for import and specify that the physical bucket should be retained when removed from the stack.

choices.text: Run a normal CREATE_UPDATE with the same physical name; it will automatically take over an existing bucket.
choices.explanation: A normal create or update does not import an existing standalone bucket into a stack.

choices.text: Empty and delete the bucket, then create it again with the same name from the stack.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to preserve the existing objects and physical resource.

choices.text: Specify the existing bucket name as the physical resource identifier and run a CloudFormation import operation.
choices.explanation: This associates the existing resource with a logical ID in the template.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Snapshot to trigger an import during a normal stack update.
choices.explanation: An update replacement policy is not a way to import an external resource.

source.label: CloudFormationの手動リソースインポート

learning.reason: Importing a resource differs from recreating its physical resource.
learning.concept: Associate the existing resource identifier with a management logical ID and specify in the template how to handle it on deletion.

title: Check a critical setting before deployment
prompt: A small CDK refactor must not change the visibility timeout setting of the generated SQS queue, as required by your conventions. Which unit test checks this without deploying to the cloud and does not fail if unrelated resources are added to the template?

choices.text: Deploy the CDK stack to production every time and measure messages received by SQS.
choices.explanation: This can verify actual behavior, but it is not a unit test without deployment.

choices.text: Require the entire synthesized CDK template to match a single snapshot exactly.
choices.explanation: The comparison would fail even if only an out-of-scope resource were added.

choices.text: Use Template.fromStack to get the synthesized result and hasResourceProperties to check the target queue's properties.
choices.explanation: This checks only the resource and settings of interest without deploying them to the cloud.

choices.text: Check only that the stack output contains the word Timeout.
choices.explanation: This does not show whether the intended resource has the specific property value.

source.label: AWS CDKアプリケーションのテスト

learning.reason: Verify only the synthesized template properties that determine the required behavior.
learning.concept: A test for a specific configuration can be narrowly scoped instead of fixing the entire template in a snapshot.

title: Test how to read a notification without using a real bucket
prompt: You changed a Lambda handler that extracts the bucket name and key from an S3 notification. This time, you want to test only its JSON input handling, without uploading anything to the development account or configuring notifications. A SAM function definition is available. Which procedure fits?

choices.text: Use sam local generate-event to output an example S3 creation event as JSON, then pass that event to sam local invoke.
choices.explanation: You can invoke the function locally with input modeled on a service event.

choices.text: Use sam local start-api to send an HTTP GET request and treat it as the same input event.
choices.explanation: An HTTP API event has a different structure from an S3 notification event.

choices.text: Use sam validate to inspect the template and confirm that the input key is read.
choices.explanation: Template validation does not run the function code with the specified event.

choices.text: Use sam sync --watch to deploy to a cloud development stack and place a file in S3.
choices.explanation: This can test the real service, but goes beyond the requested local-only scope.

source.label: SAMのローカルイベント生成

learning.reason: Use the event shape being tested and combine event generation with a procedure that runs the function.
learning.concept: Testing local input and confirming that events are delivered in the cloud cover different scopes.

title: Preview lifecycle policy candidates before deletion
prompt: You want to automatically expire unused images in an ECR repository. Before deleting any images, you need to see which images a new set of prioritized rules would select, and make sure it does not select images kept for past rollbacks. Which procedure should you choose?

choices.text: Make the repository tag-immutable and determine expiration from the tag-immutability exclusion list.
choices.explanation: Tag mutability settings do not show which images are candidates for expiration.

choices.text: Apply the lifecycle policy normally, then inspect CloudTrail deletion records to identify the candidates.
choices.explanation: Expiration may begin after the policy is applied, so this does not let you review the impact beforehand.

choices.text: Use image vulnerability scan results to determine which images have reached the expiration threshold.
choices.explanation: Image scanning does not evaluate lifecycle rule conditions or priority.

choices.text: Start a preview of the proposed lifecycle policy, review the images marked for expiration, and then apply the policy.
choices.explanation: The preview shows which images match, letting you review the rules’ impact without deleting them.

source.label: ECRライフサイクルポリシーのプレビュー

learning.reason: Check which images the rules would expire before enabling the policy.
learning.concept: Image scanning, tag-immutability controls, and retention management are separate functions.

title: Why the old stop hook runs
prompt: In a CodeDeploy deployment to EC2, you update the new revision’s AppSpec file and stop script. On an instance that is already running, however, ApplicationStop runs the old script. Which statement describes the normal CodeDeploy EC2 lifecycle behavior?

choices.text: ApplicationStop runs after the new revision is installed, but only old CloudWatch Logs were displayed.
choices.explanation: In the normal sequence, ApplicationStop runs before the new revision is downloaded.

choices.text: ApplicationStop uses the AppSpec file and scripts from the last successfully deployed revision.
choices.explanation: When stopping the old version, the hook from the last successful revision recorded on the instance is run.

choices.text: All hooks are fixed to the AppSpec file used when the deployment group was created and cannot be changed later.
choices.explanation: Each application revision can have its own AppSpec file. The stop hook has a specific revision-selection behavior.

choices.text: ApplicationStop runs only during the first deployment, so a different hook must have run this time.
choices.explanation: This hook does not run on the first deployment, when there is no previous deployment.

source.label: CodeDeploy EC2のAppSpecフック

learning.reason: Check which revision supplies the hook as well as the hook’s position in the lifecycle.
learning.concept: The procedure for stopping the previous application belongs to the revision being replaced.

title: Handle responses with no configuration changes
prompt: You are using the AppConfig Data API in a custom client. The initial configuration is retrieved successfully, but reusing the same initial token causes an error. When there are no changes, the response body is empty. Which two implementations are appropriate?

choices.text: Reuse the first token for the same session in every GetLatestConfiguration call.
choices.explanation: A polling token can be used only once; it cannot be reused.

choices.text: Pass each response’s NextPollConfigurationToken to the next call and observe the specified polling interval.
choices.explanation: Using the next token and interval returned by the service avoids reusing a token.

choices.text: If the response body is empty, clear the cache because the configuration has changed to an empty value.
choices.explanation: This would discard the last valid configuration when there is simply no new configuration body.

choices.text: Keep the previous configuration when the response body is empty, and update the cache only when a new body is returned.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes an unchanged configuration from an unsuccessful API call and preserves a valid value while there are no changes.

choices.text: Ignore the response’s NextPollIntervalInSeconds and send requests without delay whenever a NextPollConfigurationToken is returned.
choices.explanation: Even when using a new token, follow the service’s specified interval before polling again.

source.label: AppConfig Data GetLatestConfiguration

learning.reason: Handle the information that advances polling separately from the configuration body the application adopts.
learning.concept: Do not discard a valid value when there is no change; update the polling token as directed by the service.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Inspect read capacity consumed by each resource
prompt: The same DynamoDB table receives Query requests against the table itself and against several indexes. During load testing, you want each request’s response to show whether the read capacity was consumed by the table or an index. Which request parameter should you specify?

choices.text: Set ReturnConsumedCapacity to INDEXES.
choices.explanation: The response includes the total consumed capacity and a breakdown for the table and indexes used by the operation.

choices.text: Set ReturnConsumedCapacity to TOTAL.
choices.explanation: This returns the operation’s total capacity, but not a breakdown for the table and indexes.

choices.text: Set Select to COUNT.
choices.explanation: This requests the number of items returned; it does not enable a breakdown of capacity information.

choices.text: Put the index name in ProjectionExpression.
choices.explanation: A projection specifies which attributes to return from items; it does not control capacity information in the response.

source.label: DynamoDB Queryの消費容量情報

learning.reason: Get per-request clues about where capacity was consumed, in addition to aggregate metrics.
learning.concept: When capacity details are needed in the response, specify whether you need a breakdown or only the total.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Compare Error Rates as Invocation Volume Changes
prompt: The number of Lambda invocations per minute varies widely by time of day. You want CloudWatch to show the proportion of executions of the same function and alias that resulted in errors, rather than the raw error count. Use only existing metrics and compare intervals in which invocations occurred during the same one-minute period. Which calculation should you use?

choices.text: Divide the Sum of Errors by a fixed value of 60.
choices.explanation: This gives a value closer to a rate per unit of time; it does not show how many executions failed out of the total.

choices.text: Get the Sum of Errors and Invocations for the same period and target, then divide Errors by Invocations in a CloudWatch metric math expression.
choices.explanation: Counting the numerator and denominator over the same interval gives the proportion of executions in that interval that resulted in errors.

choices.text: Divide the Maximum of Errors by the Maximum of ConcurrentExecutions.
choices.explanation: Concurrent executions are the number of executions in progress at a point in time, not the total number that ran during that minute.

choices.text: Subtract Throttles from Errors and display the difference as the error proportion.
choices.explanation: The difference between these two counts is not a proportion of all invoked executions.

source.label: CloudWatchのメトリクス数式

learning.reason: To compare intervals with different traffic volumes, normalize using counts from the same population.
learning.concept: Combine numerator and denominator metrics that use the same period, statistic, and dimensions.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Generate a Unique Initialization ID for Each Restored Environment
prompt: You enabled SnapStart for a Java Lambda function. During initialization, it generates a UUID to identify the execution environment, but the same UUID appears in logs from different restored environments. You need a different value for each restored environment, not for each invocation. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Generate multiple UUIDs during the same initialization and save only the last one in the state.
choices.explanation: If the final value is included in the snapshot, it is copied to multiple restored environments.

choices.text: Use the function version and alias name in place of the UUID.
choices.explanation: Multiple execution environments can run with the same version and alias.

choices.text: Generate the UUID in a beforeCheckpoint hook that runs before the SnapStart snapshot is created.
choices.explanation: This does not solve the problem: a value generated before the checkpoint is retained in the snapshot.

choices.text: Generate a new UUID for each execution environment in an afterRestore hook.
choices.explanation: Recreating the value after each restore avoids copying the same value that was included in the snapshot.

source.label: Lambda SnapStartで一意性を保つ

learning.reason: Separate state shared from the snapshot from state created by each environment after restoration.
learning.concept: A value that must be unique can be duplicated if it is included in reusable initialization state.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: VPC Connection Fails Despite Spare Function Concurrency
prompt: After adding a new Lambda function to the same VPC, you receive ENILimitReachedException. The function's reserved concurrency has headroom. Each team has many duplicated combinations of security groups and subnets for similar purposes. What should you check first to resolve the issue safely?

choices.text: Increase the function's memory to raise the network interface limit proportionally.
choices.explanation: The memory setting does not increase the VPC network interface quota.

choices.text: Check VPC ENI usage and quotas, and determine whether functions with the same communication requirements can reuse subnet and security group configurations where appropriate.
choices.explanation: Lambda uses Hyperplane ENIs for configurations, and some ENIs can be shared by functions with the same configuration. This can help investigate the quota issue.

choices.text: Increase Reserved Concurrency to increase the available VPC ENIs.
choices.explanation: The concurrency allocation and VPC networking quota are separate.

choices.text: Add NAT gateways so the functions no longer need to use VPC interfaces.
choices.explanation: A NAT gateway provides an outbound route but does not replace the Lambda-side mechanism for connecting to a VPC.

source.label: Lambdaのネットワーク問題の診断

learning.reason: Distinguish the concurrency quota from the network quota for VPC connectivity.
learning.concept: Functions with the same network configuration can share interfaces more readily than when their configurations are unnecessarily different.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: No Messages from Long Polling with Many In-Flight Messages
prompt: Messages continue to be sent to an SQS standard queue, but workers using long polling do not receive new messages. The queue has messages waiting to be received, and ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible is near the service's in-flight message limit. There is no usual OverLimit response. Which investigation should be prioritized?

choices.text: Conclude that the in-flight message limit has not been reached because the receive response did not include OverLimit.
choices.explanation: With long polling, SQS may stop returning new messages at the limit without returning an error.

choices.text: Treat the queue as empty and only increase the sender's delivery rate.
choices.explanation: Messages are already waiting to be received, and sending more will not free up in-flight capacity.

choices.text: Check worker completion and the success rate of DeleteMessage to determine whether undeleted messages are occupying in-flight capacity.
choices.explanation: Messages remain in flight while their visibility timeout is active. With long polling, an error might not be returned explicitly when the limit is reached.

choices.text: Do not investigate deletion; increase WaitTimeSeconds because a longer wait will lift the in-flight message limit.
choices.explanation: The call's wait time does not change the in-flight message limit.

source.label: SQSの可視性と処理中メッセージ上限

learning.reason: Do not infer the balance of waiting and in-flight messages from an empty response alone.
learning.concept: Deleting a message after processing completes frees in-flight capacity without waiting for the message to be received again.

sourceLabel: SQS visibility and in-flight message limit

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Distinguishing deployment failures from individual task stops
prompt: A deployment circuit breaker is configured for a rolling update in Amazon ECS. You want to notify the operations team only when the service deployment is determined to have failed, without notifications for a small number of stopped tasks. Do not poll DescribeServices. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Send a notification for every STOPPED event from ECS Task State Change.
choices.explanation: This also includes tasks stopped during normal replacement and does not directly indicate that the service deployment as a whole failed.

choices.text: Use EventBridge to match ECS Deployment State Change events with SERVICE_DEPLOYMENT_FAILED for the target service, then send them to the notification destination.
choices.explanation: This directly uses the event that ECS emits when it determines that a service deployment has failed.

choices.text: Use CloudWatch to detect tasks whose CPU utilization has reached 0 and treat each occurrence as a deployment failure.
choices.explanation: CPU utilization alone cannot determine whether a deployment succeeded or why a task stopped.

choices.text: Notify on a successful CloudTrail UpdateService event and treat acceptance of the request as confirmation of deployment success or failure.
choices.explanation: Acceptance of the update API request does not include the outcome of subsequent initialization or health checks.

source.label: ECSデプロイ状態のイベント

learning.reason: Distinguish API acceptance, task state, and the deployment state of the service as a whole.
learning.concept: Limiting notifications to the operationally relevant state change helps avoid false alerts during normal configuration-driven task replacement.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Filtering traces by a recorded customer segment
prompt: A plan segment that contains no personally identifiable information has already been added to the distributed traces sent to X-Ray. When the issue recurs, you want to first narrow the trace list by specifying that segment. Where should you record it?

choices.text: Put the segment only in metadata and assume that its value is automatically indexed across all traces.
choices.explanation: Metadata can be viewed in a trace, but it is not indexed for searches using filter expressions.

choices.text: Append the segment to every service name on a per-request basis.
choices.explanation: This changes service-name aggregation and is not how to add an attribute needed for searching.

choices.text: Record the segment as an annotation key and value.
choices.explanation: Annotations are indexed and can be referenced in trace filter expressions.

choices.text: Replace part of the trace ID with the segment.
choices.explanation: A trace ID identifies related segments; it is not a value for storing arbitrary search attributes.

source.label: AWS X-Rayのアノテーションとメタデータ

learning.reason: Distinguish attributes used only for viewing an individual trace from attributes needed as search criteria.
learning.concept: Intentionally index values that need to be searchable. Manage the scope of recorded sensitive values separately.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Failing promptly when no database connection can be borrowed
prompt: When an API borrows a connection from RDS Proxy, database connections are temporarily exhausted, and the request ends up waiting until its overall deadline. The application must return a failure within the time remaining, and the SQL timeout after a connection is established is already short. Which proxy setting should you adjust?

choices.text: Shorten IdleClientTimeout to limit how long a request waits to borrow a connection.
choices.explanation: This setting controls the lifetime of an idle client connection; it does not control how long a request waits to borrow a connection.

choices.text: Set MaxIdleConnectionsPercent to 0 so that borrowing fails immediately.
choices.explanation: This setting controls how many idle database connections the pool retains, not how long a request waits to acquire a connection.

choices.text: Set ConnectionBorrowTimeout to a duration within the remaining time, allowing a margin for response handling.
choices.explanation: This setting limits how long a request waits when no database connection is available to borrow.

choices.text: Reduce the SQL execution timeout further so that it also applies to the wait in Proxy before a connection is available.
choices.explanation: The SQL timeout does not control the Proxy wait that occurs before a connection is borrowed.

source.label: RDS Proxy接続設定

learning.reason: Separate the overall request deadline into the wait to borrow a connection and SQL execution.
learning.concept: The timeout is configured in a different place before a connection is acquired than while SQL is executing.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Resuming without repeating successful steps
prompt: A Standard workflow failed the previous day. You do not want to repeat the preparation step that already completed successfully. The external dependency for the failed operation has been restored, and you want to continue with the output of the successful step using the original input and state machine definition. The execution meets the conditions for redrive. Which method should you use?

choices.text: Start a new execution from the beginning with StartExecution.
choices.explanation: Even if you pass the original input, a new execution runs from the beginning, including the successful steps.

choices.text: Resume the failed existing execution with RedriveExecution.
choices.explanation: This continues from the failed portion and uses the history and results of successful steps.

choices.text: Change the input of the failed execution and rerun it from its current intermediate state.
choices.explanation: Redrive preserves the original input; it does not overwrite the input of a failed execution.

choices.text: Add Retry to the failed task's definition and wait for the already terminated execution to resume automatically.
choices.explanation: Editing the definition does not automatically resume a terminated execution.

source.label: Step Functionsの実行redrive

learning.reason: Check whether successful work can be carried forward within the same execution.
learning.concept: Idempotency is still needed if a step being retried by redrive has partial side effects.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Process keys in parallel within a shard
prompt: IteratorAge is increasing for a Lambda function that reads from Kinesis. Read throughput, the Lambda account concurrency quota, and downstream capacity are all sufficient. The delay is caused by processing only one batch at a time for each shard. How can you increase processing throughput through the event source mapping while preserving record order for the same partition key?

choices.text: Increase the event source mapping's ParallelizationFactor.
choices.explanation: This allows multiple batches from one shard to be processed concurrently while preserving order for records with the same partition key.

choices.text: Change the stream's starting position to LATEST so that queued batches are processed in parallel.
choices.explanation: The starting position changes which records are read; it does not change the number of concurrent batches per shard.

choices.text: Increase only the Lambda function's Reserved Concurrency and leave the parallelization factor at 1.
choices.explanation: The account quota is already sufficient, so this does not change the mapping's limit of one concurrent processing unit per shard.

choices.text: Add another event source mapping for the same stream and function so both mappings process the same records.
choices.explanation: This reads the same data as a separate subscription; it is not a setting that naturally divides the processing workload.

source.label: LambdaのKinesisイベントソースマッピング

learning.reason: Distinguish the stream's read-throughput limit from the concurrency used to process the batches that have been read.
learning.concept: A setting can parallelize work within a shard while preserving the required order for each key.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Different languages share a cache entry
prompt: CloudFront caches an information page at the same public URL. The origin switches the content based on the X-Site-Language header, which the application normalizes to ja or en before sending. The header is already forwarded to the origin, yet users sometimes receive a cached response in another language. How can you fix this while keeping caching enabled?

choices.text: Add the header to the origin request policy again.
choices.explanation: This changes the value forwarded to the origin, but not the key used to select a cached response.

choices.text: Shorten the cache TTL slightly and invalidate the cache only when another language is served.
choices.explanation: This may shorten the period of an incorrect response, but different languages would still use the same cache key.

choices.text: Add X-Site-Language to a response headers policy so it is included in the response to viewers.
choices.explanation: Changing the returned header does not separate the cache entries CloudFront uses.

choices.text: Include X-Site-Language in the cache key in the cache policy.
choices.explanation: This caches responses separately for each language value. A header included in the key can also be forwarded to the origin request.

source.label: CloudFrontのキャッシュキーポリシー

learning.reason: Make the cache distinguish responses that the origin varies by language.
learning.concept: Including headers that do not change a response in the key needlessly fragments the cache.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Investigate an integration error without function logs
prompt: An HTTP API's existing access logs record only status code 500 for a Lambda integration. There are no logs in Lambda for the request, and you need to investigate an integration error that occurred before the function ran. Which variable should you add to the access log format without recording the API request body?

choices.text: Add only $context.requestTime.
choices.explanation: This helps correlate events by time but does not show the integration error.

choices.text: Use $context.integrationErrorMessage to record the integration error message.
choices.explanation: This provides information about integration errors observed by API Gateway, such as why a Lambda invocation failed.

choices.text: Treat $context.routeKey as the error message.
choices.explanation: The route identifies which entry point was used; it does not show why the integration failed.

choices.text: Record $context.integrationLatency and use that duration alone to determine the reason for the integration failure.
choices.explanation: This provides the integration response time, but not details such as why the invocation was rejected.

source.label: HTTP APIのLambda統合エラー調査

learning.reason: Errors that occur before reaching the function can still have diagnostic information available to the component invoking the integration.
learning.concept: Correlate the relevant access logs and use diagnostic information available without recording the request body.

sourceLabel: HTTP API Lambda integration error investigation

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: A container runs out of memory despite spare task capacity
prompt: A Fargate task has 1,024 MiB of memory, and its stopped worker container has a hard limit of 256 MiB. The stop reason is OutOfMemoryError, and a known healthy batch needs 330 MiB. A sidecar running at the same time stays within 128 MiB. Which change should you investigate without changing the task size?

choices.text: Increase the sidecar's CPU and keep the worker's hard limit at 256 MiB.
choices.explanation: Changing CPU allocation does not raise the worker's memory limit.

choices.text: Increase only the worker's memoryReservation and leave its hard memory limit at 256 MiB.
choices.explanation: The reservation and hard limit are separate settings. Keeping the hard limit prevents the worker from using the required amount.

choices.text: Raise the worker's hard memory limit to a value that accommodates 330 MiB plus headroom, and verify that the worker and other containers fit within the task's total memory budget.
choices.explanation: The worker stops at its container-specific limit, which is below the task's total capacity, so adjust the limit that is constraining it.

choices.text: Extend the ALB health check grace period and ignore the worker's stop.
choices.explanation: The health check grace period does not prevent a process from stopping after exceeding its memory limit.

source.label: Amazon ECSのメモリ不足の調査

learning.reason: Check the container-level limit even when the task has unused capacity.
learning.concept: For an out-of-memory stop, first check the stop reason and actual usage, then account for the required memory and headroom in the capacity plan.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Task CPU and image platform mismatch
prompt: After switching to an ARM64 Fargate task, an existing image in ECR could not be resolved. The image manifest contains only linux/amd64, and network and registry access have been verified. Which change meets the requirement to run on ARM64 while also supporting existing AMD64 deployments?

choices.text: Tag the amd64 image as arm64 and make it runnable through the task definition alone.
choices.explanation: Changing the tag does not change the platform in the manifest or the platform of the executable binaries.

choices.text: Extend the retention period for amd64 images in the ECR lifecycle policy.
choices.explanation: Changing the retention period does not provide an image for ARM64.

choices.text: Switch the task back to X86_64 and apply the ARM64 setting only to the build environment.
choices.explanation: This restores operation for AMD64, but does not meet the production task's ARM64 requirement.

choices.text: Publish a multi-architecture image that also includes linux/arm64, and update the ARM64 task to reference it.
choices.explanation: The image includes a platform that can run on the target environment while continuing to support existing amd64 environments.

source.label: Fargateタスク定義のランタイムプラットフォーム

learning.reason: Compare the CPU required by the task definition with the target CPU of the image in the registry.
learning.concept: Even when distributing a single tag to multiple environments, the image must be runnable in each environment.

sourceLabel: Runtime platform for Fargate task definitions

title: Process nonmatching events from a shared queue
prompt: Multiple processes share an SQS order queue. Even after adding an event source filter to the billing Lambda, delivery events that do not match the filter must still be passed to another process. Given what happens when a message retrieved by Lambda does not match the filter, what should you choose?

choices.text: Enable the filter on the shared queue. Nonmatching messages will always return to the delivery process after the visibility timeout.
choices.explanation: A nonmatching message received by Lambda from SQS is deleted.

choices.text: Route events when they are sent, and separate the billing and delivery queues. Configure each queue's Lambda mapping independently.
choices.explanation: This delivers the required input to both processes without relying on nonmatching messages surviving in a shared queue.

choices.text: In addition to the Lambda mapping, configure a dead-letter queue on the queue, and have delivery read all messages from there.
choices.explanation: A filter mismatch is not a processing failure retry and does not trigger queue redrive.

choices.text: Set the receive batch size to 1 and enable the filter. Only delivery events will remain in the shared queue.
choices.explanation: Changing the batch size does not change the behavior that deletes nonmatching messages.

source.label: LambdaのSQSイベントフィルター

learning.reason: Check how filtering after retrieval affects the lifetime of a message in its original queue.
learning.concept: When messages must be delivered independently to multiple consumers, distinguish routing at delivery time from filtering at consumption time.

title: Use the API value as the correlation ID sent to the integration
prompt: You need to observe an existing HTTP API HTTP integration without changing the backend. For X-Service-Trace sent to the integration, use only the API Gateway requestId, and do not preserve the original value if the client sends a header with the same name. Which mapping should you specify?

choices.text: Set $context.requestId for append:header.X-Service-Trace.
choices.explanation: append adds a value when one already exists, so it cannot remove the original value.

choices.text: Set $context.requestId for overwrite:querystring.X-Service-Trace.
choices.explanation: This overwrites the query string and does not affect the request header read by the backend.

choices.text: Set $context.requestId for overwrite:header.X-Service-Trace in the request parameter mapping.
choices.explanation: This replaces the target header in the integration request with the API value.

choices.text: Add $context.requestId to a response header for the client.
choices.explanation: This does not set the value in the request sent to the HTTP integration.

source.label: HTTP APIパラメーターマッピング

learning.reason: Distinguish the direction of the rewrite, where the value is stored, and whether it is appended or overwritten.
learning.concept: Setting the correlation value before the integration prevents a client-supplied value with the same header name from being passed through unchanged to the backend.

title: Map a Lambda business error to HTTP 409
prompt: API Gateway's REST API invokes Lambda through a non-proxy integration, and the existing mapping is used for successful responses. You want only an order conflict error thrown by the function to return 409, while preserving the handling of other errors and successful responses. The Lambda error message has a distinguishable prefix. Where should you configure this?

choices.text: Require the error prefix as a field in method request validation.
choices.explanation: Request validation handles input before the function is invoked.

choices.text: Have Lambda include statusCode in the exception body and assume that this automatically returns 409 for a non-proxy integration.
choices.explanation: The response contract for a proxy integration cannot be used to transform errors in this non-proxy integration.

choices.text: Set only the HTTP code for stage throttling rejections to 409.
choices.explanation: A throttling rejection is different from a business error reported by the backend.

choices.text: Define a 409 method response, then map only the matching Lambda error with the selectionPattern in the integration response.
choices.explanation: With a non-proxy integration, you can explicitly map an integration response to the error message it matches.

source.label: API GatewayでのLambdaエラー処理

learning.reason: Transform a function's business error to match the HTTP contract presented to the client.
learning.concept: The place where the response code is determined differs between proxy and non-proxy integrations.

sourceLabel: Handling Lambda errors in API Gateway

title: Select an event when either of two fields matches
prompt: Use EventBridge to filter inspection events. The source and event type are fixed, and the event should be routed to the responsible team if detail.severity is critical or customerTier is premium. Both conditions do not need to be true at the same time. How should this be represented in a single rule?

choices.text: Keep the source and event type conditions, and specify the severity condition and the customerTier condition as separate fields under detail.$or.
choices.explanation: This evaluates conditions on different fields as an OR while keeping the shared conditions outside it.

choices.text: List severity and customerTier as ordinary fields under detail.
choices.explanation: Listing separate fields normally requires both conditions to match.

choices.text: List critical and premium in the array of severity values, and omit customerTier.
choices.explanation: This compares values only for the same field, so it cannot evaluate customerTier.

choices.text: Put the conditions in the target input transformer and leave the rule's event pattern unchanged.
choices.explanation: An input transformer changes the shape of a selected event; it does not replace rule-based filtering.

source.label: EventBridgeイベントパターンの演算子

learning.reason: Represent conditions that are always required separately from conditions where either one is sufficient.
learning.concept: Matching multiple values of one field differs from expressing an OR across multiple fields.

title: Route to a queue only when event delivery fails
prompt: An EventBridge rule targets a standard SQS queue. If the rule cannot deliver an event to the queue, the original event and information about the failed rule or target must be available in a separate queue. Worker processing failures after the message reaches the queue are handled through a separate path. What should be configured?

choices.text: Configure only a redrive policy on the target SQS queue.
choices.explanation: A redrive policy for consumer failures cannot capture an event that never reached the queue.

choices.text: Configure a standard SQS DLQ on the EventBridge rule's target and allow EventBridge to send messages to it.
choices.explanation: Events that could not be delivered to the target can be received with attributes about the target rule and the cause.

choices.text: Add the failure-notification queue as an ordinary second target.
choices.explanation: An ordinary target receives events that match from the start; it cannot be limited to delivery failures.

choices.text: Configure asynchronous OnFailure on the Lambda that reads from the target.
choices.explanation: This cannot capture an EventBridge-to-SQS delivery failure that occurs before Lambda receives the message.

source.label: EventBridgeターゲットのデッドレターキュー

learning.reason: Attach the failure-handling configuration to the delivery path where the failure occurs.
learning.concept: Failure to deliver to a target and failure to consume data after it arrives are different stages.

title: Retry an interrupted receive as the same attempt
prompt: A worker reading an SQS FIFO queue calls ReceiveMessage but does not receive the response because the network connection is interrupted. The worker wants to retry the same logical receive shortly afterward and receive the original messages or ReceiptHandle again. The received messages have not been deleted or had their visibility changed. What should it use?

choices.text: Use the MessageDeduplicationId from sending to control duplicate ReceiveMessage calls.
choices.explanation: That ID is used for send-side deduplication; receive calls use a different identifier.

choices.text: Use the same MaxNumberOfMessages and WaitTimeSeconds values as in the previous ReceiveMessage call.
choices.explanation: Using the same batch size and wait time does not identify the request as the same logical receive.

choices.text: Set the worker ID as the MessageGroupId and use it to reproduce the ReceiveMessage response.
choices.explanation: The group ID controls ordering when sending; it does not request a prior receive response again.

choices.text: Set a ReceiveRequestAttemptId on the initial request and retry within its validity period using the same ID.
choices.explanation: For a FIFO queue, the same ID can be used to retry a logical receive and, when the conditions are met, return the same messages and handles.

source.label: SQS ReceiveMessageの受信試行ID

learning.reason: Distinguish a retry of an API call whose response was lost from a new operation.
learning.concept: The FIFO receive attempt ID and the send-side deduplication ID apply at different stages.

title: Order consecutive records from one producer
prompt: An application writes two records to Kinesis in sequence using the same partition key. It sends each record with an individual PutRecord call and wants to specify the ordering relationship with the previous successful response on the second write, instead of leaving consumers to reorder the records. What should it do?

choices.text: Put the previous hash value in the second record's Data.
choices.explanation: The record body contains application data; it is not a parameter for specifying write order at the service level.

choices.text: Pass the SequenceNumber returned by the first PutRecord call as SequenceNumberForOrdering on the second call.
choices.explanation: For the same producer and partition key, this specifies the preceding sequence number as the ordering reference.

choices.text: Use the same partition key for both writes and send them in parallel.
choices.explanation: Using the same key does not specify the service-side arrival order of concurrent requests.

choices.text: Put the sequence number in the second PartitionKey and treat it as referring to the same shard.
choices.explanation: Changing the key no longer meets the requirement to order records under the same key.

source.label: Kinesis PutRecordの書き込み順序

learning.reason: For consecutive writes that require ordering, carry the previous successful response into the next request.
learning.concept: Partition assignment and the ordering of consecutive record writes are specified separately.

title: Read related items with a consistent view
prompt: A contract and a billing quota are stored as separate DynamoDB items and updated in the same TransactWriteItems call. A reader must avoid seeing a combination in which the contract reflects the update but the billing quota is still old. The keys for both items are known. Which read should be used?

choices.text: Send GetItem requests in sequence, specifying ConsistentRead for each item.
choices.explanation: Each individual read can see committed updates, but an update could be committed between the two requests.

choices.text: Pass all keys to BatchGetItem and enable strong consistency.
choices.explanation: The consistency of each item read can be increased, but the batch does not become an atomic read.

choices.text: Pass both keys to the same TransactGetItems call.
choices.explanation: This reads multiple items as one transaction and can retrieve related items atomically.

choices.text: Specify one key in Query and get the other result from a cache.
choices.explanation: Independent cached results cannot be aligned to the same side of an update.

source.label: DynamoDB TransactGetItems

learning.reason: Distinguish strong consistency for an individual item from atomicity across multiple items.
learning.concept: When related data is updated transactionally, consider the consistency required by readers as well.

title: Update a document without overwriting an existing initial value
prompt: Each time a DynamoDB document item is edited, its update time must be refreshed. For an older item that does not yet have createdBy, set that value only on the first edit; if it already exists, preserve it. Saving the update time must always succeed. Which implementation avoids an intervening read?

choices.text: Use SET in UpdateItem to update updatedAt and specify if_not_exists(createdBy, :actor) for createdBy.
choices.explanation: This uses the initial value only when the target attribute is missing, while allowing other attributes to be updated at the same time.

choices.text: Update both attributes with UpdateItem and add attribute_not_exists(createdBy) to ConditionExpression.
choices.explanation: If createdBy already exists, the entire operation fails, so the update time cannot be saved.

choices.text: Overwrite createdBy with the current actor each time and later derive the old value from logs.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to retain the original value in the item.

choices.text: Set ReturnValues to ALL_OLD on PutItem and assume the returned old value is automatically retained in the new item.
choices.explanation: The return value setting does not change PutItem's replacement of the item.

source.label: DynamoDB更新式のif_not_exists

learning.reason: Conditional initialization of an attribute has a different failure scope from conditional execution of the entire request.
learning.concept: A single update expression can specify attributes to change and attributes whose existing values must be preserved.

title: Specify the tenant and month in key conditions
prompt: A DynamoDB table has tenantId as its partition key and a UTC timestamp followed by an order ID as its sort key; an example is 2026-10-07T12:00:00Z#A12. For a specific tenant, you need to read only October 2026 in UTC and must not read other months before filtering them out. Which Query should you use?

choices.text: Use only tenantId as the key condition and check whether the sort key is in October with FilterExpression.
choices.explanation: The filter is applied after the items matching the key condition have been read, so it does not prevent reading other months.

choices.text: Specify a tenantId match and begins_with on the sort key with 2026-10- as the key condition.
choices.explanation: This limits reads within the tenant's partition to the range with the timestamp prefix.

choices.text: Specify the tenant with begins_with on the partition key and use the sort key as a filter condition.
choices.explanation: Query requires equality for the partition key; prefix filtering is for the sort key.

choices.text: Set 2026-10- in ProjectionExpression to return only that month's items.
choices.explanation: Projection selects the attribute names to return; it does not narrow the range of item keys.

source.label: DynamoDB Queryのキー条件

learning.reason: To reduce the range actually read, express the restriction as a key condition when possible.
learning.concept: A sort key with an ordered structure and prefix can help narrow searches by period.

title: Retrieve the version selected at publication time later
prompt: A report is stored under the same key in an S3 bucket with versioning enabled. The approval system can record the version ID returned at upload time. If a newer version is created later, the approval screen must still show the content from that time. Which retrieval method should be used?

choices.text: Pass the approval date to GetObject's If-Unmodified-Since parameter.
choices.explanation: A conditional retrieval checks whether the current object meets the condition. It does not select a past version by date.

choices.text: Read the current content with GetObject and display it as approved even if its ETag differs from the one at approval time.
choices.explanation: When the latest version changes, this does not preserve the content that was approved.

choices.text: Specify the saved version ID along with the key in GetObject.
choices.explanation: A versioned object can be selected by its version identifier.

choices.text: Use ListObjectVersions to select the first version each time the content is displayed.
choices.explanation: If a newer version is added, this may read a version other than the one previously approved.

source.label: S3のオブジェクトバージョン取得

learning.reason: For a fixed reference, record the version as well as the key.
learning.concept: Conditionally reading the current object and selecting a stored past version are different operations.

title: Copying a large object without routing its data through the runtime
prompt: An 8 GB object is stored in an S3 bucket in the same Region. An application must copy the same data to another key without bringing the body into the application's memory or network path. The source version is fixed, and each copy range meets the allowed conditions. Which procedure should it use?

choices.text: Copy the 8 GB object with a single CopyObject request, then send the same request multiple times to combine the copies.
choices.explanation: A single CopyObject request exceeds the supported size limit. Repeating the same request does not create a multipart copy.

choices.text: Start a multipart upload, use UploadPartCopy to copy the source ranges into the parts, and complete the upload.
choices.explanation: S3 copies the ranges internally and combines them in part-number order when the upload is completed. The application does not need to relay the body.

choices.text: Retrieve the object in chunks with GetObject and Range, then pass each response to UploadPart.
choices.explanation: This limits memory use, but the object body passes through the application.

choices.text: Complete a multipart upload for the new key using only the UploadId of an existing multipart upload.
choices.explanation: An upload ID belongs to a specific upload and destination; it is not a reference for copying a completed object.

source.label: S3 UploadPartCopy

learning.reason: The SDK sends only the instructions for the parts; S3 handles the data movement.
learning.concept: Sending the object body from the application to upload parts differs from creating parts from source data already in S3.

title: Preventing a delayed, older notification from reverting search results
prompt: Overwrite notifications for the same S3 bucket and key can arrive in an order different from the order of changes. A search index is updated from notifications, but an older notification must not be processed after a newer change has already been applied. Which value should be stored and how should it be compared?

choices.text: Sort issued event IDs lexicographically and use the largest one for every key.
choices.explanation: There is no basis for using event IDs to determine the order of changes to the same object.

choices.text: Compare the time Lambda started processing the notification as the time the object changed in S3.
choices.explanation: Processing start order is affected by notification arrival order and does not necessarily match change order.

choices.text: Keep one largest sequencer for the entire bucket and use it for events on other keys as well.
choices.explanation: Sequencers cannot be used to compare the order of events for different keys.

choices.text: Keep the last sequencer for each bucket and key, left-pad the shorter value with zeros before comparing, and apply only a newer value.
choices.explanation: Values can be compared for the same key. If their lengths differ, pad them to equal length before comparing.

source.label: S3通知イベントのsequencer

learning.reason: Advance state using the unit for which the ordering guarantee applies.
learning.concept: Do not infer change order from notification arrival order or comparisons across keys.

title: Changing only Content-Type while preserving existing metadata
prompt: A PDF stored in S3 was registered with an incorrect Content-Type. Use CopyObject to correct it without changing the object body. Existing user metadata and the required HTTP metadata must also be preserved explicitly. Which method should be used?

choices.text: Retrieve the required existing metadata, set MetadataDirective to REPLACE, and send the new Content-Type along with the values to preserve.
choices.explanation: REPLACE is not a partial update, so values that are not changing must also be specified as new metadata.

choices.text: Leave MetadataDirective set to COPY and send only the new Content-Type.
choices.explanation: The directive to copy the original metadata does not replace the required metadata.

choices.text: Set MetadataDirective to REPLACE and send only Content-Type. All other values are automatically inherited from the original.
choices.explanation: Metadata omitted from a replacement is not necessarily preserved automatically.

choices.text: Add a Content-Type tag with PutObjectTagging so that it is returned as the HTTP Content-Type.
choices.explanation: Object tags and response metadata are different.

source.label: S3 CopyObjectのメタデータ指定

learning.reason: When replacing stored metadata, send both the values being changed and those being retained.
learning.concept: Whether unspecified values carry over depends on using COPY or REPLACE.

title: Retries from the internal queue can still occur when the retry count is 0
prompt: MaximumRetryAttempts=0 is configured for an asynchronous Lambda function. An event that caused the function to return an exception was not executed again, but an event that arrived while the concurrency limit was temporarily exhausted was executed after capacity became available. Which statement explains this difference?

choices.text: MaximumRetryAttempts always disables both function-error retries and throttling retries.
choices.explanation: A value of 0 applies to retries for function errors; throttling before execution is handled differently.

choices.text: An exception thrown during an asynchronous invocation is always retried up to the maximum event age.
choices.explanation: MaximumRetryAttempts controls the number of additional attempts for function errors.

choices.text: For throttling and other temporary delivery errors, the event returns to the asynchronous queue and is retried within limits such as elapsed time.
choices.explanation: A failure to run the function and an error returned by a function that ran use different retry settings.

choices.text: When concurrency capacity becomes available, the caller always sends a new Invoke request.
choices.explanation: The function can run later through retries from the asynchronous queue alone.

source.label: Lambda非同期呼び出しのエラーと再試行

learning.reason: Distinguish the function's execution result from a failure to obtain an execution slot.
learning.concept: The failure-attempt count and the event's allowed time in the queue are controlled by different settings.

sourceLabel: Lambda asynchronous invocation errors and retries

title: Fixing Input Conditions That Fail Despite a Catch-All
prompt: In a JSONPath-based Step Functions workflow, a state has InputPath set to $.pricing.total. When the input has an optional pricing field set to null, the state fails with States.Runtime. The state's Catch includes States.ALL. What is the best change to route to a default price when the optional field is missing?

choices.text: Add MaxAttempts to the States.ALL Catch.
choices.explanation: MaxAttempts is a Retry setting; it does not make an invalid input path valid.

choices.text: Use a Choice state to check that the required path exists and is non-null before routing to this state; otherwise, route to the default-value path.
choices.explanation: This handles the condition that causes States.Runtime before the state is entered. A States.ALL Catch does not catch this failure.

choices.text: Move States.ALL to the beginning of the list and treat it as including States.Runtime.
choices.explanation: Changing the order does not make States.ALL catch States.Runtime.

choices.text: Add one Retry when the input is null and reevaluate the same path against the unchanged input.
choices.explanation: If the input does not change, retrying does not resolve a path failure caused by a missing value.

source.label: Step Functionsのエラー処理
