learning.reason: When routing depends on input values, check those values first instead of relying only on error handling.
learning.concept: Some runtime errors are excluded even from error specifications that appear to cover all errors.

title: Pass the Original Input Forward with the Task Result Added
prompt: A Step Functions JSONPath Task calculates a tax amount. The data passed to the Task and the result format are already correct. Which setting sends the Task's result under tax to the next state while retaining the original order ID and line items?

choices.text: Omit ResultPath and assume the Task result is automatically merged with the original input.
choices.explanation: By default, ResultPath replaces the state's input with the Task result.

choices.text: Set InputPath to $.tax so that both the tax amount and the original order are output.
choices.explanation: InputPath filters the input passed to the Task; it does not combine the result with the input.

choices.text: Set ResultPath to null and assume the Task response is added to the original input.
choices.explanation: Setting it to null discards the Task result and passes only the input to the next state.

choices.text: Set ResultPath to $.tax to place the Task result at that path in the state's original input.
choices.explanation: The result is placed at the configured path while the other original input fields are retained.

source.label: Step Functions ResultPath

learning.reason: Control separately which input a state receives and where its result is placed for the next state.
learning.concept: Using a result does not require replacing the entire original input.

title: Carry the User's Previous Message into the Next Inference Request
prompt: An internal help feature uses Bedrock Converse. A user follows up with, “Make those steps shorter.” The application retains the previous response, but sends only the new message in the next API request, so the model cannot tell what “those steps” refers to. What should the application change?

choices.text: Append this user's relevant user and assistant messages to messages in order, and send them with the latest message to Converse.
choices.explanation: With a standard Converse request, the application includes the conversation history in the next call.

choices.text: Use the same model ID as before; Bedrock will restore the user's conversation history internally.
choices.explanation: A model ID alone does not identify a particular user's previous conversation.

choices.text: Increase maxTokens in the new request so that the previous response is added to the input.
choices.explanation: Changing the output limit does not add input context that was not sent.

choices.text: Extract only the token count from the previous response and pass it in requestMetadata.
choices.explanation: Information attached for logging does not give the model the contents of previous messages for inference.

source.label: Bedrock Converseの会話推論

learning.reason: Include the relevant prior messages from the history retained by the application in the next API input.
learning.concept: The identifier used to call a model and the method for managing each user's conversation are different things.

title: Handle Generated Text and Final Usage Separately
prompt: A streaming-capable model is called with Bedrock ConverseStream, and each generated portion of the response is displayed as it becomes available. Usage is recorded after the response. Tool calls are not used. Which two event-handling steps should be implemented?

choices.text: Treat the response text and all usage as final as soon as messageStart is received.
choices.explanation: The start of a stream does not indicate that generation has finished or that usage is final.

choices.text: Apply the text delta from contentBlockDelta to the corresponding block and display it to the user incrementally.
choices.explanation: Received portions can be displayed before the complete response is finished.

choices.text: Each time contentBlockStop is received, resend the same prompt to Converse to retrieve the text.
choices.explanation: The stream already provides deltas. Repeating inference does not guarantee the same response and adds processing.

choices.text: Read usage from a metadata event in the stream and record the generation's usage.
choices.explanation: Usage is provided in a separate event from the text deltas.

choices.text: Use the number of bytes received in HTTP chunks directly as the model's output token count.
choices.explanation: The size of the network representation does not match the model's token count.

source.label: Bedrock ConverseStream API

learning.reason: Process display text separately from events that report stream completion and usage.
learning.concept: A network chunk and a model token are different units.

title: Apply Additional Implementation Guidance Only to Matching Files
prompt: In Kiro, you want the implementation guide for the orders API to be included automatically only when working with files under services/orders/. Use the existing always-on guidance for rules that apply across the project, and do not load the additional guide when editing unrelated screens. How should you configure the orders guide?

choices.text: Set the additional guide to always and instruct users to ignore it when editing other areas.
choices.explanation: Because it is always included, this does not meet the requirement to limit its application automatically by file scope.

choices.text: Set the additional guide to manual and assume it will be selected automatically when a matching file is opened.
choices.explanation: manual means the guide is specified when needed; it is not automatically applied based on file conditions.

choices.text: Set the orders steering file to fileMatch and define a fileMatchPattern that matches the orders directory.
choices.explanation: The guide is included only when a matching file is being worked on.

choices.text: Set all shared guidance to manual and move the orders guide outside the repository.
choices.explanation: This meets neither the requirement to keep shared rules always on nor the requirement to apply the additional guide automatically to orders files.

source.label: KiroのSteeringと適用範囲

learning.reason: Represent the paths that need the additional rules with a path-based condition.
learning.concept: Guidance that is always needed and guidance needed only for a particular directory can use different application conditions.

title: Only Cryptographic Operations Immediately After Grant Creation Are Denied
prompt: Immediately after creating a KMS grant scoped to a role used by a processing job, GenerateDataKey using that same role is denied. It succeeds after a short wait. Which approach lets the job use the grant as soon as CreateGrant succeeds, without adding permanent permissions?

choices.text: Put the GrantId returned by CreateGrant in the GrantTokens for GenerateDataKey.
choices.explanation: GrantId and GrantToken are different values.

choices.text: Pass the GrantToken returned by CreateGrant in the job's first relevant KMS request.
choices.explanation: This lets the request use the new grant without waiting for its propagation through eventual consistency.

choices.text: Register the KMS key in an application environment variable and use it as a local key until propagation completes.
choices.explanation: A KMS key ARN is an identifier, not the value of an encryption key.

choices.text: Put the grant creation time in the EncryptionContext for GenerateDataKey.
choices.explanation: The encryption context does not prove or compensate for propagation of a new grant.

source.label: KMSのグラントとトークン

learning.reason: To use a new grant immediately, use the returned token, not the grant ID.
learning.concept: Distinguish a grant's identifier from the mechanism for referring to a new grant temporarily.

title: Allow Decryption with a Replica Key in the Standby Region
prompt: An application decrypts data in a standby Region that was encrypted using a related multi-Region key in AWS KMS. The replica key has been created, but the application role in the standby Region has no authorization on the replica. Keeping the ciphertext, where should you configure access?

choices.text: Update only the primary key policy and wait for it to synchronize automatically to the standby Region.
choices.explanation: Key policies are managed per Region, even for related keys.

choices.text: Create an unrelated single-Region key in the standby Region and use it to decrypt the existing ciphertext as is.
choices.explanation: An unrelated key cannot decrypt the same ciphertext.

choices.text: Allow the target role to use Decrypt with the replica key in the standby Region, and decrypt with KMS in that Region.
choices.explanation: The related keys share key material, but authorization is still required for the replica key that is actually used.

choices.text: Give the primary and replica keys the same alias so IAM and key policy permissions are unnecessary.
choices.explanation: An alias is a name; it does not grant permission to perform key operations.

source.label: AWS KMSのマルチリージョンキー

learning.reason: Consider shared cryptographic properties separately from authorization managed in each Region.
learning.concept: Key policies, grants, tags, and other settings are not automatically identical across related keys.

title: Sign an Artifact Without Giving Verifiers the Private Key
prompt: The publisher signs a configuration file for distribution. Consumers verify the signature without connecting to the cloud, but only the internal publishing system can generate signatures. The publisher does not export the private key from KMS. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Use an asymmetric KMS key with the SIGN_VERIFY key usage, call KMS Sign, and have consumers verify with the retrieved public key and the corresponding algorithm.
choices.explanation: The private key remains in KMS, while the public key can be used to verify the signature.

choices.text: Encrypt the file with a symmetric KMS key and distribute the ARN of the same key to consumers.
choices.explanation: The key ARN cannot be used for offline verification, and encryption alone is not signature verification with a public key.

choices.text: Generate a MAC with a KMS HMAC key and retrieve and distribute the HMAC key's public key.
choices.explanation: HMAC is symmetric; it has no public key for verification.

choices.text: Call KMS Sign with an asymmetric KMS key that has the ENCRYPT_DECRYPT key usage.
choices.explanation: A KMS key cannot perform signing operations unless its key usage is for signing.

source.label: KMSのキー仕様と用途

learning.reason: Separating the signing and verification roles requires letting consumers verify with a public key without giving them signing authority.
learning.concept: The permitted operations depend on the key usage selected when an asymmetric KMS key is created.

title: Restricting an Application Access Point to One VPC
prompt: You want to keep sharing the S3 bucket itself while making an access point dedicated to one application usable only from a specific VPC. The bucket delegation and VPC endpoint are already configured. What should you select when configuring the new access point?

choices.text: Set the network origin to Internet and include the VPC ID in the access point name.
choices.explanation: A resource name does not restrict the network origin.

choices.text: Configure only S3 Block Public Access on the access point.
choices.explanation: Blocking public access alone does not restrict permitted private requests to a specific VPC.

choices.text: Select VPC as the network origin and specify its VPC ID.
choices.explanation: This limits requests through the access point to those originating from the specified VPC.

choices.text: Only allow roles in the same account in the access point policy.
choices.explanation: Restricting the principal does not ensure that the same role is used from within that VPC.

source.label: VPCに制限したS3アクセスポイント

learning.reason: Restrict who is allowed to use the access point separately from which network can be used.
learning.concept: A VPC restriction applies to requests made through the access point.

sourceLabel: S3 Access Points Restricted to a VPC

title: Avoiding Policy Updates Whenever an Account Joins
prompt: You want to allow read access to an S3 bucket containing internal artifacts only from authorized roles in the same AWS Organizations organization. When a new account joins the organization, you should not have to add its account ID individually if its roles are authorized. This bucket policy is the only policy granting access to other accounts. Which condition should you use?

choices.text: Specify the organization ID for aws:PrincipalAccount.
choices.explanation: This condition compares account IDs. Organization IDs are handled by a different condition key.

choices.text: Add an aws:PrincipalOrgID match condition to the bucket policy granting read access, and authorize the operation for the calling role as well.
choices.explanation: This groups callers by organization membership, while also accounting for the cross-account permission required on the calling role.

choices.text: Check only that aws:RequestedRegion matches a Region used by the company.
choices.explanation: Using the same Region does not establish that the caller belongs to the organization.

choices.text: List every account to allow and update the bucket policy whenever an account joins.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid manually adding individual accounts.

source.label: IAM条件キー aws:PrincipalOrgID

learning.reason: Use organization membership as a resource-side allow condition instead of maintaining a list of accounts.
learning.concept: Checking organization membership does not replace granting each role the permissions it needs.

title: Assigning Different AWS Permissions to Pods on the Same Node
prompt: An EKS cluster uses the EKS Pod Identity Agent. A read-only Pod and a write-enabled Pod run on the same node. You want to avoid adding permissions to the node role or using long-term keys in environment variables, and you want to use the default credentials provider chain in a compatible SDK. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Add write permissions to the node IAM role and assume that permissions are separated by container name.
choices.explanation: The node role itself does not automatically split permissions by container name.

choices.text: Share one Kubernetes service account and attach the same Pod Identity role to both Pods.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the goal of using different policies for the two Pods.

choices.text: Put two IAM access keys in Kubernetes Secrets and provide them separately through environment variables.
choices.explanation: This distributes long-term keys instead of obtaining temporary credentials through the SDK provider chain.

choices.text: Assign a separate service account to each workload and create Pod Identity associations with the appropriate IAM roles, including the cluster and namespace.
choices.explanation: Each Pod can obtain temporary credentials for the role associated with its service account.

source.label: EKS Pod Identityの仕組み

learning.reason: Assign AWS permissions per workload even when the workloads share compute resources.
learning.concept: The association among the cluster, namespace, and service account determines the scope of the role provided to a Pod.

title: Restricting the Tables Accessible Through One Network Path
prompt: You want to limit operations to approved tables only for traffic that passes through an application's dedicated VPC DynamoDB gateway endpoint. Some application roles also use other tables in a separate environment, and those permissions must remain. Which configuration does not grant roles additional permissions through the endpoint itself?

choices.text: Change the VPC routes so each DynamoDB table ARN is sent through a different route.
choices.explanation: Route tables select paths based on IP prefixes; they do not authorize DynamoDB resources.

choices.text: Restrict the endpoint policy to the required operations and approved tables, while retaining the caller's IAM permissions.
choices.explanation: This adds constraints to requests made through the endpoint. The endpoint policy does not, by itself, authorize AWS operations.

choices.text: Remove all permissions for tables in the separate environment from the application roles' IAM policies.
choices.explanation: This does not limit only the network path and also removes permissions needed in the separate environment.

choices.text: Specify the table resource ARN in the security group's allow rules.
choices.explanation: Network controls do not authorize DynamoDB actions or table ARNs.

source.label: VPCエンドポイントポリシー

learning.reason: Set an upper bound on the operations accepted over that path separately from the caller's permissions.
learning.concept: Both the endpoint restriction and the access permissions evaluated by the service must be satisfied.

title: Allowing a function URL, but not direct invocation, for cross-account processing
prompt: A Lambda function URL created in 2026 uses AWS_IAM authentication and must be accessible to a specific role in another account. Access must be limited to the URL; the same role must not be allowed to call the direct Invoke API. Which two settings are required?

choices.text: Set the authentication type to NONE and manage cross-account access only through IAM.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to restrict access to the specified authenticated role.

choices.text: Allow InvokeFunctionUrl and InvokeFunction in the calling role's identity-based policy.
choices.explanation: For a cross-account caller, permissions are required on both the function-owning side and the calling side.

choices.text: Grant InvokeFunctionUrl to the function's execution role.
choices.explanation: What the function can do while running is separate from whether an external role can access the function.

choices.text: Allow both actions for the role in the function's resource-based policy, and add the InvokedViaFunctionUrl condition to the InvokeFunction permission.
choices.explanation: This provides the two permissions required for a newly created URL while preventing the InvokeFunction permission from being used for direct invocation.

choices.text: Allow only InvokeFunctionUrl in the function's resource policy; that is treated as permission for both actions.
choices.explanation: A newly created URL requires InvokeFunctionUrl and InvokeFunction; InvokeFunctionUrl alone is insufficient.

source.label: Lambda関数URLの認証とアクセス制御

learning.reason: For cross-account invocation, check permissions on both the principal and the resource.
learning.concept: Permissions can distinguish invocations through the URL from direct function invocations.

sourceLabel: Lambda Function URL authentication and access control

title: Testing new connection credentials before promoting them to the current version
prompt: A custom Secrets Manager rotation has stored new database credentials as AWSPENDING and updated the database configuration. Before switching the current version read by the application to the new value, what should the rotation function do?

choices.text: Call finishSecret to move AWSCURRENT immediately, then wait for users to report failures.
choices.explanation: A connection test failure would affect users, so this would not verify the credentials before promotion.

choices.text: Connect using the AWSPREVIOUS credentials and assume AWSPENDING will also work if that succeeds.
choices.explanation: Testing the previous version does not validate the new credentials.

choices.text: Use the AWSPENDING credentials with testSecret to verify the connection, then move AWSCURRENT with finishSecret after the test succeeds.
choices.explanation: Test the candidate value that will be promoted, then advance the label after it succeeds.

choices.text: Check only the version ID returned by SetSecretValue and treat the database connection as successful.
choices.explanation: A successful storage API call does not show that the stored value works with the database.

source.label: Secrets Managerのローテーション手順

learning.reason: After storing new credentials as a secret value, verify that they also work in the target system.
learning.concept: During rotation, staging labels distinguish the candidate from the current version read by the application.

title: Attaching a viewer certificate from another Region to delivery from a domestic origin
prompt: You use CloudFront with a custom domain and an ALB in the Tokyo Region as the origin. HTTPS to the ALB is already working, but you cannot select in CloudFront the ACM certificate requested in Tokyo for use with viewers. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Specify the ALB certificate ARN as the CloudFront viewer certificate.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the Region requirement for an ACM viewer certificate used with CloudFront.

choices.text: Pin CloudFront edge caching to the Tokyo Region before configuring the certificate.
choices.explanation: The origin and cache locations do not change the ACM Region requirement for a viewer certificate.

choices.text: Provision an ACM certificate in us-east-1 that matches the viewer-facing custom domain, and associate it with CloudFront.
choices.explanation: An ACM certificate used for HTTPS between CloudFront and viewers must be provisioned in us-east-1.

choices.text: Remove the origin HTTPS configuration and wait for the Tokyo certificate to become selectable for viewers only.
choices.explanation: Changing communication with the origin does not change the Region requirement for a viewer certificate.

source.label: CloudFrontの証明書要件

learning.reason: Manage certificates separately for the viewer-to-distribution connection and the distribution-to-origin connection.
learning.concept: The ACM Region for a certificate that CloudFront presents to viewers is independent of the origin's Region.

title: A long session is rejected by the second AssumeRole call
prompt: A developer uses temporary credentials obtained from an initial AssumeRole call to call AssumeRole for another role. The second role has MaxSessionDuration set to more than three hours, but the call fails when DurationSeconds is set to 7,200. In a design that assumes roles in sequence, which assessment is correct?

choices.text: For the second role in a role chain, set DurationSeconds to no more than 3,600 seconds, and design credential acquisition for long-running work to meet the requirements.
choices.explanation: When one assumed role assumes another role, the one-hour limit applies even if the target role has a longer maximum session duration.

choices.text: Increase MaxSessionDuration for the second role; that will ensure the same request succeeds.
choices.explanation: The target role's longer maximum does not override the role-chaining limit.

choices.text: Use the same RoleSessionName as for the first role to carry over and extend the session.
choices.explanation: The name identifies the session; it does not change the session-duration limit.

choices.text: Attach an additional session policy to the second role to allow a longer DurationSeconds value.
choices.explanation: A session policy can narrow permissions, but it cannot extend the duration limit.

source.label: STS AssumeRoleのロールチェーン

learning.reason: Check how the current credentials were issued when determining the session duration that can be requested.
learning.concept: The limit imposed by the role-assumption path can apply in addition to the configured maximum session duration.

title: Limit excessive requests before they reach the backend
prompt: For a regional API Gateway REST API, you want to limit excessive requests from each source independently of user authentication. Keep the existing routes and authentication, apply the control only to the production stage, and observe the match count while testing it safely. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Use the Lambda function's Reserved Concurrency to determine the request count for each source.
choices.explanation: This setting limits concurrency for the function as a whole; it does not evaluate each client at the gateway.

choices.text: Use only REST API IAM permissions to count requests from each source over a fixed period.
choices.explanation: IAM policies authorize requests, but they do not aggregate request counts by IP address.

choices.text: Associate a regional AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule to the production stage, verify it with Count, and then switch to Block.
choices.explanation: Requests to the specified stage are evaluated upstream, and you can review the match count before switching to blocking.

choices.text: Associate a web ACL with the ALB behind API Gateway, assuming that this also evaluates requests before they are integrated with the API.
choices.explanation: A control attached only downstream does not evaluate requests before they are sent to the API Gateway integration.

source.label: AWS WAFによるAPI Gateway REST APIの保護

learning.reason: Configure evaluation at the processing boundary where requests must be blocked.
learning.concept: Rate limiting and principal authorization serve different purposes; Count lets you assess a rule's impact first.

sourceLabel: Protecting an API Gateway REST API with AWS WAF

title: Detect IAM policy errors before deployment
prompt: A CI pipeline checks the JSON for an IAM identity policy. You want AWS check results that report invalid action names and usage patterns that warrant attention, without attaching the policy to an actual role. Which operation should you include?

choices.text: Use IAM GetPolicyVersion to analyze undeployed JSON and retrieve a list of warnings.
choices.explanation: GetPolicyVersion reads an existing policy version; it does not validate undeployed content.

choices.text: Pass the document and the IDENTITY_POLICY type to IAM Access Analyzer ValidatePolicy, then process the returned findings.
choices.explanation: This provides syntax and AWS best-practice check results without deploying the document.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to confirm a successful AttachRolePolicy call and obtain all syntax and recommendation findings from that event.
choices.explanation: This requires attaching the policy, and an audit event is not a list of validation findings.

choices.text: Set a temporary permissions boundary and call the API; if the call succeeds, treat the entire document as meeting all recommendations.
choices.explanation: A single execution result does not validate unused statements or the document's overall construction.

source.label: IAM Access Analyzerのポリシー検証

learning.reason: Validate the document before deployment; check permissions in the actual environment separately.
learning.concept: Syntax and recommendation checks do not prove that every real request will be allowed.

title: Record audited object retrievals
prompt: The existing CloudTrail setup records bucket configuration changes, but you cannot determine who called GetObject on objects under S3 prefix private/reports/. Do not additionally collect data events for objects outside that scope or any write events. What should you configure?

choices.text: Change the trail's management events to read-only and assume that S3 GetObject events will be included.
choices.explanation: GetObject on an object is a data event, not a management event.

choices.text: Change the lifecycle policy of the bucket that stores the trail logs to generate object-read events.
choices.explanation: Changing log retention does not change which events the trail collects.

choices.text: Collect all S3 data events and filter out unwanted events only when displaying the results.
choices.explanation: This would capture the needed retrieval history, but it does not meet the requirement to avoid collecting out-of-scope events.

choices.text: Enable S3 object data events and use advanced event selectors to restrict them to the target object ARN prefix and GetObject.
choices.explanation: You can select the resource type, key scope, and API operation separately.

source.label: CloudTrailのデータイベント記録

learning.reason: Treat service configuration changes and operations that access actual data as different event types.
learning.concept: Narrowing the resource scope at collection time controls both the volume of recorded events and the investigation scope.

title: Reject updates without trusted signatures before deployment
prompt: A ZIP-based Lambda function is updated in production. You want only artifacts signed with an approved signing profile to be deployed to the function. A failed signature check must stop the actual deployment, not merely be logged. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Associate a code-signing configuration that allows the approved AWS Signer profile with the function, and set it to Enforce.
choices.explanation: With this configuration, a failed signature validation can block deployment of the code package.

choices.text: Use the same signing configuration with Warn and assume that a deployment with a warning will automatically fail.
choices.explanation: Warn records the issue but does not stop deployment solely because the signature check failed.

choices.text: Update the Lambda execution role's trust policy to include the deployer's name instead of the signing profile.
choices.explanation: Assuming an execution role at runtime does not verify the integrity of the package being deployed.

choices.text: Pass the signature file to the function as an environment variable after deployment and treat the already-deployed package as having been verified beforehand.
choices.explanation: A post-deployment step does not prevent unapproved code from being deployed in the first place.

source.label: Lambdaコード署名

learning.reason: Verify the signature of the artifact being deployed before relying on any custom checks at application runtime.
learning.concept: A setting that records warnings is different from one that rejects updates with invalid signatures.

title: Include newly disclosed vulnerabilities without repushing
prompt: An ECR repository contains container images used in production, and only scan on push is enabled. When new vulnerabilities are disclosed, you want to keep evaluating the OS and programming-language packages in the same images throughout the monitoring period without repushing them. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Keep scan on push enabled for basic scanning.
choices.explanation: Without another push, this setting does not provide continuous evaluation, and its coverage is different.

choices.text: Make ECR tags immutable so that images cannot contain newly discovered vulnerabilities.
choices.explanation: Preventing tag overwrites stops content changes; it does not evaluate newly identified issues.

choices.text: Enable enhanced continuous scanning for the target repository and set the coverage period in Amazon Inspector.
choices.explanation: Images under monitoring are reevaluated as new vulnerability information becomes available. OS packages and supported language packages are covered.

choices.text: Enable an image lifecycle policy and scan when an image reaches its expiration date.
choices.explanation: A retention setting does not trigger reevaluation when the vulnerability database changes.

source.label: ECRの拡張スキャン

learning.reason: Track existing artifacts for vulnerabilities discovered after publication, in addition to checking them at publication time.
learning.concept: Scan frequency, package coverage, and the rescan period are separate aspects to consider.

title: Require a guardrail for inference through permissions
prompt: An IAM role for an internal application calls a supported Bedrock model-inference API. You do not want to allow inference unless an approved guardrail is specified, even if the client changes. Which control should you use in the application's role IAM policy?

choices.text: Allow guardrail creation only, and do not add a condition to the InvokeModel permission.
choices.explanation: Permission to create a guardrail is separate from requiring its use in an inference request.

choices.text: Use bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier as a condition on the inference action, and deny requests that do not specify the required guardrail.
choices.explanation: Explicitly denying requests that fail the condition enforces the required guardrail for permitted inference.

choices.text: Append the guardrail name to the model name and call Bedrock with that string.
choices.explanation: A model identifier does not represent a guardrail setting and does not enforce it through IAM.

choices.text: Enable inference logging and notify the team afterward when a request has no guardrail.
choices.explanation: This can detect such requests, but it does not meet the requirement to reject them before inference runs.

source.label: Bedrock推論で指定ガードレールを強制

learning.reason: Include the required control in inference permissions instead of relying only on client-side configuration.
learning.concept: Detecting requests through logs and rejecting them in advance through a policy serve different purposes.

sourceLabel: Enforce a specified guardrail for Bedrock inference

title: Allow routine updates while blocking database replacement
prompt: A database managed with CloudFormation should allow frequent capacity-setting changes, but updates that require physical resource replacement must be limited to a separate, approved procedure. Other resources should continue to update as before. Which setting blocks replacement during a normal stack update?

choices.text: Use a stack policy to deny Update:Replace for the target logical ID and allow other required updates.
choices.explanation: This can deny physical replacement of the target while preserving permitted routine updates and updates to other resources.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy to Retain to reject updates that replace the original database.
choices.explanation: This controls retention of the physical resource; it does not block an ordinary replacement request.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Snapshot.
choices.explanation: This changes what happens to the old resource after replacement, but does not prohibit replacement with a new physical resource.

choices.text: Enable termination protection for the entire stack.
choices.explanation: Termination protection prevents stack deletion; it does not restrict resource replacement during a stack update.

source.label: CloudFormationのスタックポリシー

learning.reason: Allow only the update types needed for the target logical ID.
learning.concept: Controlling whether a resource can be replaced and deciding how to retain the old resource are separate settings.

title: Create a production database without putting its password in the template
prompt: You are creating an RDS DB instance for the first time with CloudFormation. The specified Secrets Manager secret contains the credentials to use, and the CloudFormation execution role can read it. How can you use the current version at creation time without putting plaintext in the source or in a template parameter's default value?

choices.text: Put the current value in the parameter's Default and enable NoEcho.
choices.explanation: Masking the displayed value does not meet the requirement to keep plaintext out of the source.

choices.text: Convert the current value to Base64 and embed it in a parameter.
choices.explanation: Base64 is reversible and does not eliminate the need to distribute the secret value.

choices.text: Use a versionless dynamic reference to the required JSON key in the target secret for the database credential property.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation can resolve the current value from Secrets Manager during the operation without embedding plaintext in the template.

choices.text: Set the database password to the secret ARN string itself.
choices.explanation: For that property to resolve a Secrets Manager reference, use the dynamic-reference syntax processed by CloudFormation.

source.label: CloudFormationのSecrets Manager動的参照

learning.reason: Keep the secret value out of the source and resolve it when operating on the target resource.
learning.concept: A versionless reference selects the current version, but rotation later is not guaranteed to update an existing resource automatically.

title: Phase in a change to a shared export in use
prompt: Multiple stacks in the same account and Region reference the network stack’s NetSubnet output with Fn::ImportValue. The workload is moving to a new subnet, but the old reference must remain usable until the existing consumer stacks have switched over. How should the change be made?

choices.text: Overwrite the original export value directly, then update each consumer stack in sequence.
choices.explanation: An export value cannot be changed while other stacks import it.

choices.text: Export the new value under a new name, migrate the consumer stacks one by one, and remove the old output only after no imports remain.
choices.explanation: This keeps the output available while dependencies remain and lets consumers switch to the new reference.

choices.text: Delete the original output first and assume consumer stacks will retain the old value automatically.
choices.explanation: An export cannot be deleted while imports remain.

choices.text: Export the same name in another Region in place of the old output.
choices.explanation: Fn::ImportValue references are limited to the same account and Region; they do not automatically move to an export in another Region.

source.label: CloudFormation Fn::ImportValue

learning.reason: Keep the identifier used by dependent stacks available while consumers migrate first.
learning.concept: When an export becomes a shared interface, its name and value cannot be changed freely.

title: Prepare a destination for CDK assets in a new Region
prompt: A CDK app contains local ZIP and container image assets. Synthesis succeeds, but the first deployment to a new account and Region lacks the AWS resources required for those assets. Deployment works in the existing development environment. What is the appropriate action?

choices.text: Run cdk synth again in the existing development Region.
choices.explanation: Synthesis creates template and asset information, but it does not set up the infrastructure in the new deployment environment.

choices.text: Remove the asset definitions from the CDK source and wait for the files to move to production automatically.
choices.explanation: Without specifying assets to deploy, the required artifacts are not associated with the deployment.

choices.text: Assume the bootstrapped environment in the same AWS account is used automatically in every Region.
choices.explanation: A CDK deployment environment is an account and Region pair, and the required resources must be available in that environment.

choices.text: Run cdk bootstrap for the target account and Region, then deploy after the asset infrastructure is in place.
choices.explanation: This prepares deployment resources in the target environment, such as an asset bucket, a repository, and related roles.

source.label: AWS CDKブートストラップ

learning.reason: Synthesis of source code and initial setup of the target environment are separate steps.
learning.concept: Deployments containing files or images need a destination in each environment.

title: Apply a shared validation to nested resources
prompt: A CDK stack uses several team-owned Constructs. A resource that violates a standard must be checked during synthesis and reported as a validation error, regardless of which Construct contains it. How can this be implemented without modifying each Construct individually?

choices.text: Add one new output to the App and automatically inspect each Construct’s children from the output value.
choices.explanation: Stack outputs publish values; they do not traverse child nodes to validate a standard.

choices.text: Register a CDK Aspect on the target scope, then use visit to inspect the target resource types and properties and add errors.
choices.explanation: An Aspect can traverse the construct tree in that scope and apply the same check to child resources.

choices.text: Add CloudWatch alarms for each AWS service after deployment and treat configuration errors as synthesis errors.
choices.explanation: Runtime notifications do not fail synthesis before deployment.

choices.text: Compare custom snapshots that inspect only Construct names.
choices.explanation: Names alone cannot validate the actual configuration values of the resources covered by the standard.

source.label: AWS CDKのAspects

learning.reason: Attach the check to the scope being inspected instead of duplicating the standard in every resource-creation path.
learning.concept: Shared changes or validation can run at synthesis time against the Construct tree.

title: Check SAM template properties before deployment
prompt: A SAM template is readable as YAML, but errors in resource property types or usage constraints cause deployment to fail. The goal is to add CloudFormation Linter checks to CI without a new deployment to the cloud. Which command meets this goal?

choices.text: Run sam build alone and treat a successful dependency build as validation of all properties.
choices.explanation: Building artifacts is not a CloudFormation Linter check of the template.

choices.text: Use sam local invoke to test an arbitrary function and assume settings for resources the function did not invoke are also valid.
choices.explanation: Running a function does not validate all resource properties in the template.

choices.text: Run sam validate --lint and handle the CloudFormation Linter results in CI.
choices.explanation: The SAM CLI can enable cfn-lint to validate template structure and resource properties.

choices.text: Run sam deploy in production and use the first update failure as the validation result.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for a static pre-deployment check and may update the live environment.

source.label: SAMテンプレートのcfn-lint検査

learning.reason: Valid syntax alone does not guarantee valid resource configuration.
learning.concept: The CLI lint option can also check resource definitions before deployment.

title: Reuse a Shared Serverless Configuration as a Nested Application
prompt: Several SAM applications deploy the same audit queue and function configuration as part of their respective stacks. You want to share the template as a file and pass values such as the environment name from each parent application. How can you avoid duplicating the template definition?

choices.text: Declare an AWS::Serverless::Application in each parent that points to the shared template, and pass environment-specific values through Parameters.
choices.explanation: A nested SAM application reuses the shared definition, and each parent can provide its own values.

choices.text: Pass only the ZIP file for the function created by the shared application to each parent, and assume the queue and event integration are reused as well.
choices.explanation: Sharing only the code artifact does not share the audit queue or its related configuration.

choices.text: Copy the shared template into each parent and assume that future changes will sync automatically as long as the parameter names match.
choices.explanation: Resource definitions copied into each parent do not sync automatically.

choices.text: Retrieve a single Output from the shared application, define it directly as a Parameter in each parent, and create the shared resources in each parent as well.
choices.explanation: Using an output value alone does not deploy the shared template as part of each parent.

source.label: SAM AWS::Serverless::Application

learning.reason: Separate the shared configuration definition from the caller that supplies environment-specific values.
learning.concept: You can nest an application that defines multiple resources, independently of sharing code.

title: Python Cannot Find a Dependency Even After a Layer Is Attached
prompt: You added a ZIP layer to Lambda containing dependencies built for the same Python version and Linux environment. The ZIP contains only the dependency packages at its root, and the standard Python import mechanism cannot find them. How should you change the layer ZIP without adding a custom search path to the function code?

choices.text: Create a directory named dependencies/ at the ZIP root and move the packages into it.
choices.explanation: A directory with an arbitrary name is not part of the runtime's default layer search path.

choices.text: Create a python/ directory at the ZIP root and put Python dependencies compatible with the target runtime under it.
choices.explanation: After extraction, the Python runtime treats /opt/python as a standard dependency location.

choices.text: Put the ZIP inside another ZIP and wait for Lambda to extract the inner archive automatically.
choices.explanation: Standard layer resolution does not extract nested archives and turn them into Python packages.

choices.text: Change the function handler name in the environment variables to the name of the dependency package directory.
choices.explanation: The handler setting specifies the function's entry point; it does not change where libraries are located for import.

source.label: Python Lambdaレイヤーの構成

learning.reason: Even when the build artifact is compatible, its contents must be placed in a path searched by the layer runtime.
learning.concept: Structure a layer ZIP according to its extraction destination and the runtime's conventions.

title: Reuse a Dependency Cache Across Build Hosts
prompt: CodeBuild builds start on different hosts. You want to reuse downloaded dependencies but avoid using a stale dependency cache when the lockfile changes. Which CodeBuild cache configuration should you use?

choices.text: Use only a local cache and assume every build in the project runs on the same host.
choices.explanation: A local cache depends on the state of the build host and does not guarantee reuse across hosts.

choices.text: Use an S3 cache and always save it under the same fixed key.
choices.explanation: This can work across hosts, but the key does not change when the lockfile changes.

choices.text: Use an S3 cache and include the lockfile hash in the cache key in the buildspec.
choices.explanation: Different hosts can use the same key, and a changed lockfile results in a different cache.

choices.text: Use only the CodeBuild run ID as the cache key.
choices.explanation: Each run gets a different key, so it cannot reuse a cache from an earlier run even when the lockfile is unchanged.

source.label: CodeBuildのS3キャッシュ

learning.reason: The storage location determines where reuse can occur, while the key determines which dependency versions can be reused.
learning.concept: When a cache key is tied only to inputs that have not changed, it can be reused on a later run.

title: Connect to Both a Private Database and Public Packages
prompt: You connected CodeBuild to a VPC to run integration tests against RDS in the VPC. The build connects to RDS and also accesses public packages over HTTPS. Artifacts use the existing route. The build ENI cannot be assigned a public IP address. How should you configure this setup?

choices.text: Connect to a public subnet that routes directly to an internet gateway so that CodeBuild is assigned a public IP address.
choices.explanation: This does not assign a public IP address to the network interface created by CodeBuild.

choices.text: Choose private subnets with outbound internet access through a NAT gateway, and also allow the build security group to communicate with RDS.
choices.explanation: This establishes separate paths for access to RDS within the VPC and outbound access to public packages.

choices.text: Add only an S3 gateway endpoint and use it to reach any public HTTPS domain that hosts packages.
choices.explanation: An S3 endpoint does not provide an internet route to arbitrary public package servers.

choices.text: Remove the VPC configuration from the build project so it can reach the private RDS database through the same route.
choices.explanation: This removes the path to the database in the private VPC.

source.label: CodeBuildのVPC接続

learning.reason: Provide explicit connectivity to internal services and an outbound route for public services.
learning.concept: Selecting a public subnet alone does not guarantee that a public address will be assigned to a deployed ENI.

title: Source Artifacts with Git History Available During Builds
prompt: A CodePipeline Git connection is in use. Downstream CodeBuild needs to inspect Git history as well as the working tree to run differential tests. How can the existing connection be used to make history available to the downstream build instead of extracting flat source files to S3?

choices.text: Use the usual CODE_ZIP and assume that extracting the ZIP also includes the .git history.
choices.explanation: Packaging source files as a ZIP does not provide the metadata for a full Git repository.

choices.text: Change only the artifact output format in CodeBuild from ZIP to another format.
choices.explanation: The output format does not change whether Git history can be obtained from the upstream source.

choices.text: Pass only the source action's CommitId variable and assume that the repository history containing that commit will be made available to the build.
choices.explanation: Passing a commit ID does not bring the history containing that commit into the downstream build.

choices.text: Select CODEBUILD_CLONE_REF for the connection source output and receive that reference in a CodeBuild action that can use the connection.
choices.explanation: This passes CodeBuild a reference it can use to obtain a full Git clone.

source.label: CodePipelineの接続ソースとGitクローン

learning.reason: Choose an artifact format based on whether the build needs only source contents or Git history as well.
learning.concept: The downstream action must support clone references and be authorized to use the connection.

sourceLabel: CodePipeline connection sources and Git clones

title: Make a Release from Before Replication Rules Available
prompt: Cross-Region replication has been configured in ECR. The latest image pushed after configuration reached the destination, but a rollback image published before configuration is missing there. How can you place the earlier version that matches the current rules in the destination without republishing its existing tag?

choices.text: Start ECR replication backfill for the destination Region and registry.
choices.explanation: This can replicate existing images that match the current rules to the existing destination, even though they were not included in normal replication.

choices.text: Disable tag immutability at the destination so that all historical images are replicated.
choices.explanation: Changing tag settings does not trigger a process to replicate images published before configuration.

choices.text: Redeploy the destination ECS service first so that the missing image is replicated automatically from the source.
choices.explanation: An ECS deployment does not backfill images missing from the specified destination repository.

choices.text: Extend the retention period in the lifecycle policy so that images from before configuration are also sent to the destination.
choices.explanation: The scope of a retention rule and when replication is initiated are separate matters.

source.label: ECRレプリケーションバックフィル

learning.reason: Check ongoing synchronization separately from the migration of assets that existed before operations began.
learning.concept: The arrival of new artifacts does not show that older rollback versions are available.

title: Keep Four Tasks Healthy While Replacing Them One at a Time
prompt: An ECS rolling deployment has a desiredCount of 4. Which setting keeps all 4 current healthy tasks while allowing at most 1 new task to be added first, so that an old task is replaced after the new task becomes healthy? The cluster has capacity for 1 additional task.

choices.text: minimumHealthyPercent=75, maximumPercent=100.
choices.explanation: This allows a temporary reduction in task count and does not allow a new task to be added first.

choices.text: minimumHealthyPercent=100, maximumPercent=125.
choices.explanation: This keeps at least 4 tasks healthy and allows up to 5 tasks to be running or starting at the same time.

choices.text: minimumHealthyPercent=100, maximumPercent=100.
choices.explanation: The maximum is 4 after keeping 4 tasks healthy, leaving no room to stop a healthy old task or start a new task first.

choices.text: minimumHealthyPercent=75, maximumPercent=150.
choices.explanation: This sets the minimum to 3 and the maximum to 6, which is a wider range than the required 4 to 5.

source.label: ECSローリングデプロイのタスク数

learning.reason: Set the minimum number of healthy running tasks and the maximum total number of tasks during an update separately.
learning.concept: With additional capacity, a newly launched task can become healthy before an old task is stopped.

title: Start the Application After Its Dependency Is Ready
prompt: An ECS task has an application container and a local proxy. Before the application starts, the proxy must be ready and pass its defined container health check. The proxy must remain running while the application runs. Which task definition should you use?

choices.text: Set the application's dependsOn condition to START.
choices.explanation: This waits for the container to start, but does not require its health check to pass.

choices.text: Set the dependency on the proxy to COMPLETE.
choices.explanation: This requires the container to exit, so it is unsuitable for a proxy needed while the application runs.

choices.text: Only increase the application's health check start period and leave the startup order unspecified.
choices.explanation: The grace period changes how the application's check results are treated, but does not make the application wait for its dependency to be ready.

choices.text: Set HEALTHY for the proxy in the application's dependsOn.
choices.explanation: The application starts after the dependency container's health check succeeds.

source.label: ECSコンテナの起動依存条件

learning.reason: A process having started is different from being ready for use.
learning.concept: The HEALTHY condition is checked at startup, so handling failures after startup must be considered separately.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Isolate latency hidden by the service-wide average
prompt: Structured logs in CloudWatch Logs contain a route and durationMs for each request. You want to use the existing logs to see the 95th percentile by route and in 5-minute intervals, and determine whether a rise in short-term latency is limited to certain routes. What should you aggregate?

choices.text: Calculate only avg(durationMs) for each route.
choices.explanation: An average does not show an increase in the upper tail of the distribution, and it does not separate different time periods.

choices.text: Use Logs Insights stats to calculate pct(durationMs, 95), grouped by route and bin(5m).
choices.explanation: This gives the 95th percentile of the logged durations for each route and time interval.

choices.text: Select the single row with the maximum durationMs and treat it as the 95th percentile for every route.
choices.explanation: The maximum is not the 95th percentile, and this provides no results for other routes or time periods.

choices.text: Aggregate count() by route and assume that routes with more log entries have a higher 95th percentile.
choices.explanation: The number of records does not reveal the distribution of individual request durations.

source.label: CloudWatch Logs Insights stats

learning.reason: Reflect the distribution and comparison units you want to observe directly in the aggregation.
learning.concept: Averages, counts, and percentiles describe different properties; choose the measure that matches the investigation.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Check how many items expiration processing actually deleted
prompt: After configuring TTL for data in DynamoDB, you want to monitor how many expired items are actually deleted each day. Do not count DeleteItem calls from the application or items that have expired but remain in the table. How should you use existing CloudWatch metrics?

choices.text: Check the Sum of TimeToLiveDeletedItemCount for the target TableName.
choices.explanation: This metric can be summed over a specified period to get the number of items DynamoDB deleted through TTL.

choices.text: Limit SuccessfulRequestLatency to DeleteItem and use its average as the number of deleted items.
choices.explanation: Successful API request latency is not the count of TTL deletions.

choices.text: Sum ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits and treat the entire amount as TTL deletions.
choices.explanation: This measures capacity consumed by TTL deletions and other writes; it does not represent the number of TTL-deleted items.

choices.text: Calculate TTL deletions alone from the day-over-day change in the table's ItemCount.
choices.explanation: New items and application deletions also affect the change.

source.label: DynamoDB CloudWatchメトリクス

learning.reason: Expiration and actual background deletion are separate events to observe.
learning.concept: When a metric exists for the specific operation you care about, do not estimate it from a table-wide difference.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Isolate a specific container's CPU usage from the service average
prompt: The average CPU utilization for an ECS service is normal, but requests are slow on some tasks. You know the ID of a problematic task and want to observe the CPU usage of its application and sidecar separately. Which method collects metrics at the required granularity in CloudWatch without changing the application code?

choices.text: Compare the ECS service's CPUUtilization using the same ServiceName and apportion the value between the application and sidecar.
choices.explanation: An aggregate at the service level cannot identify a specific container in the target task.

choices.text: Notify on ECS task stop events alone and treat those notifications as a CPU time series.
choices.explanation: Stop notifications do not collect CPU utilization for running containers.

choices.text: Enable Container Insights with enhanced observability on the cluster, then check ContainerCpuUtilization with dimensions that include TaskId and ContainerName.
choices.explanation: In addition to service-wide data, this lets you isolate resource utilization for each container in the target task.

choices.text: Add a fixed CPU value to the Fargate task definition and monitor it as actual usage.
choices.explanation: The CPU allocation in a task definition is not the CPU amount each container actually used.

source.label: ECSの拡張Container Insightsメトリクス

learning.reason: When service-level aggregation is insufficient, drill down to the task and container level.
learning.concept: Configured allocations and actual usage at a given time are different.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Reduce detailed application logs while retaining platform information
prompt: A supported Node.js Lambda function uses console.debug and console.error. You want to send only application logs at ERROR level or higher to CloudWatch Logs, while retaining the report that Lambda emits at INFO level. You will not change the code. Which two settings are required?

choices.text: Change the log format to JSON so that Lambda can apply its filter using the structured log level.
choices.explanation: Lambda log-level filtering requires a supported JSON log format.

choices.text: Shorten the log group retention period.
choices.explanation: This changes the retention period after writing; it does not stop DEBUG logs from being sent.

choices.text: Set ApplicationLogLevel to ERROR and SystemLogLevel to INFO.
choices.explanation: You can set different minimum levels for application and platform logs.

choices.text: Set both levels to ERROR.
choices.explanation: This would not retain the platform's INFO report.

choices.text: Exclude DEBUG in the Logs Insights search results.
choices.explanation: This changes what appears in search results, but does not reduce the amount sent to CloudWatch Logs.

source.label: Lambdaのログレベルフィルター

learning.reason: Decide which information to retain before ingestion, separately for each log source.
learning.concept: Application diagnostics and runtime platform logs can be managed at different levels.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Modeling Normal Load That Varies by Time of Day
prompt: The payment API normally handles high load during the day and low load at night. A request volume that is unremarkable during the day should be detected as anomalous if the same volume occurs at night. Which approach uses a history-based normal range without manually setting a fixed threshold for each time period?

choices.text: Set one fixed upper limit for all time periods and increase the number of evaluations above the threshold.
choices.explanation: Changing the number of evaluations does not provide different normal ranges for different times of day.

choices.text: Treat missing data as breaching and consider high values to be deviations from normal.
choices.explanation: How missing data is treated does not teach the system the normal range of observed values.

choices.text: Calculate the maximum value over the entire period each month and use only that value as the upper limit.
choices.explanation: This will not detect a nighttime load that is unusually high for night but remains below a past daytime peak.

choices.text: Use CloudWatch anomaly detection and alarm when the metric falls outside its periodic normal range.
choices.explanation: It creates a history-based band and compares the metric with upper or lower bounds that account for daily patterns.

source.label: CloudWatch異常検知

learning.reason: When the same value has a different meaning depending on the time, the baseline should reflect that variation.
learning.concept: A single historical maximum and a periodic expected range produce different boundaries.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Allow Time to Investigate After Moving to a DLQ
prompt: The source standard SQS queue retains messages for up to 4 days, and you want to be able to investigate them for at least 3 days after they are moved to a standard DLQ. Operationally, a message may be moved to the DLQ after spending nearly 4 days in the source queue. How should you set the DLQ retention period?

choices.text: Set it to 3 days. The message will always be retained for 3 days from the time it reaches the DLQ.
choices.explanation: In a standard queue, the original enqueue timestamp does not change, so a message that has already aged 3 days will not meet the desired period.

choices.text: Set it to the same 4 days as the source queue. Retain messages independently for the same number of days in both queues.
choices.explanation: The DLQ expiration is measured from the original enqueue timestamp, so a message moved after about 4 days will expire soon.

choices.text: Add the source queue's maximum age of 4 days to the 3-day investigation period, and configure the DLQ to retain messages for at least 7 days.
choices.explanation: This preserves the investigation period even when the expiration is measured from the original enqueue time.

choices.text: Use only the elapsed time reported by the DLQ's ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage as the retention period.
choices.explanation: That metric reports elapsed time after the move, but the standard queue's actual expiration is not recalculated from that point.

source.label: SQS DLQのメッセージ保持期間

learning.reason: Include the time spent before a message moves to a standard DLQ in the retention design.
learning.concept: The age shown for a message on a DLQ and the starting point the service uses for expiration are different.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: GET Fails Over, but POST Does Not
prompt: The CloudFront origin group is configured to fail over to the secondary origin when the primary returns 503. A GET test succeeded, but when a POST received a 503, the request was not sent to the secondary origin. Which statement correctly describes CloudFront's behavior?

choices.text: Add POST to the allowed HTTP methods, and CloudFront will perform the same failover for POST as it does for GET.
choices.explanation: Allowing POST to be sent to the origin is separate from method-specific failover behavior during an outage.

choices.text: CloudFront origin failover is limited to GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS. Design write recovery separately, such as in the application.
choices.explanation: Even when 503 is a failover condition, POST is not included in the methods covered by that failover.

choices.text: For any method, increasing the origin response timeout enables sending the request to the secondary origin.
choices.explanation: The timeout duration does not change which HTTP methods are eligible for failover.

choices.text: Add POST to the cache policy so a cache miss sends the request to the secondary origin.
choices.explanation: Changing the cache configuration does not make POST eligible for origin failover.

source.label: CloudFrontオリジンフェイルオーバー

learning.reason: Even with the same status code, recovery behavior can differ by HTTP method.
learning.concept: Do not equate automatic failover for read-oriented methods with retrying write operations.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Inspecting Express Workflow History After Execution
prompt: For a high-volume Express workflow, you need to find out how far it progressed after a failure. The application payload must not be sent to the monitoring destination, and you need to record state transitions for both successful and failed executions. Do not rely on saved Express execution history being retained automatically in the console. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Periodically call DescribeExecution for Express and retrieve the state history.
choices.explanation: This does not retrieve execution history for each Express state.

choices.text: Capture the StartExecution management event in CloudTrail and use it as the state history for each step.
choices.explanation: The workflow start record does not include the execution progress of internal states.

choices.text: Set the workflow's CloudWatch Logs level to ALL and disable logging of execution data.
choices.explanation: This records the necessary state events without logging the input and output payloads.

choices.text: Enable only the CloudWatch ExecutionsFailed metric.
choices.explanation: It shows the number of failures but not how far a specific execution progressed.

source.label: Step Functionsの実行履歴ログ

learning.reason: For services that must retain execution history, check the recording destination for each workflow type.
learning.concept: The event types to record and whether to include payloads can be configured separately.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Update instrumentation while keeping the trace backend
prompt: An application sends traces using the X-Ray SDK and daemon. You want to migrate its instrumentation to OpenTelemetry while keeping the existing X-Ray investigation view. You also want to verify during the migration that traces remain connected across existing services. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Keep the X-Ray SDK and change only the X-Ray daemon's log level.
choices.explanation: This does not migrate trace instrumentation and delivery to OpenTelemetry.

choices.text: Instrument the application with OpenTelemetry, use a collector or similar component that can send data to X-Ray, and verify that trace context propagates between services.
choices.explanation: You can migrate the instrumentation approach while continuing to use X-Ray as the trace backend.

choices.text: Convert X-Ray traces to ordinary text logs and rely only on CloudWatch Logs to preserve distributed trace correlation.
choices.explanation: Text logs alone cannot preserve trace delivery and the linking of distributed spans as they are.

choices.text: Set the same fixed trace ID in every service.
choices.explanation: This mixes separate requests and prevents tracking each request as an independent distributed trace.

source.label: X-Ray計装からOpenTelemetryへの移行

learning.reason: Distinguish instrumentation, context propagation, and the backend when planning a migration.
learning.concept: Even when you can update instrumentation without changing the backend, verify correlation across service boundaries.

sourceLabel: Migrating from X-Ray Instrumentation to OpenTelemetry

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Keep TLS validation working after certificate rotation
prompt: RDS is migrating its server certificate to a new CA. The application's database connections validate the certificate and hostname, but currently trust only the old CA. How should you prepare to keep connections working before and after the update without disabling validation?

choices.text: Before the update, distribute a trust bundle containing the new AWS CA to the application, then switch the RDS certificate and verify connections while both the old and new CAs can be trusted.
choices.explanation: Preparing the client to validate the new certificate chain first lets you maintain TLS validation during the migration.

choices.text: Disable validation in the application before updating RDS, then re-enable trust only for the old CA afterward.
choices.explanation: This does not maintain validation, and the old CA alone cannot validate the new certificate.

choices.text: Recreate the AWS SDK credentials and leave the database driver's trust bundle unchanged.
choices.explanation: IAM credentials are separate from whether the driver trusts the RDS server certificate.

choices.text: Switch the RDS certificate first, then add the new CA to the trust bundle after observing connection errors.
choices.explanation: Although connections may eventually work, this creates a period when new connections fail before the new CA is available.

source.label: RDSのSSL/TLS証明書の更新

learning.reason: Prepare the client's trust configuration before changing the server certificate.
learning.concept: Database authentication and validation of the destination's TLS certificate are independent mechanisms.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Distinguish TTL expiration from memory pressure when keys disappear
prompt: In node-based ElastiCache for Valkey, values disappear before their configured TTL. Load rises during periods when memory is near its limit. You need to distinguish normal expiration from keys being removed because the memory limit was reached. Which observations should you use?

choices.text: Count every decrease in CacheHits as an expiration.
choices.explanation: There are other reasons for a cache miss, including eviction due to capacity, so it cannot be identified as expiration.

choices.text: Assume all keys had their TTL shortened because the engine's CPU utilization briefly increased.
choices.explanation: CPU utilization alone does not show why a key is missing.

choices.text: Compare the affected node's Evictions with memory utilization and expiration metrics at the same time.
choices.explanation: Evictions indicates keys removed because of conditions such as the memory limit, which can be observed separately from expiration.

choices.text: Treat the decrease in current connections as the number of keys that disappeared before expiration.
choices.explanation: Connection count does not indicate why stored keys were removed.

source.label: ElastiCache for Valkeyのメトリクス

learning.reason: When keys disappear before their TTL, also check the configured memory limit and eviction policy.
learning.concept: Miss counts alone cannot distinguish expiration from eviction due to capacity.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Investigate persistent 429 responses affecting one customer
prompt: A REST API uses API keys and usage plans. One customer continues to receive 429 responses even with a low request rate, while other customers succeed. The access log records QUOTA_EXCEEDED as the response type. What should you check first?

choices.text: Assume the account-wide burst limit is insufficient and increase the limit for all users.
choices.explanation: Other users succeed, and the log indicates a response caused by a specific usage quota.

choices.text: Check the usage for the affected key, the associated usage plan's quotas by period, and the reset time.
choices.explanation: This helps determine whether the key reached a period quota, separately from per-second throttling.

choices.text: Increase Lambda concurrency first without checking whether API Gateway is rejecting the request.
choices.explanation: Requests rejected by the gateway will not be accepted just by increasing the downstream Lambda limit.

choices.text: Increase the client's retry count and wait for the period quota to recover through rapid retries.
choices.explanation: If a period quota is the cause, retrying rapidly will not restore the quota.

source.label: API Gatewayのゲートウェイ応答種別

learning.reason: 429 responses have multiple causes, so check the response type and the affected customer's usage.
learning.concept: The remedy differs for a usage limit over a period and a short-term request-rate limit.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Assessing Error-Budget Burn During a Brief Outage
prompt: In CloudWatch Application Signals, an availability SLO based on requests is set to 99.9%. The percentage of bad requests in the most recent observation window was 0.8%. Which burn rate and interpretation describe the recent error-budget consumption rate?

choices.text: 0.8; the recent percentage is below the allowable threshold.
choices.explanation: The 0.8% value is not itself the rate. A 99.9% target allows a 0.1% error rate.

choices.text: 0.125; divide the target's allowable error rate by the observed rate.
choices.explanation: The numerator and denominator are reversed.

choices.text: 8%; the remaining long-term budget can therefore be assumed to have automatically fallen to 92%.
choices.explanation: Burn rate is a ratio and, by itself, does not establish how much budget remains over the full measurement period.

choices.text: 8; during this observation window, the budget is being consumed at eight times the baseline rate of 0.1%.
choices.explanation: Divide the observed error rate for the window by the allowable error rate derived from the SLO target.

source.label: CloudWatch SLOのバーンレート

learning.reason: Read the short-term error rate as a multiple of the error rate allowed by the target.
learning.concept: Do not confuse the short-term consumption rate with the budget remaining over the entire measurement period.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Handling Temporary 503 Errors During a Sharp Increase in Access
prompt: When several new workers simultaneously begin writing at a high rate to the same S3 prefix, 503 Slow Down errors increase briefly. Permissions and keys are correct, and these operations can be retried safely. How should you reduce the load and failure rate?

choices.text: Have all workers retry without delay and increase the request rate until they succeed.
choices.explanation: Simultaneous retries during a temporary load spike can make the surge even larger.

choices.text: Ramp up worker starts or the sending rate gradually, and retry 503 responses with backoff that includes waiting and jitter. If needed, spread access across multiple prefixes.
choices.explanation: This addresses temporary errors while S3 scales and also reduces retry spikes at the same moment.

choices.text: Only increase the SDK connection timeout and wait for the 503 response to turn into a success on the server side.
choices.explanation: A received 503 is the result of that request. Increasing the timeout alone does not retry it or distribute the load.

choices.text: Grant the same permissions to another IAM role and send duplicate requests from multiple roles.
choices.explanation: Changing the request identity does not reduce the sharp increase in access to the prefix or the concentration of retries.

source.label: Amazon S3のパフォーマンス最適化

learning.reason: When load rises sharply, smooth out both the start of traffic and retries of failed requests.
learning.concept: Check the error type and use a retry policy appropriate for it, rather than one intended for configuration errors.

title: Indexing Only Orders That Have Not Been Processed
prompt: All orders are stored in DynamoDB, and each team needs to find its unprocessed orders. Most orders have already been processed, and only unprocessed orders should appear in a secondary index. The orders themselves must remain after processing. Which design should you choose?

choices.text: Create a GSI with the status of every order as its partition key, then specify unprocessed orders when searching.
choices.explanation: This can find unprocessed orders, but processed orders are also included in the index.

choices.text: Remove status from the GSI projection and assume that processed orders are then excluded from the projection entirely.
choices.explanation: A projection selects which attributes an index stores; it does not conditionally exclude items.

choices.text: Set TTL on processed orders so that they expire from only the GSI.
choices.explanation: TTL deletes the item from the base table itself, which does not meet the requirement to retain it after completion.

choices.text: Use a GSI key attribute that is present only on unprocessed orders, and remove that attribute from the item when processing is complete.
choices.explanation: Only items that have the GSI key attribute are included in the index, so the original order can remain after processing.

source.label: DynamoDBの疎なインデックス

learning.reason: Choose an index key attribute that is present only when an item should appear in the index.
learning.concept: Filtering the candidate set at read time differs from designing which items are included in the index itself.

title: Strongly Consistent Reads of a Customer’s Transactions by Settlement Time
prompt: A new DynamoDB table will use customerId and transactionId as its primary key. You need to retrieve a customer's transactions within a settlement-time range, sorted by that time, and strong consistency is required immediately after writes complete. The data volume per customer will remain within the LSI limits. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Create a GSI with settlement time as its sort key and set ConsistentRead to true.
choices.explanation: Strongly consistent reads are not available for a GSI.

choices.text: Query the base table by transaction ID, then sort the results by settlement time after retrieving them.
choices.explanation: You cannot use settlement time as a key condition to narrow the range before retrieving the results.
