choices.text: When creating the table, define an LSI with the same customerId and settlement time as the sort key, then use a strongly consistent Query.
choices.explanation: It provides another sort order for the same partition key, and an LSI supports strongly consistent reads.

choices.text: Create the table first, then add the LSI after the application is running.
choices.explanation: An LSI must be defined when the table is created and cannot be added to an existing table.

source.label: DynamoDBローカルセカンダリインデックス

learning.reason: Consider the required sort order, consistency, and when the index must be defined together.
learning.concept: A secondary index changes the available choices for partition keys and read consistency.

title: Preventing a function from retriggering on its own output
prompt: An S3 object-created notification invokes an image-conversion Lambda function. The function should process only objects under incoming/ in the same bucket and write converted images to processed/. Both the input and output files have the same extension, and the function should not be invoked for events it does not need to process. Which additional notification configuration should you use?

choices.text: Configure only a suffix filter based on the file extension.
choices.explanation: Because the input and output have the same extension, this cannot exclude notifications for output objects.

choices.text: Only check for processed/ at the start of the function and return early.
choices.explanation: This avoids recursive conversion, but the function is still invoked for events it does not need to process.

choices.text: Set the function's reserved concurrency to 1.
choices.explanation: Limiting concurrent invocations does not prevent notifications for output objects.

choices.text: Set the S3 object-created notification's prefix filter to incoming/.
choices.explanation: This restricts the keys that trigger the notification in S3, so writes to processed/ do not trigger it.

source.label: S3イベント通知とLambda

learning.reason: Separate the input location from the processed-data location, and limit the notification trigger to the input side.
learning.concept: Ignoring an event inside a function and filtering it out before a notification is issued have different effects on invocation counts.

title: Cleaning up only parts from interrupted uploads
prompt: A large file is uploaded to S3 as a multipart upload. If the browser is closed partway through, incomplete parts remain and incur charges. You want to leave the retention period for completed files unchanged and clean up only parts from interrupted uploads after a set number of days. What should you use?

choices.text: Set the same number of days in the standard object expiration rule.
choices.explanation: This affects the expiration of completed objects and is separate from the setting that aborts incomplete uploads.

choices.text: Configure AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload in a lifecycle rule.
choices.explanation: This aborts uploads that have not been completed after the specified number of days and deletes the remaining parts.

choices.text: Run only the standard DeleteObject against the destination key for the incomplete upload.
choices.explanation: Deleting a completed object and aborting an upload session use different APIs.

choices.text: Configure CompleteMultipartUpload to retry indefinitely.
choices.explanation: This does not stop transfers with missing parts or set an expiration for abandoned parts.

source.label: S3未完了マルチパートのライフサイクル

learning.reason: Keep the lifetime of incomplete data separate from that of completed data saved by users.
learning.concept: The work state from starting a multipart upload until completion is not part of a standard object.

title: Using the Aurora Data API to put two updates in one transaction
prompt: You have enabled the Aurora Data API. An application updates an order and inventory with two ExecuteStatement calls, and you want both updates rolled back if either one fails. Which two operations let the calls use the same transaction, even across HTTP requests?

choices.text: Call each ExecuteStatement without a transactionId and treat the calls as part of the same transaction if they come from the same client.
choices.explanation: Calls without a transaction ID are not automatically grouped into the same transaction.

choices.text: Call BeginTransaction, then pass the same returned transactionId to both ExecuteStatement calls.
choices.explanation: This associates both updates with the same transaction across calls.

choices.text: Call BeginTransaction once after the first update, so that the earlier update is included retroactively.
choices.explanation: An update executed before the transaction begins cannot be added to it afterward.

choices.text: Use a different transactionId for each ExecuteStatement and commit only the successful one.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent a state in which only one update succeeds.

choices.text: Call CommitTransaction if both calls succeed, and call RollbackTransaction with the same ID if either one fails.
choices.explanation: This instructs the API to commit or discard the same unit of work.

source.label: Aurora Data APIのトランザクション

learning.reason: Even with an HTTP-based API, explicitly passing a transaction ID preserves the unit of work.
learning.concept: Use the same identifier from the transaction's start through statement execution and commit or rollback.

title: Streaming generated download content as it is produced
prompt: A Lambda function on a supported Node.js runtime returns a report through an authenticated function URL. If the function waits until the entire result is generated before returning it, the first data takes too long to arrive. Which two changes are required to send each generated portion as it becomes available while preserving the existing authentication?

choices.text: Set the function URL's InvokeMode to RESPONSE_STREAM.
choices.explanation: This selects the invocation mode that streams responses through the function URL.

choices.text: Leave the function URL in BUFFERED mode and record output fragments in the application's logs.
choices.explanation: Log fragments are not delivered to the user in sequence as an HTTP response.

choices.text: Change the function URL's authentication type to NONE so that the response is streamed automatically.
choices.explanation: Authentication settings and invocation mode are separate, and removing authentication is not required.

choices.text: Use a supported streaming handler to write generated data to the response stream as it is produced.
choices.explanation: This lets the function send part of the response before buffering the entire result.

choices.text: Build a standard buffered response and only add the Transfer-Encoding header to the response.
choices.explanation: If the function continues to return the complete result at once, it cannot send earlier portions before the rest are generated.

source.label: Lambda関数URLの応答ストリーミング

learning.reason: Both the invocation path and the function implementation must support partial responses.
learning.concept: Even if a response is generated in chunks, the receiver gets it all at once unless streaming delivery is enabled.

title: Read the Same POSIX File from Different Execution Environments
prompt: Multiple Lambda functions in the same VPC open the same file by path using an existing library. They must be able to read the same work results from a shared POSIX file system, even when they run in different execution environments. Which two additional settings are needed to configure this with EFS?

choices.text: Give each function the same name for /tmp and assume the execution environments will automatically share files.
choices.explanation: Temporary storage belongs to each execution environment; using the same name does not make it shared.

choices.text: Configure the same EFS access point for each function and specify a supported local mount path, such as under /mnt.
choices.explanation: Each environment can use the common file system through a path the library can access.

choices.text: Copy the EFS shared data into each function's ZIP and make the contents of the ZIP writable.
choices.explanation: Distributing a local copy in the ZIP does not share files updated during processing with other environments.

choices.text: Leave the functions outside a VPC and use the EFS console URL as the mount location.
choices.explanation: Mounting EFS uses a network path to the file system, not HTTPS access to the console.

choices.text: Allow the Lambda subnets to reach the EFS mount targets, and provide the required NFS communication and access permissions.
choices.explanation: In addition to configuring the mount, network connectivity and permission to access the files are required.

source.label: Lambdaのファイルシステムアクセス

learning.reason: Execution-environment-specific temporary storage cannot meet a shared-file requirement.
learning.concept: Configure the access point, network connectivity, and permissions to access the files themselves.

title: Resume from a Persisted Checkpoint in the Same Shard
prompt: A custom Kinesis consumer has reliably applied processing results through a persisted sequence number in a shard. When a worker restarts, it must read the same shard, which is still within its retention period, starting just after that number. Which retrieval method should it use?

choices.text: Specify AT_SEQUENCE_NUMBER and the persisted number.
choices.explanation: The record at the persisted number itself is included as the read starting position.

choices.text: Use LATEST and treat it as the position just after the persisted number.
choices.explanation: This could skip unprocessed records that arrived before the restart.

choices.text: Choose TRIM_HORIZON and assume that, when a sequence number is present, it starts just after the oldest record.
choices.explanation: This method starts at the oldest record in the retention range; it does not indicate the application's saved progress.

choices.text: Call GetShardIterator with AFTER_SEQUENCE_NUMBER and the persisted value as StartingSequenceNumber.
choices.explanation: This excludes the persisted record and starts reading after it in the same shard.

source.label: Kinesis GetShardIteratorの開始位置

learning.reason: Do not treat the last processed position and the next read position as unconditionally identical.
learning.concept: Exclude the record already reliably applied, then read the remaining data after it.

title: Schedule a Recurring Run for the Local Morning
prompt: Use EventBridge Scheduler to start a process at 9:00 a.m. local time on business days in New York. Business days are weekdays, and the local time must remain the same when daylight saving time begins. Do not manually change the UTC conversion by season. Which settings should you choose?

choices.text: Specify one fixed UTC time and assume it will always correspond to the same local time, including during daylight saving time.
choices.explanation: The UTC offset changes with daylight saving time, so a fixed UTC time does not preserve the local time.

choices.text: Use rate(24 hours) to start after the same elapsed time every day and assume this also meets the weekday and local 9:00 a.m. requirements.
choices.explanation: A fixed interval does not express a weekday condition or the daylight-saving change in local time.

choices.text: Use a cron expression for 9:00 a.m. on weekdays and set the schedule expression's time zone to America/New_York.
choices.explanation: The execution time is evaluated in the specified time zone, accommodating daylight saving time.

choices.text: Keep the cron expression in UTC and only set a time zone in the Lambda environment variables.
choices.explanation: Handling time in the function does not change when Scheduler starts it.

source.label: EventBridge Schedulerのcronとタイムゾーン

learning.reason: For a recurring run whose required time is local time, evaluate the schedule in that time zone.
learning.concept: Distinguish a fixed elapsed-time interval from a schedule based on calendar time.

sourceLabel: EventBridge Scheduler cron expressions and time zones

title: Prepare Consumer Types from an Event Schema
prompt: Multiple teams handle the same custom EventBridge event. A version of the event is registered in the schema registry, and receiving applications in supported languages should use the event's type without having to write it by hand each time. What should they do?

choices.text: Replay an archive and assume the receiving applications' type declarations will be updated automatically.
choices.explanation: A replay redistributes events; it does not generate language types.

choices.text: Infer the types of all fields directly from the rule's event pattern without inspection.
choices.explanation: An event pattern expresses matching conditions. A schema that describes the entire data structure serves a different purpose.

choices.text: Configure an input transformer to directly change the programming-language types within the consumers.
choices.explanation: An input transformer can change the data being sent, but it does not generate the receiving applications' source code.

choices.text: Generate and retrieve code bindings from the specified schema version, then include them in the consumers' code.
choices.explanation: The event can be handled using types that correspond to its schema.

source.label: EventBridgeスキーマのコードバインディング

learning.reason: Associate the data definition's version with the corresponding code.
learning.concept: Even when using generated types, the application remains responsible for checking compatibility with the events it receives.

title: Change notification content without adding Publish calls
prompt: The same SNS topic has SMS and email subscriptions. You need to announce a deployment completion in one Publish call, sending a short message to SMS, detailed content to email, and a common message to other protocols. How should you specify this?

choices.text: Set MessageStructure to json and pass a JSON object in Message with string values for default, sms, and email.
choices.explanation: The service selects the value matching the subscription protocol and uses the default body if no protocol-specific value is provided.

choices.text: Use a regular string body and put the SMS message in an attribute value in the filter policy.
choices.explanation: A subscription filter selects whether to deliver a message; it does not construct protocol-specific message bodies.

choices.text: Send one long message and assume the SMS subscription will rewrite it into any short message required by the application.
choices.explanation: The SMS length limit may cause the message to be split, but that does not specify the intended short message.

choices.text: Set sms and email in MessageAttributes and leave Message as the default text.
choices.explanation: Adding attributes does not specify replacement message bodies for individual protocols.

source.label: SNS Publishのプロトコル別メッセージ

learning.reason: Distinguish attributes used to select destinations from message bodies selected for each delivery protocol.
learning.concept: A single publish can specify a default body and bodies for particular protocols.

title: Process remaining parent records before child shards after resharding
prompt: You are resharding Kinesis Data Streams. In a custom consumer, processing began as soon as child shards were discovered, so their records were processed before records still remaining in the parent shards. You want to preserve the order of the same input without tracking shard dependencies yourself. Which change is appropriate?

choices.text: Start child shards at LATEST and assume they will automatically catch up with unprocessed parent records.
choices.explanation: A child's starting position does not control the processing order of records remaining in its parent.

choices.text: Process parents and children at the same time, using the same start time for each.
choices.explanation: Aligning processing start times does not make a child wait for its parent to finish.

choices.text: Use the Kinesis Client Library and let it manage progression to child processing after parent processing completes.
choices.explanation: KCL assigns shards according to parent-child ordering.

choices.text: Only enable dedicated throughput with enhanced fan-out.
choices.explanation: This separates read capacity among consumers; it does not replace parent-child dependency management in a custom consumer.

source.label: Kinesisのリシャーディングとレコード処理

learning.reason: Preserve the order of work remaining on parents and work on children even as shards are added or removed.
learning.concept: Separating throughput and managing shard dependencies after resharding are different problems.

title: Wait in a workflow until each request's processing time
prompt: A JSONPath workflow in Step Functions Standard receives a different releaseAt value with each input. The value uses a supported UTC format, and you need the next step in the running execution to wait until that absolute time. You do not want to add a Lambda function to sleep. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Put the releaseAt string in Seconds in the Wait state.
choices.explanation: Seconds specifies a duration to wait; it does not accept an absolute time.

choices.text: Set Timestamp in the Wait state to the string $.releaseAt.
choices.explanation: Timestamp takes a time value directly. Use another field to obtain the value from a JSONPath.

choices.text: Set $.releaseAt in TimeoutSecondsPath in a Task state.
choices.explanation: A Task timeout limits how long processing may run; it does not pause the successful path until a specified time.

choices.text: Set $.releaseAt in TimestampPath in the Wait state.
choices.explanation: This reads the time from the state's input and waits until that absolute time.

source.label: Step Functions Wait状態

learning.reason: Distinguish waiting for a fixed duration from waiting until a time specified in the input.
learning.concept: Use the corresponding path field when the time or wait duration is selected dynamically.

title: Add a shared request ID to each array item
prompt: A JSONPath Step Functions Map iterates over $.items. Each iteration should receive only its item and the shared $.requestId. You do not want to pass the array or the entire original workflow input on every iteration. Which Map setting should you use?

choices.text: Set ItemsPath to $.requestId and assume it will find the existing array automatically.
choices.explanation: ItemsPath selects the array to iterate over; it does not extract and assemble shared fields.

choices.text: Set ResultPath to $.requestId and assume the Map will distribute the request ID to each item before execution.
choices.explanation: ResultPath concerns where to place the result; it does not define the input passed to each iteration.

choices.text: Pass the entire input to the Map as one item and extract the same array on each iteration.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy both processing one item at a time and avoiding extra input.

choices.text: Use ItemSelector to assemble each iteration's input from $$.Map.Item.Value and $.requestId.
choices.explanation: You can create each iteration's input using the iteration item in the Map context and the shared value in the state input.

source.label: Step Functions MapのItemSelector

learning.reason: Separate selecting the collection to iterate over from assembling the input each iteration receives.
learning.concept: Pass shared fields and per-item values in the required shape.

title: PDF generated by a REST API arrives as text
prompt: A API Gateway REST API using Lambda proxy integration returns a PDF to an administrative client other than a browser. The client sets Accept to application/pdf. Which two settings let the client receive the body as raw PDF data?

choices.text: Put the bytes directly in Lambda's body and use any type in the proxy integration JSON.
choices.explanation: The body in a Lambda proxy response must be a string, and binary data must be represented in the supported way.

choices.text: Set the function's body to a Base64 string, set isBase64Encoded to true, and return the appropriate Content-Type.
choices.explanation: The representation in the JSON and the flag indicating conversion to binary data must agree.

choices.text: Require the client to send only Accept-Encoding: base64.
choices.explanation: HTTP content-encoding negotiation does not configure binary handling in a Lambda proxy response.

choices.text: Add application/pdf to the REST API's binaryMediaTypes and deploy the update to a stage.
choices.explanation: API Gateway must also be told which media types to handle as binary.

choices.text: Specify the PDF type in a REST API request validator.
choices.explanation: This feature validates client requests; it does not decode responses from Lambda.

source.label: REST APIのLambdaプロキシ応答でバイナリーを返す

learning.reason: Check both the Lambda response format and the API Gateway media type configuration.
learning.concept: Configure the HTTP client's Accept value to match the media type that should be handled as binary.

sourceLabel: Returning binary data in a REST API Lambda proxy response

title: Connect a no-transformation intake API directly to SQS
prompt: An API Gateway HTTP API passes input to a fixed queue. The application waits only until SQS accepts the message; it does not wait for the worker's processing result. The function has no business logic beyond sending the body. Which two settings implement this without adding Lambda?

choices.text: Use the SQS-SendMessage integration subtype in an HTTP API AWS service integration.
choices.explanation: API Gateway can call SendMessage directly.

choices.text: Use SQS ReceiveMessage as the HTTP API integration and start the enqueue operation from the receive result.
choices.explanation: ReceiveMessage reads from a queue; it does not enqueue the request body.

choices.text: Set the queue URL and MessageBody in the integration parameters, and grant API Gateway permission to send to the target queue.
choices.explanation: With the destination, body, and service permission configured, the accepted data can be passed directly to the queue.

choices.text: Set only the queue's resource name as the integration target and assume SendMessage permission is granted to the caller automatically.
choices.explanation: A resource name alone neither grants runtime permission for the service integration nor specifies the message body.

choices.text: Create only a VPC link for the queue and assume an HTTP POST is automatically converted to SQS SendMessage.
choices.explanation: Network routing does not select an AWS service action or transform its parameters.

source.label: HTTP APIのAWSサービス統合サブタイプ

learning.reason: When no intermediary function is needed, connect the request to the corresponding AWS operation.
learning.concept: The synchronous wait is for queue acceptance and is independent of the queue consumer's business processing.

sourceLabel: HTTP API AWS service integration subtypes

title: Notify a connected user when there is no HTTP request
prompt: Send completion of a background process to an admin console connected to a WebSocket API. By the time processing finishes, execution of the original route has completed, and a different service sends the notification. The target connection ID and send permission are available. Which method should be used?

choices.text: From the sender, use the corresponding management API endpoint and pass the target connectionId and data to PostToConnection.
choices.explanation: The backend can send specified data to an existing WebSocket connection.

choices.text: Invoke $connect again from the completed process and return the body on the existing connection.
choices.explanation: $connect is a route associated with establishing a connection, not an API for sending arbitrary notifications to an already-open connection.

choices.text: Return a REST response to the internet-facing user's IP address and treat it as the same WebSocket connection.
choices.explanation: An IP address is not the same as a logical WebSocket connection, and a REST response cannot notify the target connection.

choices.text: Update the previous integration response and assume the already-completed request will be sent again later.
choices.explanation: Updating a response after the request has been processed does not send data over the open connection.

source.label: API Gateway WebSocket @connections

learning.reason: Distinguish a response to a route invocation from a later send by an asynchronous process.
learning.concept: To send to an existing client, specify the management endpoint for the API and stage and the target connection.

title: Constrain the response body to machine-readable JSON
prompt: A ticket-classification application uses a model that supports structured output with Bedrock Converse. The result must include category and priority, and the model must be given known types and required fields explicitly. Which method constrains the structure instead of relying only on instructions in a free-form prompt?

choices.text: Write “JSON” in the system instructions and assume the output will always match the template without a format setting.
choices.explanation: Free-form instructions may encourage a format, but they do not specify a schema constraint for model output.

choices.text: Set temperature to 0 and assume the requested JSON structure is validated.
choices.explanation: A setting for reproducibility is different from a constraint that the output satisfy a specified schema.

choices.text: Set the maximum output tokens to the number of fields and assume only those fields will be returned as JSON.
choices.explanation: The token limit restricts output length; it does not define field names or types.

choices.text: Provide a JSON Schema from the supported subset in Converse outputConfig.textFormat.
choices.explanation: Within the supported subset, this constrains the model's generated result to a format with the required types and fields.

source.label: BedrockのJSON構造化出力

learning.reason: Provide the data shape the reader needs in a format that the generation API can configure.
learning.concept: Format conformance and validation that the content is correct for the business task are both necessary.

title: Passing model-specific settings through a shared API
prompt: Several models are accessed through the shared Bedrock Converse interface. One model accepts an inference setting that is not available in Converse's shared inferenceConfig. The field name and supported value are known from the product documentation. Where should the setting be specified?

choices.text: Put the additional setting in requestMetadata so the model recognizes it as an inference setting.
choices.explanation: requestMetadata is for monitoring information; it does not extend a model's inference settings.

choices.text: Write the value in additionalModelResponseFieldPaths to pass it to the inference engine.
choices.explanation: This field specifies additional paths to retrieve from the response; it is not for request inference settings.

choices.text: Add the setting name as a user message to the messages for all existing models.
choices.explanation: Adding content to a message does not specify an API inference setting that the model recognizes.

choices.text: Specify the corresponding setting in additionalModelRequestFields only for calls to the target model.
choices.explanation: This lets you pass model-specific fields that cannot be expressed through the shared inference settings.

source.label: Bedrock Converse APIの追加フィールド

learning.reason: Use shared parameters and model-specific extensions for their respective purposes.
learning.concept: An input-side extension and a request for additional response fields use different fields.

sourceLabel: Additional fields in the Bedrock Converse API

title: Automatically running a related test when a file is saved
prompt: When editing an order API in Kiro, you want to run an existing short test command every time the corresponding file is saved to detect regressions. You want to use the actual command's success or failure, rather than relying on a generative AI's pass-or-fail comment. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Configure a file-save hook scoped to the target path and run the existing test as a shell command.
choices.explanation: A configured event can run a specified command, and the result can be determined by an actual test.

choices.text: Only add the testing procedure to the order API's Steering guide.
choices.explanation: This can share instructions, but it does not configure a trigger to run the test command when the file is saved.

choices.text: Mark the Spec task complete and assume the test will run automatically on every save.
choices.explanation: Updating a task's status is different from triggering a command when a file is saved.

choices.text: Have AI generate a description of the saved changes and use that text as a substitute for the test.
choices.explanation: Generating a description does not verify the code's behavior when it runs.

source.label: Kiroのフック機能

learning.reason: Connect a trigger condition to the action it should run.
learning.concept: Sharing behavior through a guide and running a routine check on an event serve different purposes.

title: Enforcing a limit on presigned URL age at issuance
prompt: Several issuing applications create presigned GET URLs for the same S3 bucket. Even if some applications specify a longer validity period, you want the bucket to reject any use more than five minutes after signing. You must not rely only on changes to each application. Which control should you use?

choices.text: Configure a lifecycle rule to expire objects after a short period.
choices.explanation: This changes the lifetime of the objects and does not evaluate the time elapsed since each URL was signed.

choices.text: Set the objects' Cache-Control value to five minutes.
choices.explanation: This controls response caching; it does not set the deadline for S3 to accept a presigned request.

choices.text: Only shorten the default validity period in the SDK used by each issuer.
choices.explanation: This does not enforce a bucket-side limit when an issuer specifies a value longer than the default.

choices.text: Use a bucket policy to deny applicable requests when s3:signatureAge exceeds 300000 milliseconds.
choices.explanation: The bucket can limit the time elapsed since signing independently of the validity period specified by the issuer.

source.label: S3署名付きURLのsignatureAge条件

learning.reason: Distinguish the validity period set at issuance from the permitted age of a signature enforced by the recipient.
learning.concept: A policy can enforce an organization-wide limit without relying only on each issuer's default setting.

title: Retaining a specific version only while an investigation remains open-ended
prompt: In a bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled, some object versions must be preserved for an investigation. There is no planned end date, and preservation must continue until an authorized investigator releases the hold. Routine retention is managed separately. What should be applied to the versions under investigation?

choices.text: Set a fixed retention date one year in the future for every target version.
choices.explanation: If the investigation continues beyond that date, the version is not guaranteed to remain protected until the investigation is over.

choices.text: Only add a tag named keep to the target versions.
choices.explanation: A tag alone does not enable deletion protection for an object version.

choices.text: Disable the routine expiration rule, but do not add any control on manual deletion.
choices.explanation: Changing lifecycle expiration does not prevent deletion of a specific version.

choices.text: Set a Legal Hold on each target object version and restrict permission to release it to authorized investigators.
choices.explanation: A Legal Hold has no automatic expiration and remains in effect until a permitted principal releases it.

source.label: S3 Object Lockのリーガルホールド

learning.reason: Choose between retention through a specified date and retention until a specific release action.
learning.concept: Object Lock evaluates protection at the object-version level.

title: Old development credentials are signing requests despite a task role
prompt: A Java 2.x application on ECS uses DefaultCredentialsProvider and does not specify credentials in its source code. The runtime environment still contains AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY for old development keys. Which change will make the application use temporary credentials from its task role?

choices.text: Only add the required permissions to the task role.
choices.explanation: Adding permissions to the role does not fix the issue if the SDK selects different credentials first.

choices.text: Move the old keys to Java system properties.
choices.explanation: System properties are also evaluated before container credentials.

choices.text: Only override the container credential retrieval endpoint while keeping the environment variable keys already set.
choices.explanation: The change will not take effect while credentials found earlier in the chain remain available.

choices.text: Remove the environment variable settings that provide the old keys so the default chain can reach the ECS container credentials.
choices.explanation: In this SDK, environment variable credentials are evaluated before container credentials.

source.label: AWS SDK for Java 2.xの既定認証情報チェーン

learning.reason: When access is denied, check both the required permissions and the principal the SDK actually selected.
learning.concept: When multiple credential sources are available, the first source that yields usable credentials is selected.

sourceLabel: Default credentials chain in AWS SDK for Java 2.x

title: Give a short-lived role only to a specified repository branch
prompt: Remove long-term AWS keys from a GitHub Actions deployment job and use the registered GitHub OIDC provider. The job does not specify a GitHub Environment and uses the default subject format. Trust for the production role must be limited to the main branch of a specific repository owned by your organization. Which two elements belong in the trust policy?

choices.text: Use the GitHub OIDC provider as the Federated principal and allow sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.
choices.explanation: This configures the trust path for assuming an AWS role with an OIDC token.

choices.text: Allow requests from GitHub's domain without checking the token's issuer or audience.
choices.explanation: Network-level information alone cannot authorize a token issued for the intended repository.

choices.text: Set the audience to STS, but allow every repository and branch in the organization in the subject condition.
choices.explanation: Even with the correct audience, this does not restrict the issuing job to the main branch of the specified repository.

choices.text: Require aud to be sts.amazonaws.com and sub to match the repository and main branch ref.
choices.explanation: This checks both that the token is intended for STS and that it comes from the specified repository and branch.

choices.text: Put the repository name in the access policy and leave the role trust policy unrestricted.
choices.explanation: A policy name is not evaluated as a condition for assuming the role.

source.label: IAMでのOIDCフェデレーションとGitHub Actions

learning.reason: Verify an external workload's identity using the token's audience and issuer context.
learning.concept: Set separate conditions for who can assume a deployment role and which actions the assumed role can perform.

sourceLabel: OIDC federation and GitHub Actions in IAM

title: A KMS key denies a request despite an IAM allow
prompt: An application role in the same account has an IAM policy allowing Decrypt on a customer managed KMS key. The key policy names only a dedicated administrator role, contains no statement delegating permissions to IAM, and there is no grant for the application. What should you change to allow the application to decrypt data only?

choices.text: Add an allow for Decrypt by the application role to the key policy.
choices.explanation: The key policy can directly allow the principal and required operation. There is no need to broaden the existing IAM statement beyond the target key.

choices.text: Change the Resource in the IAM policy to * so that the existing key policy automatically allows the application.
choices.explanation: Broadening the IAM permission does not resolve the lack of an authorization path in the key policy.

choices.text: Add an alias to the KMS key with the same name as the target role.
choices.explanation: An alias is a name that refers to a key; it does not grant permissions.

choices.text: Add an EncryptionContext to the application's request so it can decrypt without key policy authorization.
choices.explanation: An encryption context does not automatically grant authorization.

source.label: AWS KMSのキーポリシー

learning.reason: Check whether the key policy allows the IAM permission to take effect.
learning.concept: Distinguish between directly authorizing the application principal and delegating authorization to IAM policies in the account.

title: Restore decryption with a key that is pending deletion
prompt: A KMS key was accidentally scheduled for deletion. The owner notices during the waiting period and can cancel the deletion. Without migrating data to a new key, what sequence of actions will resume decryption with the key used for the existing ciphertext?

choices.text: Cancel deletion and assume that the key immediately returns to Enabled.
choices.explanation: After cancellation, the key is Disabled and cannot immediately perform cryptographic operations.

choices.text: Leave the key pending deletion and run DisableKey and EnableKey in sequence.
choices.explanation: You must cancel the deletion schedule before resuming decryption.

choices.text: Cancel deletion, enable the resulting Disabled key, and then verify decryption.
choices.explanation: Canceling deletion prevents the key from being deleted, but a separate enable operation is required to make it usable.

choices.text: Create a new key with the same name, switch the alias, and use it to decrypt the existing ciphertext.
choices.explanation: Using the same name does not restore the key material that protected the ciphertext.

source.label: AWS KMS削除予定の取り消し

learning.reason: Decrypting data also requires that the original key still exists and is in a state that allows cryptographic operations.
learning.concept: Canceling a pending deletion and making the key usable again are separate actions.

title: Preventing sign-in errors from revealing whether an account exists
prompt: A Cognito user pool app client uses USER_PASSWORD_AUTH. You want to return the same authentication failure for both a user who does not exist and a user who entered the wrong password. Password verification must continue. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Set PreventUserExistenceErrors to ENABLED for the app client, and display the same failure message in the user-facing interface.
choices.explanation: With this password flow, a generic authentication failure is returned even when the user does not exist.

choices.text: Only increase the password policy's minimum length.
choices.explanation: Changing the rules for new passwords does not change how sign-in failures are handled.

choices.text: Shorten the app client's token validity period.
choices.explanation: This changes the expiration of tokens issued after successful authentication and does not affect failure responses.

choices.text: Disable password verification in the user pool so both inputs produce the same result.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to keep authentication active during sign-in.

source.label: Cognitoのユーザー存在エラー制御

learning.reason: Even when reporting an authentication failure, do not include unnecessary account information in the response.
learning.concept: Standardize the errors shown to users without changing the authentication requirement.

title: Control user access separately from API keys
prompt: An API Gateway REST API uses API keys to measure usage by customer. An additional requirement is to allow access only to users within the same customer who are authorized to view orders. How should you implement user authentication and authorization while keeping the usage plan?

choices.text: Issue an API key to each user and use the key alone as proof of identity and order-viewing permission.
choices.explanation: API keys are for usage plans; they are not a way to implement user authentication and authorization.

choices.text: Keep the usage plan's API keys and use an authorizer that integrates with the existing identity system to validate tokens and order-viewing permissions.
choices.explanation: You can use the usage classification key alongside checks on what an authenticated user is allowed to do.

choices.text: Increase the customer's quota and allow access to orders whenever usage is within the permitted range.
choices.explanation: Usage levels do not verify whether a user is authorized to view orders.

choices.text: Replace the API key string with a group name for authorization and assume API Gateway will treat that string as proof of the user's membership.
choices.explanation: Naming a string does not associate it with an authenticated principal or group membership.

source.label: API Gatewayの使用量プランとAPIキー

learning.reason: Separate the identifier used to apply usage limits from the evidence used to determine who can perform which actions.
learning.concept: Usage management is not a substitute for user access control.

sourceLabel: API Gateway usage plans and API keys

title: Call an API from a process that does not involve user sign-in
prompt: A backend billing batch calls an API issued by Cognito. It needs to obtain an access token with only the invoice/read scope required by the batch, without a person signing in or a personal password being stored. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Configure a service app client with the client credentials flow and the required custom scope, then obtain a token using securely stored client credentials.
choices.explanation: This obtains a token with a custom scope from the authorized resource server without a person signing in.

choices.text: Manually issue a user pool authorization code every day and store the code as the batch's permanent key.
choices.explanation: An authorization code is a short-lived value to exchange, so it is not suitable for ongoing processing without a user.

choices.text: Store a user pool ID token long term and use it as the service's OAuth scope.
choices.explanation: An ID token represents user identity information; it is not a way to obtain the required API scope for a service.

choices.text: Configure a public app client with no secret and use client credentials without any input.
choices.explanation: With client credentials, the service must authenticate as the client.

source.label: CognitoのM2M認証とカスタムスコープ

learning.reason: Use a service-oriented authentication flow when access is needed by a service rather than through a person's actions.
learning.concept: Match the token's required access scope to a scope defined by the resource server.

sourceLabel: Cognito M2M authentication and custom scopes

title: Prevent an intermediate service from reading a specific form field
prompt: A form is submitted over HTTPS through CloudFront. The body uses the corresponding URL-encoded format, and only the value of the specified application number must be unreadable to an intermediate service that receives HTTP; only the final processing service may decrypt it. Keep the ordinary form fields and HTTPS. Which additional setting should you use?

choices.text: Only replace the HTTPS certificate presented to viewers.
choices.explanation: A service that terminates the HTTPS connection can handle the submitted values unless additional protection is applied.

choices.text: Exclude the application-number field from the cache policy.
choices.explanation: A cache policy determines what is used for caching; it does not encrypt a specified field in a POST body.

choices.text: Encrypt only responses from the origin and use that to protect the application number.
choices.explanation: The value to protect is in the request body sent to the service, not in the response.

choices.text: Use CloudFront field-level encryption to specify the form field, and let only the final processing service hold the private decryption key.
choices.explanation: CloudFront protects the specified field with a public key so that only limited downstream processing can decrypt it.

source.label: CloudFrontのフィールドレベル暗号化

learning.reason: In addition to encrypting data in transit, restrict which processing destination can decrypt the value.
learning.concept: Protecting a specified form field has a different scope from the protection provided by ordinary HTTPS.

title: Password connections fail after IAM authentication is enabled for the same database user
prompt: In RDS for PostgreSQL, an existing operations batch job that uses password authentication can no longer connect after rds_iam is granted to its database user. A new batch job will use IAM authentication, while the existing job still needs password authentication. How should they be handled?

choices.text: Use a dedicated database user with rds_iam for the new batch job, and create a separate least-privilege user without rds_iam for the existing job.
choices.explanation: Separating the authentication methods by database user lets each job continue using the method it needs.

choices.text: For connections using the same database user, always try a password first and switch to IAM only if it fails.
choices.explanation: When rds_iam is granted to this database user, IAM authentication takes precedence over password authentication in PostgreSQL.

choices.text: Store an IAM token as a fixed password for the existing batch job for an extended period.
choices.explanation: IAM tokens are for short-lived connection authentication and cannot serve as permanent passwords.

choices.text: Change the IAM role's duration and assume the same database user will automatically revert to password authentication.
choices.explanation: The duration of an AWS role does not change the precedence of authentication methods on the PostgreSQL side.

source.label: RDSのIAM DB認証

learning.reason: Check whether assigning the IAM authentication role to a database user affects its existing connection method.
learning.concept: During a migration, different database users can be assigned to the old and new authentication methods according to their needs.

title: Require user approval before performing a change
prompt: An internal assistant built with Bedrock Agents can look up appointments and cancel reservations. Looking up an appointment does not require additional approval. For a change such as canceling a reservation, the assistant must ask the user before calling the function and must not proceed if the user declines. Where should this be configured?

choices.text: Add a note to the original system instructions and leave the action group settings unchanged.
choices.explanation: Instructions alone do not configure the service to request confirmation before calling the target function.

choices.text: Ask for confirmation in the result message after the function has canceled the reservation.
choices.explanation: The change has already taken effect before the user can decline, so this does not meet the requirement for approval before execution.

choices.text: Set the cancellation Lambda's concurrency limit to 1 and treat that as approval.
choices.explanation: Concurrency controls parallel processing; it does not check the user's intent.

choices.text: Enable user confirmation for the cancellation action in the action group.
choices.explanation: This requests explicit confirmation before performing the target operation. The lookup action does not need the same setting.

source.label: Bedrock Agentsのアクション前確認

learning.reason: Configure pre-execution approval for the operations that require confirmation.
learning.concept: Conversation instructions and the prerequisite for starting an actual function call can be configured independently.

title: Restrict a KMS key to a specific log group
prompt: A customer managed KMS key is associated with one CloudWatch Logs log group. The regional CloudWatch Logs service is allowed to perform cryptographic operations, but the key policy must also restrict use to that log group. Which condition is appropriate?

choices.text: Set an alias with the same name as the log group and treat it as the scope for cryptographic operations.
choices.explanation: An alias names a key; it does not restrict which log group can use the key.

choices.text: Match only aws:RequestedRegion.
choices.explanation: This restricts the Region, but cannot distinguish among multiple log groups in that Region.

choices.text: Grant Decrypt to every application that sends logs and omit permission for the CloudWatch Logs service.
choices.explanation: Adding permissions for log writers does not restrict the key used by CloudWatch Logs to a specific log group.

choices.text: Restrict the key permission so that kms:EncryptionContext:aws:logs:arn matches the target log group's ARN.
choices.explanation: The encryption context for the log group used by CloudWatch Logs can be used to scope the key policy.

source.label: CloudWatch LogsのKMS暗号化

learning.reason: In addition to allowing the service that performs encryption, use the resource context supplied by the service to limit the scope.
learning.concept: Even for the same service and Region, you can restrict which log groups can use the KMS key.

title: Bucket settings do not override account-level restrictions
prompt: You are testing how S3 public access settings behave. BlockPublicPolicy is disabled for the bucket but enabled at the account level. Saving a new bucket policy that allows public read access is denied, even though the necessary IAM permissions are in place. Which explanation is correct?

choices.text: A setting disabled on an individual bucket takes precedence over the account-level setting.
choices.explanation: The most restrictive applicable setting is enforced.

choices.text: The account-level BlockPublicPolicy applies, so a public bucket policy cannot be set.
choices.explanation: Relaxing a setting on an individual bucket does not remove restrictions applied at the account level.

choices.text: BlockPublicPolicy applies only to ACLs, so this denial is unrelated to the bucket policy.
choices.explanation: This setting rejects requests to configure a policy that is determined to be public. A separate setting applies to ACLs.

choices.text: Public access is evaluated only after the bucket's first object has been made public.
choices.explanation: The operation that sets the public policy is evaluated.

source.label: S3 Block Public Accessの適用範囲

learning.reason: For access control, check settings at higher levels as well as those on the individual resource.
learning.concept: When a setting with the same name exists at multiple scopes, the bucket's displayed value alone does not determine the effective value.

title: Add HSTS to delivery responses without changing the origin
prompt: A static site served through CloudFront already has HTTPS configured. You want to return Strict-Transport-Security to viewers without changing the origin, including on cache hits that do not contact the origin again. Where should you configure this?

choices.text: Add Strict-Transport-Security to the origin request policy.
choices.explanation: This configures requests sent to the origin; it does not change the response returned to viewers.

choices.text: Set the viewer protocol policy to Redirect HTTP to HTTPS and assume that HSTS is added automatically.
choices.explanation: Redirecting HTTP to HTTPS and sending an HSTS response header to the browser are separate behaviors.

choices.text: Include the Strict-Transport-Security request header in the cache key.
choices.explanation: Changing how the cache differentiates requests does not add a response header sent to viewers.

choices.text: Associate a response headers policy that includes HSTS with the applicable cache behavior.
choices.explanation: CloudFront adds the header to responses sent to viewers, including responses served from the existing cache.

source.label: CloudFrontレスポンスヘッダーポリシー

learning.reason: Changing a response returned to viewers is separate from configuring requests or the cache key.
learning.concept: A response headers policy can also be applied when content is returned from the cache.

title: Rotate JWT signing keys while honoring existing tokens
prompt: An HTTP API JWT authorizer retrieves public keys from the issuer's JWKS. You are switching to a signing key with a different kid, but valid tokens issued before the switch must remain usable for a while. Which procedure accounts for API Gateway's public key cache?

choices.text: Remove the old public key from the JWKS at the same moment you start using the new key.
choices.explanation: A validator without a cached key, or one that has refreshed its cache, would no longer be able to validate previously issued valid tokens.

choices.text: Replace only the public key material while keeping the same kid, and assume all caches update immediately.
choices.explanation: While a cache still holds the old key, it cannot reliably validate new signatures associated with the same identifier.

choices.text: Disable JWT signature validation only when a key cannot be retrieved.
choices.explanation: Authentication must remain in place; this gives up validation instead of improving the key rotation procedure.

choices.text: Publish the new public key first, then publish both old and new keys during a migration period that accounts for key caching and the validity period of already issued tokens.
choices.explanation: This prepares the system to validate valid tokens that use either key during the migration period.

source.label: API Gateway JWT公開鍵のキャッシュ

learning.reason: Account for when the public keys become visible to validators as well as when the signing side switches keys.
learning.concept: Update the key identifier and provide a migration period in which previously issued tokens can still be validated.

sourceLabel: API Gateway JWT Public Key Caching

title: Require token-based metadata requests while retaining the instance profile
prompt: An application on EC2 uses temporary credentials from its instance profile. Its SDK supports IMDSv2, and the metadata service is still needed. You must keep the existing role and disallow IMDS requests without a token. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Keep HttpEndpoint enabled and set HttpTokens to required for the instance.
choices.explanation: This keeps metadata access available while requiring token-based IMDSv2 requests.

choices.text: Add a condition only to the instance role's trust policy, without changing the instance's metadata settings.
choices.explanation: Changing permission to assume the role does not control the request method used with the metadata service.

choices.text: Set HttpEndpoint to disabled, and have the application continue retrieving credentials from the same metadata service.
choices.explanation: Disabling the endpoint prevents the application from obtaining the existing instance profile credentials through that path.

choices.text: Set HttpTokens to optional and rely on the compatible SDK alone to enforce this for all clients.
choices.explanation: Even if the compatible SDK uses IMDSv2, optional does not reject other requests made without a token.

source.label: EC2インスタンスメタデータの設定

learning.reason: Keep the required path for retrieving workload credentials while limiting which metadata request methods are allowed.
learning.concept: Enabling the endpoint and requiring a token are independent settings.

title: Avoid overwriting other environment variables during concurrent updates
prompt: A deployment job adds one environment variable to a Lambda function's $LATEST configuration. An operator may update a different environment variable at the same time. You must preserve the variables already present and, if another update occurs after you read the configuration, fetch it again before applying your change. Which two actions are required?

choices.text: Retrieve the configuration, merge the new value into the existing Variables, and send the entire map.
choices.explanation: An environment variable update replaces the entire map with the one you send, so include the values you want to preserve.

choices.text: Include only the variable being changed in Variables and assume the service automatically merges the other entries.
choices.explanation: This is not a partial update that preserves existing variables omitted from the request.

choices.text: Update the function using the same function name and assume concurrent operations are merged by key.
choices.explanation: The function name alone cannot detect a configuration change that occurred after you read it.

choices.text: Specify the retrieved RevisionId in the update request, and, if the configuration has changed, retrieve it again and merge again.
choices.explanation: The update can be conditioned on the revision read, preventing a replacement based on stale configuration.

choices.text: Temporarily set the maximum concurrency to 1 so that deployment operations also run one at a time.
choices.explanation: Function invocation concurrency does not provide mutual exclusion for configuration update APIs.

source.label: Lambda環境変数とRevisionId

learning.reason: Understand the scope of configuration replacement and use an update condition to detect changes made after reading it.
learning.concept: Even when merging client-side, do not perform the update unconditionally.

title: Pass a built local artifact to a separate deployment job
prompt: After a SAM build, the template references a local artifact to be deployed. You want to place the ZIP in S3 before approval and pass a template with the reference rewritten, without handing the working directory to the job that deploys to production. Which operation should you use?

choices.text: Run sam validate to validate the configuration and assume that the template path is automatically replaced with an S3 location.
choices.explanation: Validation does not upload local artifacts or change artifact references in the template.

choices.text: Place the local ZIP in S3 and keep the local path in the template.
choices.explanation: A separate job or CloudFormation cannot find an S3 copy from that local path.

choices.text: Run sam deploy before approval and use information about the created resources as input to the deployment job.
choices.explanation: The artifact must be prepared before approval; the requirement is not to deploy production resources in advance.

choices.text: Use sam package to upload the artifacts to a deployment bucket and output a template with the references rewritten to S3 locations.
choices.explanation: This prepares the artifact storage and lets you pass the template that references those artifacts to the next job.

source.label: AWS SAM sam package

learning.reason: Convert built artifact paths into locations that a later deployment environment can access.
learning.concept: Artifact preparation can be performed separately from starting the deployment operation.

title: Reproduce synthesis in CI using environment lookup results
prompt: CDK looks up an existing VPC when synthesizing a stack. Synthesis works locally, but environment lookup results can differ in CI, sometimes changing subnet selection. You want to review the environment lookup results cached by CDK and synthesize with the same values until you intentionally update them. How should you manage this?

choices.text: Review the lookup results for the target environment in cdk.context.json and commit the file to version control; update the relevant context only when needed.
choices.explanation: Sharing cached lookup results helps prevent synthesis for the same environment from changing unexpectedly as AWS-side state changes.

choices.text: Delete cdk.context.json each time, look up the results again from the production AWS environment, and assume they will always match the previous results.
choices.explanation: If the lookup target has changed, the results can change too.

choices.text: Pin only the CDK version and assume the VPC lookup results are pinned as well.
choices.explanation: Pinning the CDK version does not pin AWS environment lookup results, which are a separate input.

choices.text: Share only the dependency lockfile generated by the build and assume CDK will restore lookup results from the dependency data.
choices.explanation: Dependency lock information does not retain AWS environment lookup results.

source.label: AWS CDKのコンテキスト値

learning.reason: In addition to source and library versions, environment information used during synthesis affects reproducibility.
learning.concept: Update cached environment lookup results deliberately when a change is needed.

title: Reference another team’s existing bucket without taking ownership
prompt: You are deploying a file-processing Lambda with CDK. An S3 bucket is managed by another team’s stack, and this stack must not manage its creation, deletion, or replacement. In your code, you want to reference the existing bucket as an object and pass its name to the function. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Declare a new Bucket with the same name and assume it will automatically adopt the existing bucket as the same logical resource if one is present.
choices.explanation: Declaring a new resource attempts to create the existing bucket; it does not merely reference it.

choices.text: Import the bucket into your stack’s management using a CloudFormation resource import.
choices.explanation: The requirement is to reference the existing resource, not transfer its management.

choices.text: Copy the other team’s entire bucket definition as an AWS::S3::Bucket resource and set RemovalPolicy.
choices.explanation: Changing the deletion setting does not avoid declaring a resource to create and manage.

choices.text: Represent the existing bucket with a reference API such as Bucket.fromBucketName, then pass the bucket name in the function configuration.
choices.explanation: This references the existing bucket without declaring that this stack creates or manages it.

source.label: CDKで既存リソースを参照

learning.reason: Distinguish obtaining a reference from bringing a resource under a stack’s management.
learning.concept: When you reference a resource managed by another owner, you can manage only the configuration that uses it.

title: Create the route after attaching the internet gateway
prompt: A CloudFormation template defines a VPC, an internet gateway, a VPCGatewayAttachment, and a Route that uses the gateway. The Route references the gateway, but it may be created before the attachment to the VPC is complete. Which setting guarantees the order?

choices.text: Place the Route last in the template.
choices.explanation: Definition order in the file alone does not guarantee the creation order of resources without dependencies.

choices.text: Keep a Ref to the gateway ID in the Route and assume that this dependency automatically includes the attachment resource.
choices.explanation: A Ref dependency on the gateway itself does not guarantee completion of a separate attachment resource.

choices.text: Set the Route’s DependsOn to the logical ID of VPCGatewayAttachment.
choices.explanation: This makes route creation wait for the resource that attaches the gateway to the VPC, not just for the gateway to exist.

choices.text: Set the VPCGatewayAttachment’s DependsOn to the Route.
choices.explanation: This requires the reverse order, creating the Route first.

source.label: CloudFormation DependsOn

learning.reason: The existence of a resource and completion of an association that makes it usable can be separate.
learning.concept: Use DependsOn to specify creation order that an implicit reference does not express.

title: Delete on Initial Failure, Retain After Operations Begin
prompt: A CloudFormation stack creates a resource that stores data. If the initial creation operation is rolled back, you want to delete the newly created, unused resource. However, if the stack is deleted after creation succeeds and operations have begun, the data must be retained. Which DeletionPolicy should you specify?

choices.text: Set RetainExceptOnCreate.
choices.explanation: The resource is deleted if the operation that created it is rolled back; otherwise, it is treated as Retain.

choices.text: Always set Retain.
choices.explanation: The resource remains after operations begin, but it also remains if the initial creation is rolled back.

choices.text: Always set Delete.
choices.explanation: The resource is cleaned up initially, but its data is not retained when the stack is deleted after operations begin.

choices.text: Set only UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain.
choices.explanation: This controls what happens when an update replaces the resource; it does not control the specified initial rollback or stack deletion.

source.label: CloudFormation DeletionPolicy

learning.reason: The requirements differ for deletion immediately after a failed creation and deletion after the resource contains production data and is in operation.
learning.concept: A retention policy can make an exception specifically for a rollback during initial creation.

title: Package Only Deployment Files While Preserving Their Directory Structure
prompt: CodeBuild outputs web deployment files to dist/ and test data outside that directory. At the deployment destination, the archive must have index.html at its root and preserve relative paths under assets/. Which artifact configuration should you use?

choices.text: Use the repository root as the base directory, include only dist/**/*, and keep dist/ as the deployment root.
choices.explanation: This does not make the archive root match the structure expected by the deployment destination.

choices.text: Enable discard-paths to place all files together at the archive root.
choices.explanation: This loses relative paths such as those under assets/.

choices.text: Set artifacts base-directory to dist, include its contents, and leave discard-paths disabled.
choices.explanation: This excludes dist itself as the archive's leading path while preserving the relative directories in the artifacts.

choices.text: Change only the test report output location to dist and include the entire repository as artifacts.
choices.explanation: This does not exclude files that are unnecessary for deployment or limit the artifact inputs to dist.

source.label: CodeBuild buildspecの成果物設定

learning.reason: Specify separately which files to include and which relative paths to preserve inside the archive.
learning.concept: Prepare the artifact with the directory structure the deployment destination requires.

title: Use Credentials Only During the Build for Testing
prompt: A CodeBuild integration test needs only apiToken from an existing Secrets Manager secret. The value must not be included in the source or artifacts; the test should receive it as an environment variable. Which two settings are required?

choices.text: In buildspec env/secrets-manager, map the environment variable name to the secret and JSON key.
choices.explanation: This lets the source specify where to retrieve the value at build time without containing the value itself.

choices.text: Write the current token in plaintext under buildspec env/variables and commit it.
choices.explanation: The value would remain in the source, so this does not meet the requirement to retrieve the secret at build time.

choices.text: Save the token in the output archive and read it back as an environment variable only in the deployment job.
choices.explanation: There is no need to include the secret in the artifact, and this is not the point at which the test needs it.

choices.text: Allow the CodeBuild service role to retrieve the secret, and grant any required decryption permission if a customer managed key is used.
choices.explanation: In addition to configuring where to retrieve the value, the principal running the build must be allowed to retrieve it.

choices.text: Put the token in the description of a pipeline manual approval and have the build read it.
choices.explanation: This exposes the secret in human-readable approval information instead of using the service's secure retrieval path.

source.label: CodeBuild buildspecのシークレットマッピング

learning.reason: The build definition specifies where to retrieve the secret at runtime instead of storing its value.
learning.concept: Limit retrieval permission to the build service role and keep the value out of logs and artifacts.

title: Run Independent Tests in Parallel, Then Aggregate Their Results in One Stage
prompt: In one CodePipeline test stage, start unit tests and contract tests at the same time, then start an aggregation action after both complete successfully. Aggregate each test's results as a separate input artifact. Which action ordering should you configure?

choices.text: Set runOrder to 1 for all three actions.
choices.explanation: Actions with the same runOrder run in parallel, so the aggregation action does not wait for the tests to finish.

choices.text: Set runOrder to 1, 2, and 3 for the unit test, contract test, and aggregation actions, respectively.
choices.explanation: The aggregation action runs later, but the two independent tests do not start at the same time.

choices.text: Set only the stage execution mode to PARALLEL and leave the action runOrder values unset.
choices.explanation: The execution mode governs how pipeline executions relate to each other; it does not express action dependencies within a single execution.

choices.text: Set runOrder to 1 for both tests and 2 for the aggregation action.
choices.explanation: The tests with the same number run in parallel, and the later action can run after both succeed.

source.label: CodePipelineアクションのrunOrder

learning.reason: Make the ordering explicit between work that can run in parallel and work that depends on all its results.
learning.concept: Parallel actions within one execution are distinct from parallel pipeline executions.

title: Build continuously while restricting production deployment to a time window
prompt: CodePipeline should build and test at any time on weekdays. Add a control only to the production deployment stage so that it cannot be entered outside approved times and days. Define the times in the operations team's time zone. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Disable the source Git trigger and start all stages only during the allowed window.
choices.explanation: This cannot satisfy both the requirement to restrict only production and the requirement to build and test at any time.

choices.text: Check the time after the production stage succeeds and suppress the success notification if it is outside the window.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent a production deployment from starting outside the window.

choices.text: Add the day of the week to the artifact name and assume the pipeline will determine the time from the filename automatically.
choices.explanation: A name identifies an artifact; it does not configure a condition for entering a stage.

choices.text: Set a DeploymentWindow rule as a before-entry condition on the production stage, specifying the allowed days, times, and time zone.
choices.explanation: The time condition is evaluated before entry, controlling access to production independently of preceding builds and tests.

source.label: CodePipelineのDeploymentWindowルール

learning.reason: Keep pipeline execution separate from the times when production changes are allowed.
learning.concept: A condition intended to prevent an operation should be applied before that operation starts.

title: Add a deployment tag to a verified image
prompt: An image in a supported format has been verified in the same ECR repository. You want to add an unused prod tag to that same image without rebuilding it or downloading its container layers to the deployment job. Which procedure should you use?

choices.text: Rebuild from the current Dockerfile and push a new image as prod.
choices.explanation: There is no guarantee that a rebuild will produce the same content, and this does not add a tag to the existing image.

choices.text: Create a new repository for prod and register only the original image's tag name as a string.
choices.explanation: Storing the tag name alone does not provide an image with its corresponding manifest and layers.

choices.text: Use BatchGetImage to read the existing manifest, then use PutImage to specify that manifest and add the prod tag.
choices.explanation: This tags the existing image without bringing its layers onto the local machine.

choices.text: Run a new scan of the existing image and use the completion event as the prod tag.
choices.explanation: Running a scan and creating an image tag are separate operations.

source.label: Amazon ECRでのイメージ再タグ付け

learning.reason: Create a deployment reference without changing the contents of the verified artifact.
learning.concept: Once you distinguish the manifest from the image layers, you can add a reference without retrieving the image data.

title: Vary feature behavior by customer segment using one configuration version
prompt: An application uses the AppConfig Agent to deploy the configuration for one feature flag to the same environment. Trial and subscribed users should see different content, and the value returned should be selected using each request's customer segment. You do not want to split the configuration across multiple profiles. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Define rules for each segment and a default value in one multi-variant feature flag, then pass the user's segment as context when retrieving it.
choices.explanation: A matching variant can be selected from the same configuration definition using the context.

choices.text: Toggle only the feature flag's enabled value for all requests and assume it can also return different values for different users.
choices.explanation: On or off alone cannot return different configuration content based on a request's segment.

choices.text: Set the deployment strategy's Bake time separately for each customer segment to obtain a segment-specific flag value.
choices.explanation: Bake time is an observation period after deployment; it does not select a value based on request context.

choices.text: Include the customer segment in a CloudWatch alarm name and assume that a flag variant will be returned regardless of the alarm state.
choices.explanation: The name of a monitoring alarm is not an input for selecting configuration for an individual request.

source.label: AppConfigのマルチバリアント機能フラグ

learning.reason: Separate the configuration deployed for everyone from the individual value selected using context.
learning.concept: A single flag can represent multiple behaviors, including a default for requests that match no condition.

title: Switch to a verified configuration version without changing the consumer
prompt: Parameter Store has multiple versions under the same parameter name. You want the application to use only a verified version. How can the operations team switch versions and roll back without resetting the version number each time the application is deployed?

choices.text: Have the application retrieve the parameter name without specifying a version each time, and assume it will return the verified version when a new version is created.
choices.explanation: An unversioned retrieval is not pinned to the verified version you want to select.

choices.text: Overwrite the verified configuration directly in an older version, changing the contents associated with the same version number.
choices.explanation: Changing the contents of a version conflicts with the requirement to preserve the specified older version as it is.

choices.text: Deploy the version number as a hard-coded application value and redeploy the application for every switch.
choices.explanation: This allows the version number to change but does not meet the requirement to switch without redeploying.

choices.text: Label the verified parameter version, and have the application retrieve it by specifying the name and label. Move the label when a change is approved.
choices.explanation: This selects the parameter version without changing the reference string used by the application.

source.label: Parameter Storeのパラメーターラベル

learning.reason: Treat the application's stable reference and the configuration version it points to as separate things.
learning.concept: A label indicates which version to select; it does not duplicate the parameter value.

title: Restrict the origin of an internal package by package name
prompt: A CodeArtifact repository contains internal packages and uses an upstream repository for public dependencies. For one existing internal package, local publishing must remain allowed, but versions with the same name must not be pulled from upstream. Upstream access for other packages must remain available. Which setting meets these requirements?

choices.text: Remove the upstream repository from the repository as a whole.
choices.explanation: This would also prevent other packages from accessing upstream repositories.

choices.text: Set Publish to BLOCK and Upstream to ALLOW.
choices.explanation: This would block internal publishing and allow upstream ingestion, the opposite of the requirement.

choices.text: Assume that shortening the expiration of allowed tokens will also prevent packages with the same name from being pulled from upstream.
choices.explanation: Token expiration controls how long authentication remains valid; it does not restrict the source from which a specific package can be obtained.

choices.text: For the target package, set the origin control for direct publishing to ALLOW and Upstream to BLOCK.
choices.explanation: This lets you control internal publishing and ingestion from upstream separately for this package.

source.label: CodeArtifactのパッケージオリジン制御

learning.reason: Configure the entry points individually for a package whose origin must be restricted, even within the same repository.
learning.concept: Allowing direct publishing and allowing versions from upstream are separate controls.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Determine whether a slow first invocation is due to initialization or handler execution
prompt: In an on-demand Node.js Lambda function, only the first request in a new execution environment is slow. The CloudWatch Logs stream contains a REPORT line, and steady-state business processing takes about the same amount of time. Which check can isolate initialization latency?

choices.text: Treat Memory Size in REPORT as the execution time and check whether its value differs for the first invocation.
