choices.explanation: Memory Size is the configured memory capacity; it does not represent elapsed time.

choices.text: Aggregate only CloudWatch Invocations and use that to break down the first request.
choices.explanation: A count-only metric cannot distinguish initialization time from handler execution time.

choices.text: Divide Max Memory Used by Billed Duration and treat the ratio as the initialization time.
choices.explanation: Combining memory and billed time does not yield an initialization measurement.

choices.text: Check Init Duration in the REPORT line for the slow invocation and compare it separately with the handler time shown by Duration.
choices.explanation: This helps distinguish initialization, when Init Duration is reported, from function execution time.

source.label: Node.js LambdaのREPORTログ

learning.reason: Separate an increase in end-to-end latency into initialization time and business-code execution time.
learning.concept: REPORT fields use different units, such as time and capacity, so use the field that directly measures the quantity of interest.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Check runtime-version compatibility without reverting the code change
prompt: A Lambda function using a managed runtime starts failing in a specific dependency library immediately after receiving a newer runtime update, even though the function code is unchanged. The version ARN of the runtime that worked immediately before the update is known. What is an appropriate temporary measure until a permanent fix is ready?

choices.text: Temporarily switch to Manual mode and roll back to the previously working runtime version ARN. Return to regular updates after fixing compatibility.
choices.explanation: Specifying the earlier runtime version can help isolate the impact. Manual mode can be used as a temporary measure for a compatibility issue.

choices.text: Redeploy the same code and assume that AWS will always select the previous runtime version.
choices.explanation: Redeploying the code does not specify a rollback to the previous runtime version.

choices.text: Set the runtime update mode to Function update and assume it will automatically roll back to the old version without specifying a runtime version ARN.
choices.explanation: This setting changes when a runtime update is applied; it does not select a known earlier version.

choices.text: Change the function alias name and assume that the alias string determines the managed runtime patch version.
choices.explanation: An alias name does not specify the managed runtime version ARN.

source.label: Lambdaマネージドランタイム更新の制御

learning.reason: Distinguish changes to the code artifact from changes to the managed runtime that runs the code.
learning.concept: Even when a rollback to an earlier patch is available, it should not be treated as a permanent way to stop updates.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Move from API-wide metrics to monitoring a specific method
prompt: For an API Gateway REST API in prod, only Latency and 5XXError aggregated across all methods are visible. You want to monitor a specific resource and HTTP method with CloudWatch metrics, without logging request bodies or headers. Where should you configure this?

choices.text: Enable detailed CloudWatch metrics for the stage or method, using dimensions that include the resource and method.
choices.explanation: This publishes metrics at a finer granularity than API-wide metrics and does not require detailed body logs.

choices.text: Rename the API for each route and expect its current API-wide metrics to be broken down by name.
choices.explanation: Renaming an API does not create separate dimensions for resources and methods within that API.

choices.text: Only enable body tracing in the access logs.
choices.explanation: This adds detail to logs; it is separate from API Gateway metrics with the desired dimensions.

choices.text: Enable API caching and assume that CloudWatch will publish detailed dimensions for every method.
choices.explanation: Using a cache is separate from enabling detailed monitoring granularity.

source.label: API Gatewayのメトリクスとディメンション

learning.reason: Configure the granularity of the routes you want to monitor, separately from recording request bodies that do not need to be logged.
learning.concept: When adding detailed dimensions, you can limit them to the scope that is needed.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Interpreting why a download did not complete despite HTTP 200
prompt: For a large file served through CloudFront, a log row has sc-status 200, x-edge-response-result-type other than Error, and x-edge-result-type Error. Before counting this as an origin response failure, how should you interpret this combination?

choices.text: CloudFront changed every 5xx response received from the origin to 200.
choices.explanation: This combination alone does not indicate that an origin 5xx response was rewritten.

choices.text: It was a cache hit, which also guarantees that the client received all the data.
choices.explanation: Even when a response starts from the cache, the client can disconnect before receiving it all.

choices.text: The HTTP response started successfully, but the client disconnected before receiving all bytes.
choices.explanation: The result recorded before sending the response can differ from the result recorded after the transfer ends.

choices.text: CloudFront rejected the request through access control, so no HTTP response was started.
choices.explanation: The log shows HTTP status 200; evaluate the final connection result separately from the response code.

source.label: CloudFront標準ログの結果フィールド

learning.reason: Assess response-code success separately from whether the transfer completed.
learning.concept: When the results before and after delivery differ, you can distinguish a disconnect during response transmission.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Go directly to the logs for one ECS task
prompt: Many ECS tasks send standard output with awslogs to the same CloudWatch Logs log group. You know the target task ID and container name. If awslogs-stream-prefix is set in the task definition, which stream name should you look for?

choices.text: The configured prefix/container name/ECS task ID.
choices.explanation: The stream name identifies the container and the task that ran it, even within the same log group.

choices.text: The service name/task definition revision/account ID.
choices.explanation: This awslogs configuration does not build the stream name from the service name and revision.

choices.text: The task name/Region/host name.
choices.explanation: This does not follow the naming rule that uses the configured prefix and container name.

choices.text: Only the configured prefix, with all containers and tasks writing to the same stream.
choices.explanation: The stream name includes components that identify the target container and task, in addition to the prefix.

source.label: ECS awslogsのログストリーム命名

learning.reason: Use the task and container identifiers instead of searching by an ambiguous service name.
learning.concept: The awslogs stream prefix is part of the naming rule used to find logs for each task.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Reaching ECR is not enough to download image layers
prompt: You use a supported Fargate platform in a private subnet with no internet egress. For an internal image already registered in ECR in the same Region, the ecr.api and ecr.dkr interface endpoints and IAM permissions have been verified. The manifest can be retrieved, but layer transfers fail. What should you check next?

choices.text: Shorten the Docker image tag and check whether the layer path then uses only the ECR API endpoint.
choices.explanation: A tag is a reference name; it does not change the path used to transfer layer data.

choices.text: Reattach only the container's application role, without checking the network path to S3.
choices.explanation: Authentication already confirmed to work should be separated from the layer download path.

choices.text: Check the route from the task subnet to the S3 location ECR uses, and associate the required S3 gateway endpoint with the route table.
choices.explanation: ECR also uses S3 to retrieve layer data, so reaching the ECR interface endpoints alone is not enough.

choices.text: Add an endpoint for CloudWatch Logs and assume the S3 layers will download over the logging path.
choices.explanation: The log delivery path cannot replace the path used to retrieve S3 layers.

source.label: ECRをプライベートエンドポイントで利用

learning.reason: Diagnose the registry request path separately from the path used to retrieve the image data itself.
learning.concept: When different stages of a protocol use different services, configure the network path required by each stage.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: A request-level metric does not rise with partially unprocessed writes
prompt: There are periods when DynamoDB BatchWriteItem returns with some items unprocessed. In CloudWatch, WriteThrottleEvents increases, but BatchWriteItem ThrottledRequests does not increase at the same rate. How should you interpret the difference between these metrics?

choices.text: Both count write items in the same way, so one of the metrics is broken.
choices.explanation: The two metrics do not measure the same unit.

choices.text: WriteThrottleEvents counts every retry made by the API client, so individual write outcomes are irrelevant.
choices.explanation: It concerns throttled write events; it does not directly count SDK retries.

choices.text: For BatchWriteItem, ThrottledRequests increases by the number of unprocessed items in the response.
choices.explanation: You cannot treat the individual count of unprocessed items as a metric for the batch request as a whole.

choices.text: Individually throttled writes contribute to WriteThrottleEvents, while the batch-level ThrottledRequests increases only when all operations are throttled.
choices.explanation: Partial throttling can be missed if you look only at the metric for the batch request as a whole.

source.label: DynamoDBのスロットリングメトリクス

learning.reason: Distinguish the outcome of one batch API call from observations of the operations within it.
learning.concept: For workloads with partial failures, examine both request-level and operation-level metrics.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Load Is Concentrated on One Replica Despite Using the Reader Endpoint
prompt: There are multiple Aurora read replicas. A read service uses the reader endpoint, but the process maintains only one long-lived database connection, and that replica is busy. Which decision would distribute reads without changing the write target?

choices.text: Consider establishing multiple read-only physical connections through the reader endpoint. Load balancing occurs at the connection level.
choices.explanation: With one long-lived connection, the target remains fixed. Creating multiple connections can make different read targets available.

choices.text: Change the order of SELECT statements within the same connection so each query is routed to a different replica.
choices.explanation: The reader endpoint does not route individual SQL statements within an already established connection.

choices.text: Move the write connection to the reader endpoint and update a replica between each SELECT.
choices.explanation: This does not address read imbalance and does not meet the requirement to leave the write target unchanged.

choices.text: Keep one connection and shorten the DNS time to live so the existing connection automatically switches targets.
choices.explanation: Even if DNS information changes, an established TCP connection does not move to another DB instance.

source.label: Auroraリーダーエンドポイント

learning.reason: Determine whether load is distributed per SQL statement or per connection.
learning.concept: With only a few long-lived connections, connection-level distribution can still result in an uneven load.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Identify the SQL Behind a Spike in Waits Using Data
prompt: An API that uses RDS has become slow. DB CPU utilization was not high during the same period. Using the available CloudWatch Database Insights, you want to find the cause of the load, such as lock waits or I/O, and the SQL contributing to that load. What should you inspect?

choices.text: Look only at the DB instance's CPUUtilization and assume there are no DB waits if it is at its normal level.
choices.explanation: Sessions can wait on locks or I/O without using CPU, so CPU alone cannot rule out waits.

choices.text: Inspect only the CloudTrail ModifyDBInstance event and treat it as the SQL executed by the API.
choices.explanation: AWS resource management events do not provide a list of DB SQL statements contributing to load or the associated waits.

choices.text: Compare only the total number of DB connections and attribute all SQL at the time with the most connections to the same cause.
choices.explanation: Some connected sessions are inactive, so connection counts cannot identify the cause of load or wait time.

choices.text: Display DB Load by wait event for the incident period, then inspect the Top SQL contributing most during the same period.
choices.explanation: Aggregating active and waiting sessions helps identify what they are waiting on and which SQL is associated with the load.

source.label: CloudWatch Database Insightsのインスタンスダッシュボード

learning.reason: Distinguish CPU consumption from waits that block execution when investigating a cause.
learning.concept: Connect the types of waits with the SQL contributing to load over the same time window.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Execution Starts Successfully, but State Transitions Are Throttled
prompt: StartExecution succeeds for Step Functions Standard, and the dependent Lambda functions take their usual time to run. However, as you increase the number of workflows with many short states, state transitions are delayed. Which CloudWatch metric should you check to determine whether state transitions are being throttled?

choices.text: Check only ExecutionsFailed and count every execution in which a state transition was throttled.
choices.explanation: An execution does not necessarily fail even when state progress is delayed.

choices.text: Sum the Lambda Duration and use it as the number of times the state transition quota was exceeded.
choices.explanation: Lambda execution time does not directly count Step Functions state transition throttling.

choices.text: Check ExecutionThrottled.
choices.explanation: It counts throttled StateEntered events and retries, corresponding to state transition throttling.

choices.text: Use ExpressExecutionBilledDuration as a substitute for the Standard state transition limit.
choices.explanation: The Express billed duration metric is not used to measure the Standard state transition limit.

source.label: Step FunctionsのCloudWatchメトリクス

learning.reason: Observe API acceptance, dependent processing, and state transition throttling separately.
learning.concept: A delayed operation does not necessarily fail in the end.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Investigate Cache Engine CPU Load That a Host Average Can Hide
prompt: On a node-based ElastiCache for Valkey node with more than 4 vCPUs, CPUUtilization for the entire node is not high, but command responses slow down during periods of high load. Which metric should you check first to investigate engine CPU load rather than the entire host, including the OS and management processes?

choices.text: Check EngineCPUUtilization and compare it with host-wide CPUUtilization.
choices.explanation: An engine-focused CPU metric can reveal engine load even when the host-wide average looks normal.

choices.text: Average CPUUtilization over a longer period and treat it as the CPU utilization of a particular engine thread.
choices.explanation: Changing the averaging period does not narrow a host-wide metric to the engine.

choices.text: Monitor only NetworkBytesIn and convert it to the engine CPU percentage.
choices.explanation: Network bytes received do not show engine CPU utilization.

choices.text: Treat Evictions as a percentage of CPU.
choices.explanation: Evictions count keys removed due to conditions such as reaching a memory limit.

source.label: ElastiCacheのValkeyエンジンメトリクス

learning.reason: Distinguish engine utilization from utilization across the underlying host, even when both are CPU metrics.
learning.concept: A broad aggregate average can hide a constraint in a particular processing thread.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Page only when latency and errors worsen
prompt: Keep the CloudWatch metric alarms for latency and error rate. Their individual states must remain visible, but the on-call team should be paged only when both are in ALARM. How should this be configured without adding new instrumentation?

choices.text: Enable paging directly on both existing alarms, using the same notification target.
choices.explanation: This would also notify the team when only one alarm is in ALARM.

choices.text: Create a composite alarm that joins the two conditions with OR and treat it as requiring both.
choices.explanation: OR is satisfied when either condition is true.

choices.text: Add latency and error rate without normalizing their units, then notify only if the sum does not meet a threshold.
choices.explanation: A sum of different units does not show whether both existing alarm conditions are met.

choices.text: Create a composite alarm with an AND condition requiring both alarms to be in ALARM, and set the paging action on that composite alarm.
choices.explanation: This preserves the individual alarm states and notifies the team only when the combined condition is met.

source.label: CloudWatch複合アラーム

learning.reason: Keep each individual monitoring condition, then define the combination that triggers a notification separately.
learning.concept: A composite alarm can express an action condition based on the states of other alarms. Attach the paging action only to the composite alarm.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Verify the public path when no one is using it
prompt: Internal monitoring shows that the API is healthy, but problems occur only on the public HTTPS path used by customers. Even during the night, when no customers are visiting, you need to call a read-only test API on a schedule, check the expected status and response content, and notify someone if it fails. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch Synthetics canary to call the API on a schedule, check the result, and route failures to an alarm.
choices.explanation: This periodically checks the public path experienced by customers even when there is no real user traffic.

choices.text: Monitor only the number of errors reported by actual customers.
choices.explanation: If there are no customers during the night, errors on a broken path will not be observed.

choices.text: Use only EC2 status checks inside the origin.
choices.explanation: These check infrastructure health but do not test HTTPS on the public URL or the application's response content.

choices.text: Monitor only whether a DNS record exists and assume that the endpoint responds successfully.
choices.explanation: Name resolution alone does not verify TLS, HTTP, or the application's response.

source.label: CloudWatch Syntheticsカナリア

learning.reason: Exercise the required path with synthetic requests instead of relying on customer traffic.
learning.concept: DNS resolution and infrastructure health alone do not confirm the result customers receive.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Retries are increasing, but delivery is not necessarily lost
prompt: A transient error occurs at an EventBridge rule target. Monitoring shows an increase in RetryInvocationAttempts, but operations does not want to conclude that all events have permanently failed. Which statement correctly distinguishes retry attempts from final failures?

choices.text: Check RetryInvocationAttempts for transient retries and FailedInvocations for permanent invocation failures.
choices.explanation: These metrics distinguish the number of attempts made after failures from invocations that ultimately failed.

choices.text: Report RetryInvocationAttempts directly as the number of events that ultimately failed.
choices.explanation: The same delivery can be retried multiple times and may later succeed.

choices.text: Use only the ratio of MatchedEvents to RetryInvocationAttempts to determine each event's final outcome.
choices.explanation: Retry attempts and event counts are different quantities; the ratio alone does not give the number of permanent failures.

choices.text: Assume there were no retries during any period with SuccessfulInvocationAttempts.
choices.explanation: Some successful invocations may have succeeded after a retry.

source.label: EventBridgeのターゲット配信メトリクス

learning.reason: Separate activity during delivery from the final count of failed invocations.
learning.concept: The number of retries is not the number of events ultimately lost.

title: Retrying an aggregate write after a lost response
prompt: An inbound inventory process uses DynamoDB TransactWriteItems to create a receipt record and increment a quantity. The initial response is not received, and the same input will be retried a few seconds later. The quantity must be incremented only once regardless of the operation's outcome, and you do not want a separate lock item in DynamoDB. What should you specify?

choices.text: If no response arrives, retry the same data with a new request token.
choices.explanation: If the first attempt succeeded, the retry may be treated as a new operation and increment the quantity again.

choices.text: Set a fixed ID for the receipt process as ClientRequestToken and reuse it on the retry.
choices.explanation: Retrying the same write within the token's validity period does not apply the changes again.

choices.text: Set ReturnConsumedCapacity to TOTAL and query the caller for the result of the first attempt.
choices.explanation: This setting returns consumed capacity in a successful response; it cannot identify an operation whose response was lost.

choices.text: Keep ClientRequestToken unchanged on retry, but update the input timestamp to the current time.
choices.explanation: Changing the input while reusing the same token causes IdempotentParameterMismatch.

source.label: DynamoDB TransactWriteItems

learning.reason: Use the same token and the same request for the same logical operation.
learning.concept: During the 10-minute validity period, the token prevents the same write from being applied more than once.

title: Scope of the ordering guarantee for state changes
prompt: A team is replicating each product’s state to an external search system using DynamoDB Streams. Changes to different products do not need to be ordered, but consecutive changes to the same product—“received” followed by “published”—must be applied in that order. Someone proposed sorting all records by the writer’s timestamp. How should the ordering stored by Streams be used?

choices.text: Read only the latest NewImage and skip transitions from the previous state.
choices.explanation: This would not preserve the contract to apply each preceding state to the external system.

choices.text: Compare SequenceNumber values numerically across shards to reconstruct a table-wide order.
choices.explanation: Comparisons across shards do not provide a table-wide order.

choices.text: Sort all records by ApproximateCreationDateTime and use that timestamp as a unique, durable cursor.
choices.explanation: The timestamp is approximate, not a unique position; different changes can have the same value.

choices.text: Process changes to the same item in stream order, and leave ordering between items outside the application contract.
choices.explanation: Stream records for the same item are recorded in the same order as the changes.

source.label: DynamoDB Streams

learning.reason: Use the ordering guarantee of DynamoDB Streams at the item-key level.
learning.concept: Nearby change timestamps do not establish an ordering across different items.

title: List only the immediate folders and files
prompt: A customer management console needs to display one level at a time under each customer’s path in S3. It should show customer A’s invoice.pdf and monthly subfolders, without retrieving all files inside those subfolders. The target keys start with customer-a/. How should it call ListObjectsV2?

choices.text: Set Prefix to customer-a/ and Delimiter to /, then render Contents and CommonPrefixes separately.
choices.explanation: The response includes immediate keys and groups the keys up to the next delimiter position.

choices.text: Set StartAfter to customer-a/ and retrieve keys in sequence until reaching the next customer name.
choices.explanation: The immediate folders are not grouped, so this would read all keys in the subfolders.

choices.text: Set Prefix to customer-a/*/ to specify arbitrary levels with a wildcard.
choices.explanation: Prefix uses string prefix matching; an asterisk is not treated as a wildcard.

choices.text: Set MaxKeys to 1 and determine the delimiter position at the end of each key.
choices.explanation: Limiting the number of results does not group keys.

source.label: S3 ListObjectsV2

learning.reason: Use Prefix to narrow the path and Delimiter to group keys up to the next delimiter.
learning.concept: Contents and CommonPrefixes can display files and groups one level down.

title: Keep the existing cache and pass the viewer’s device to the origin
prompt: Images served through CloudFront return the same content on every device. At the origin, the team wants to record only the device class of requests that actually reach it on a cache miss. How can it forward the browser’s X-Device-Class header to the origin while preserving cache efficiency?

choices.text: Include the header in the cache key with a cache policy, and leave the origin request policy unchanged.
choices.explanation: The header reaches the origin, but the cache is split by device class.

choices.text: Set desktop as a fixed origin custom header in CloudFront.
choices.explanation: Every origin request would carry the same value, losing the classification sent by the viewer.

choices.text: Add a header with the same name using a response headers policy.
choices.explanation: That setting changes responses to viewers; it does not add the header to requests sent to the origin.

choices.text: Forward the header with an origin request policy and do not include it in the cache key with the cache policy.
choices.explanation: The header can be added to origin requests without increasing cache variations.

source.label: CloudFrontのキャッシュポリシーとオリジンリクエストポリシー

learning.reason: A header that does not change the response can be forwarded to the origin without adding it to the cache key.
learning.concept: Measuring requests that actually reach the origin differs from measuring views, including cache hits.

sourceLabel: CloudFront cache and origin request policies

title: Record expired asynchronous requests before they are discarded
prompt: A Lambda function runs asynchronously to send notifications based on 30-second aggregates. During an outage, processing events that have been in the internal queue for several minutes would send stale notifications. Events older than 2 minutes after acceptance, including the first attempt, should be excluded from processing, and the original requests should be investigated later. Which combination is appropriate? Select two.

choices.text: Set MaximumRetryAttempts to 2 and write only failures to the function’s CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: The retry count does not impose a 2-minute limit after acceptance, and the function cannot record events that expire before execution.

choices.text: Set MaximumEventAgeInSeconds to 120.
choices.explanation: Lambda marks asynchronous events that exceed the age limit for discarding.

choices.text: Set the Lambda function’s timeout to 120 seconds.
choices.explanation: This limits how long the function can run after execution starts; it does not limit time spent waiting in the queue.

choices.text: Configure an SQS queue for investigation as the OnFailure destination.
choices.explanation: It can receive invocation records, including those for events that could not be processed because they expired.

choices.text: Configure an OnSuccess destination and send all expired events there.
choices.explanation: Events that expire without being processed are not eligible for the success destination.

source.label: Lambda非同期呼び出しの設定

learning.reason: Configure how long events remain in the queue and where invocations that expire are sent.
learning.concept: If an event expires before execution starts, the function is never invoked, so the failure must be recorded externally.

title: Delay order handoff after enqueueing
prompt: Order requests are sent to an SQS FIFO queue to preserve order. As a cancellation grace period, every new message must wait 45 seconds before its first receive. The existing consumers must remain unchanged, and different delays per message are unnecessary. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Set DelaySeconds to 45 on every FIFO SendMessage request.
choices.explanation: FIFO queues do not support per-message delays.

choices.text: Set ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds to 20 and poll several times for new messages.
choices.explanation: Long polling waits for messages to become available; it does not delay delivery of individual messages.

choices.text: Set DelaySeconds to 45 on the FIFO queue.
choices.explanation: This sets a queue-level delivery delay, preventing a new message from being received immediately after it is sent.

choices.text: Set the FIFO queue's VisibilityTimeout to 45 seconds.
choices.explanation: This controls how long a received message remains hidden; it does not delay the first receive.

source.label: SQSの遅延キュー

learning.reason: The wait before delivery and the period a received message remains invisible while being processed are different settings.
learning.concept: A FIFO queue can have a queue-level delay, but it does not support per-message timers.

title: Route one undeliverable subscription to a dead-letter queue
prompt: An SNS topic has an email subscription and two SQS subscriptions. Because of a permissions change, notifications that SNS cannot deliver to one of the SQS queues are currently lost. Without changing the email subscription or the other SQS subscription, you want to retain the body of notifications SNS cannot deliver to the affected subscription in an investigation queue. Where should you configure this?

choices.text: Have the publisher inspect the success response from Publish and use it to determine whether each individual subscription received the message.
choices.explanation: A successful Publish response means SNS accepted the message; it does not confirm delivery to each subscription.

choices.text: Set the RedrivePolicy on the failing SNS subscription to point to an investigation SQS queue, and allow SNS to send messages to it.
choices.explanation: This routes failed deliveries to a dead-letter queue for that subscription, while the healthy subscriptions can continue without configuration changes.

choices.text: Enable only SNS delivery status logging and reconstruct the message body from the log entries.
choices.explanation: Delivery status logs help investigate results, but they do not retain the original undelivered message in a queue.

choices.text: Set only a RedrivePolicy on the destination SQS queue based on its receive-failure count.
choices.explanation: A message that never reached the SQS queue has no SQS receive count.

source.label: SNSのデッドレターキュー

learning.reason: SNS delivery failures are different from processing failures after a message has arrived in SQS.
learning.concept: A subscription's RedrivePolicy can retain messages that SNS cannot deliver to that subscription. Messages that SNS cannot deliver because of client-side errors, such as permission changes, are not retried and are sent directly to the subscription's dead-letter queue. For server-side errors, SNS retries delivery; messages that still cannot be delivered after all delivery retries are exhausted are sent to the dead-letter queue.

title: Preserve required results when only optional work fails
prompt: A Step Functions Parallel state runs a required inventory check and an optional promotion-data retrieval in parallel. Only when the promotion data cannot be retrieved because the provider times out, use an empty supplemental result. A failure in the inventory check must fail the entire workflow. Where should you catch the error?

choices.text: Add a States.ALL Catch only to the Parallel state and return an empty result, including for inventory.
choices.explanation: This would send the workflow down a success path even if the required inventory processing failed, and it would not provide a result for a promotion-data failure.

choices.text: Add a Catch for the relevant timeout to the promotion-data retrieval task and transition to a fallback that returns an empty result within the same branch.
choices.explanation: This handles the known failure locally in the promotion branch, while unhandled inventory errors still propagate.

choices.text: Configure Retry on the promotion task without a Catch.
choices.explanation: When retries are exhausted, the error propagates to Parallel, so the branch cannot return an empty supplemental result.

choices.text: Add the same States.ALL Catch to both branches and treat every failed branch as successful.
choices.explanation: This would also suppress inventory failures and misrepresent the outcome of the entire workflow.

source.label: Step Functions Parallelのエラー処理

learning.reason: Handle an error in the branch where omission is allowed, before it fails the entire Parallel state.
learning.concept: If the optional branch ends successfully with the agreed result format, Parallel can return its result alongside the required branch's result.

title: Publish aggregated results after the container exits
prompt: A Standard Step Functions workflow calls ECS Fargate RunTask to start an ETL job, then publishes its output in the next state. Currently, the workflow advances as soon as it starts the task and picks up an incomplete file. You want to wait for the task to finish without changing the container or adding a polling Lambda. Which integration should you use?

choices.text: Set the state's Resource to arn:aws:states:::ecs:runTask.sync and grant the execution role the permissions required by the integration.
choices.explanation: The optimized synchronous integration waits for the ECS task to finish.

choices.text: Insert a fixed 5-minute Wait state and assume Fargate will finish within 5 minutes.
choices.explanation: This does not synchronize with actual completion; if processing takes longer, the output is published too early.

choices.text: Specify runTask.waitForTaskToken to start the existing container, without making other changes.
choices.explanation: The callback pattern requires a process that receives the token to report completion.

choices.text: Use arn:aws:states:::ecs:runTask and treat a successful HTTP response from the start API as successful container completion.
choices.explanation: Acceptance of the launch request does not mean the task has finished.

source.label: Step FunctionsとECSの統合

learning.reason: A request-response integration and one that waits for job completion have different task-state completion conditions.
learning.concept: The optimized ECS integration can request that RunTask start a task and then wait for the task to finish.

title: Enrich stream records with an existing process before sending them to a queue
prompt: A DynamoDB Streams record contains an order ID for an update. Before delivery to SQS, an existing Lambda function must retrieve a receipt number from another system and add it to the message. Only INSERT events should be included. Which approach provides a single managed integration from filtering through delivery, without adding a continuously running worker?

choices.text: Connect DynamoDB Streams to SQS with Pipes, filter by event type, and configure the existing Lambda function as the enrichment step.
choices.explanation: Pipes can filter source records, invoke the Lambda function, and use its result as input to the target.

choices.text: Put the receipt number calculation in DynamoDB's ProjectionExpression and connect it to Streams.
choices.explanation: ProjectionExpression selects existing attributes; it cannot make an external call when a stream is generated.

choices.text: Put a calculation expression in an SQS message attribute and have SQS resolve it during delivery.
choices.explanation: SQS stores and delivers values but does not evaluate expressions that access external systems.

choices.text: Use an EventBridge rule input transformer to make an HTTP request to another system and retrieve the receipt number.
choices.explanation: An input transformer reshapes data by referencing existing input values; it does not make external requests.

source.label: Amazon EventBridge Pipes

learning.reason: Pipes connects source filtering, optional enrichment, and a target in sequence.
learning.concept: Distinguish transforming the input that was received from calculating or retrieving a value from an external system.

title: Pass the preceding lookup result to the next data source
prompt: In an AppSync pipeline resolver, the first function looks up a contract ID from a member ID, and the second function reads the usage limit for that contract ID. The client passes only the member ID, and the first function returns the contract ID. What should the second function's request reference?

choices.text: Read ctx.prev.result and use the returned contract ID as the key for the second data source.
choices.explanation: The value returned by the preceding pipeline step can be passed to the next function.

choices.text: Use ctx.identity for the caller of the GraphQL request as the contract ID for the data source.
choices.explanation: This represents information about the authenticated principal, not the contract ID returned by the first function.

choices.text: Read contractId from ctx.args and look it up using the value sent by the client.
choices.explanation: This API accepts only a member ID; the contract ID is not in the initial arguments.

choices.text: Read the first function's contract ID from ctx.result in the second function's request.
choices.explanation: Use prev.result to pass a result from the preceding function, and distinguish it from the current data source result.

source.label: AppSync JavaScriptのパイプラインリゾルバー

learning.reason: A step in a pipeline can access the response from the preceding step.
learning.concept: The client's initial arguments and values retrieved within a pipeline are in different contexts.

title: Transfer an unknown-length file without holding it all in memory
prompt: A Java application streams a generated file directly to S3, but its length is not known in advance. The current synchronous implementation reads the entire file into memory to calculate its length and stops when it reaches a size limit. Using the standard Java SDK v2 client, how can the application send the file without managing parts manually?

choices.text: Omit the length in fromContentProvider on the synchronous client and continue using the same approach.
choices.explanation: On the synchronous path, the SDK may buffer the entire stream to calculate its length.

choices.text: Enable multipart upload with S3AsyncClient and pass the stream in an AsyncRequestBody without specifying its length.
choices.explanation: The SDK manages the multipart upload, so the total size does not need to be calculated in advance.

choices.text: Specify an estimated Content-Length and send the data as is if the actual data is longer.
choices.explanation: If the length does not match the actual data, the upload may be truncated or fail.

choices.text: Save the entire output in a ByteArrayOutputStream during generation, then send it synchronously.
choices.explanation: Regardless of CDN or S3 settings, the memory required by the application increases with the size of the data.

source.label: Java SDKのS3ストリームアップロード

learning.reason: For an unknown-length stream, an asynchronous multipart upload can avoid buffering the entire stream in advance.
learning.concept: Distinguish synchronous uploads that require a known Content-Length from supported asynchronous uploads that do not specify a length.

title: Route commands separately over the same WebSocket connection
prompt: For a chat application, messages on the same WebSocket connection should be routed to a join handler when the JSON action is join, and to a send handler when it is send. You want to move the branching logic out of the Lambda function and into API Gateway routing, without adding connection URLs. What should you change?

choices.text: Create two $connect routes and compare each message's action.
choices.explanation: $connect is a dedicated route for establishing a connection; it does not run for each data frame.

choices.text: Register multiple integrations on $default and have them execute in order based on the message body.
choices.explanation: Selecting an integration per route requires configuring a route selection expression and route keys.

choices.text: Set the route selection expression to $request.body.action, use join and send as route keys, and assign an integration to each route.
choices.explanation: This routes messages sent to the same API to different integrations based on a value in the message body.

choices.text: Switch the HTTP method between POST and PUT for every message.
choices.explanation: Messages on an established WebSocket connection are not routed by HTTP method.

source.label: API Gateway WebSocketのルート

learning.reason: Match the value produced by the route selection expression to a route key.
learning.concept: The special routes for connecting and disconnecting are separate from selecting a route for each message.

title: Stop text generation at a specified delimiter
prompt: An internal summarization API uses Bedrock Converse. The model may generate a dedicated delimiter after the summary and then continue with unwanted notes. For a supported model, you want inference to stop as soon as the delimiter is generated, without relying only on application-side string truncation. What should you specify?

choices.text: Set maxTokens to the average token count of previous summaries.
choices.explanation: The required length varies by input, and this does not recognize the delimiter.

choices.text: Set the delimiter in Converse's inferenceConfig.stopSequences.
choices.explanation: A supported model treats the specified string as a stopping condition.

choices.text: Use only a system message to ask the model not to generate anything after the delimiter.
choices.explanation: This depends on the model's interpretation and does not define a stopping condition for the inference API.

choices.text: Lower topP to make words after the delimiter less likely through sampling.
choices.explanation: This changes the sampling range but does not ensure generation stops at the delimiter.

source.label: Bedrock InferenceConfiguration

learning.reason: stopSequences makes a specified string a condition for ending generation.
learning.concept: maxTokens and stopSequences stop generation for different reasons.

title: Use a validated prompt with only the input value changed
prompt: The team validated a template for generating product descriptions with Bedrock Prompt management. The deployed application must not be affected by edits to the draft in progress, and it must change only the product name on each run. Which fields should you specify in the Converse input? Select two.

choices.text: Set the value corresponding to the template's product-name variable in promptVariables.
choices.explanation: Using a variable lets you change only the input while keeping the definition fixed.

choices.text: Set the ARN of the validated prompt version in modelId.
choices.explanation: Specifying a version avoids dependence on draft updates.

choices.text: Append the product name to CloudWatch Logs, then invoke the same template without specifying a variable.
choices.explanation: A value written to monitoring logs is not passed as inference input.

choices.text: Keep the same model ID as before and leave the draft open in the Prompt management console.
choices.explanation: The application does not read the state of the editing screen.

choices.text: Copy the draft each time, expand the string in the application, and send it as the template ID.
choices.explanation: The result could change when the draft is edited, and the version is not fixed.

source.label: Bedrock Prompt managementの利用

learning.reason: Pin the version of the prompt definition being invoked, and pass the application's value as a variable.
learning.concept: Separating draft updates from promotion of the definition used in production makes it possible to track what is being used.

title: An aggregation condition that more examples alone may miss
prompt: In a Kiro Spec, you defined an invariant that splitting an order must preserve the original total across all line items. With three fixed examples, you missed a bug involving the combination of discounts and rounding. You want to repeatedly check the invariant for any valid input and obtain a small counterexample when a failure occurs. What should you add?

choices.text: Add the three failing orders from your local environment as one set of fixed regression tests.
choices.explanation: This protects known examples but does not explore the property across arbitrary orders.

choices.text: Measure only code coverage for Kiro implementation changes, without adding test inputs.
choices.explanation: Executing a line of code is different from proving the total condition holds across the input range.

choices.text: Generate the expected total automatically from the total returned by the current implementation.
choices.explanation: This would use the implementation's value as the baseline even when it is wrong, so it cannot detect violations of the total invariant.

choices.text: State total preservation as a correctness property in the Spec and implement a property-based test that generates valid orders.
choices.explanation: This evaluates the same assertion over diverse inputs, and the test framework can shrink a counterexample.

source.label: KiroのSpecと正しさのプロパティ

learning.reason: Represent the property that every valid input must satisfy in a test, rather than relying only on example inputs.
learning.concept: Randomized generation and counterexample shrinking can reproduce edge cases that fixed examples miss.

title: Restore access to the latest object without copying its data
prompt: A team member deleted an object without specifying a version ID in an S3 shared folder with versioning enabled. Immediately afterward, a normal GET returns 404, but an administrator confirms that the data version remains and only a new latest delete marker was added. What should you do to restore a normal GET for the original key without creating a new copy?

choices.text: Retrieve the original data and use PutObject to write it to the same key.
choices.explanation: This restores a normal GET but violates the requirement not to create a new data version.

choices.text: Call DeleteObject with the delete marker's version ID.
choices.explanation: This removes the marker, making the preceding data version retrievable again with a normal GET.

choices.text: Suspend versioning and retry the normal GET.
choices.explanation: Suspending versioning does not remove an existing delete marker.

choices.text: Delete the same key once more without specifying a version ID.
choices.explanation: This adds another delete marker, so the normal GET does not retrieve the object.

source.label: S3の削除マーカー管理

learning.reason: When the latest version is a delete marker, a normal GET treats the object as deleted.
learning.concept: Deleting the delete marker by version ID allows the earlier data version to be referenced as the current version.

title: Batch-resolving child fields in a list
prompt: An AppSync list displays 20 articles, and each article’s author field is resolved from the same Lambda data source. Currently, Lambda is invoked once per field. You can add batch support. How should you reduce the number of invocations while ensuring that an article with no matching author does not cause results for other articles to shift out of alignment?

choices.text: Use BatchInvoke in the author resolver, and have Lambda return results in the same order as the inputs. Include null at positions where no author is found.
choices.explanation: The inputs can be grouped, and results can be matched to their original articles by list position.

choices.text: Use BatchInvoke and have Lambda return only the authors it finds, sorted by author ID.
choices.explanation: The result length and order would no longer match the inputs, so results would not be matched to the correct articles.

choices.text: Increase Lambda provisioned concurrency for each article and cap the number of invocations at 20.
choices.explanation: This may reduce startup latency, but it does not combine field-level invocations.

choices.text: Keep using Invoke, extend the resolver timeout, and wait for all concurrent invocations to finish.
choices.explanation: Invocations would still occur one field at a time, so the required batching would not happen.

source.label: AppSync Lambda JavaScriptリゾルバーのBatchInvoke

learning.reason: BatchInvoke results must have the same length as the inputs and correspond to them at the same positions.
learning.concept: Omitting an input with no result can cause a result to be incorrectly matched to another field.

title: Retrying only failed entries in a batch
prompt: An ordering system publishes events to EventBridge in batches of 10 using PutEvents. The response has HTTP status 200, but some notifications are missing. How should the system identify only individual errors that are retryable and reduce the chance of resending notifications that succeeded?

choices.text: Treat only the last result as an aggregate for the entire batch and handle the batch based on its ErrorCode.
choices.explanation: Results correspond one-to-one with the inputs; the last entry does not contain the outcomes for the others.

choices.text: If FailedEntryCount is greater than zero, resend all 10 entries in the same order.
choices.explanation: Events that were registered successfully would also be resent, potentially causing duplicate target processing.

choices.text: Check FailedEntryCount and each result’s ErrorCode, then resend only retryable inputs at the same indexes as those results.
choices.explanation: Because input and result order correspond, partial failures in a batch operation can be handled individually.

choices.text: If the HTTP status is 200, treat all entries as successful and discard the data kept for retries.
choices.explanation: This would lose entries even when individual failures are returned.

source.label: EventBridge PutEventsの失敗処理

learning.reason: HTTP-level success and successful registration of each individual event are independent.
learning.concept: The correspondence between inputs and result entries lets you isolate only the failed entries.

title: Delivering the same body as separate business operations
prompt: With SQS FIFO, messages for the same customer must be delivered in order. Both messages are needed when their bodies are identical but they have different operation IDs in message attributes. The same operation ID can be used on a retry. Currently, content-based deduplication removes the second message. How should the sender be changed?

choices.text: Add the operation ID as an attribute only, and do not specify MessageDeduplicationId.
choices.explanation: Attributes are not included in the content-based hash, so identical bodies produce the same ID.

choices.text: Generate a new random MessageDeduplicationId for every send, including retries.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes separate operations, but retries of the same operation are not deduplicated.

choices.text: Set MessageDeduplicationId explicitly to the business operation ID, and reuse that value on retries of the same operation.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes separate operations with identical bodies and deduplicates retries of the same operation.

choices.text: Set MessageGroupId to a random value for each send.
choices.explanation: This breaks the requirement to preserve order in the same group for each customer, and leaves the body-based ID problem unchanged.

source.label: SQS FIFOの重複排除ID

learning.reason: A content-based ID is a hash of the message body and does not include attributes.
learning.concept: An explicit ID can represent business-level identity within the service’s deduplication scope.

title: Separating storage paths for users who share a role
prompt: Operations staff use a shared role. At sign-in, the trusted identity provider knows each user’s assigned Project ID. Uploads must be allowed only under projects/assigned-ID/ in an existing S3 bucket, and you do not want to create an IAM policy for each staff member. Which combination is required? Select two.

choices.text: Pass the assigned ID as a Project tag in the session from the trusted identity provider.
choices.explanation: The permission conditions can use a value managed by the issuer and tied to the session.

choices.text: Add a client-side naming convention to include the assigned ID in object keys, and let IAM allow the entire bucket.
choices.explanation: IAM would not restrict requests that do not follow the client-side convention.

choices.text: Use projects/${aws:PrincipalTag/Project}/* in the object ARN for the s3:PutObject Resource.
choices.explanation: This allows only objects under a path that matches the tag.

choices.text: Set the s3:PutObject Resource to the entire bucket and restrict it to projects/ by using s3:prefix.
choices.explanation: s3:prefix is a ListBucket list condition; it does not apply to PutObject resources.

choices.text: Refer only to s3:ResourceTag and set the bucket to each staff member’s assigned ID in turn.
choices.explanation: A tag shared by the bucket cannot map different sessions to different paths at the same time.

source.label: IAMポリシー変数

learning.reason: A trusted session tag can be referenced as part of a resource path.
learning.concept: Both permission to set tags and permission to operate on the corresponding paths must be controlled.

title: Explicitly separate key administrators from cryptographic operators
prompt: A new customer managed KMS key is being created. The initial permissions for the key administrator should allow key usage updates and operational management, while only the application role may encrypt and decrypt data. The administrator's normal session must not be able to use cryptographic APIs. How should this be designed?

choices.text: Grant only kms:DescribeKey to both roles and specify the key ARN in the application.
choices.explanation: Being able to describe the key does not authorize cryptographic operations.

choices.text: Grant only kms:PutKeyPolicy to the application and have it proxy cryptographic operations using the administrator's permissions.
choices.explanation: This does not limit the principal performing cryptographic operations to the application and gives the application overly broad permissions.

choices.text: Grant kms:* to the key administrator and put a separate statement granting cryptographic operations only to the application.
choices.explanation: kms:* includes Encrypt and Decrypt, so the administrator could use them in a normal session.

choices.text: Grant key management operations in an administrator statement and the required cryptographic operations in a separate application statement.
choices.explanation: This grants ordinary key operations and application encryption and decryption to separate principals.

source.label: KMSキーポリシーの既定の構造

learning.reason: Key management APIs and cryptographic APIs for data use are separate permissions.
learning.concept: Because permission to edit the key policy can change permissions later, distinguish routine separation of duties from controls over privileged changes.

sourceLabel: Default structure of a KMS key policy

title: Apply sign-out revocation to a custom JWT validation flow
prompt: When a user of a Cognito user pool signs out, access to a custom API from the same device must be denied immediately, even if the JWT still has time before expiration. The API locally validates the JWT signature, issuer, and expiration using a library. In addition to revoking the token in the authentication system, what should the API do?

choices.text: Add a tolerance period to exp on the API side to account for clock differences with Cognito.
choices.explanation: This change treats the token as valid for longer and does not check revocation immediately after sign-out.

choices.text: Retrieve Cognito's JWT signing key again and wait for the revoked token's signature to become invalid automatically.
choices.explanation: Revoking an individual session does not change the public signing key.

choices.text: When authorizing a request to the custom API, check a session record for the revocation status of the relevant session or token.
choices.explanation: This detects revocation after sign-out in addition to local signature validation.

choices.text: Additionally verify only the ID token's signature, and allow access if both signatures are valid.
choices.explanation: Even two valid signatures do not indicate whether the relevant session has been revoked.

source.label: Cognitoのトークン失効

learning.reason: After a JWT is revoked, signature and expiration checks alone do not reveal its revocation status.
learning.concept: Custom authorization needs a mechanism to check the current session state.

title: Issue access tokens that reflect subscription status
prompt: A Cognito user pool can use a V2_0 pre token generation trigger. For a user whose subscription has expired, the access token should be issued without reports/read among the scopes requested by the app client. Only the server can update subscription status. What should be configured?

choices.text: Define reports/read on the resource server and ask the client to remove it itself when the user has no active subscription.
choices.explanation: This trusts the client's request and provides no subscription check by the token issuer.

choices.text: Remove the email claim from the user's ID token.
choices.explanation: The reports/read scope in an access token is separate from the email claim in an ID token.

choices.text: Read the subscription only in a Post confirmation trigger and make no changes to later tokens.
choices.explanation: A process that runs only when a user is confirmed does not reflect later subscription changes when issuing tokens.

choices.text: Check the subscription in the V2_0 trigger and add reports/read to accessTokenGeneration.scopesToSuppress for the user.
choices.explanation: This excludes the specified scope from the access token in that issuance response.

source.label: Cognito事前トークン生成のLambdaトリガー

learning.reason: Control which scopes are included in an access token on the server side at token issuance.
learning.concept: The API should separately check the granted scopes and take any required action for already issued tokens when a subscription changes.

sourceLabel: Cognito pre token generation Lambda trigger

title: KMS conditions when enabling an S3 Bucket Key
prompt: The SSE-KMS policy for an audit bucket allows the bucket's object ARNs through the aws:s3:arn encryption context. New writes are denied by KMS when an S3 Bucket Key is enabled. Existing objects must remain readable, and access must not be expanded to other buckets. Which conditions should be adopted?

choices.text: Add the bucket's own ARN to the existing permissions and retain the existing object ARN conditions.
choices.explanation: This can allow operations using a Bucket Key as well as operations using the previous object context.

choices.text: Remove all KMS conditions and allow all use from the same IAM role.
choices.explanation: This expands access to other uses and no longer limits the bucket through the encryption context.

choices.text: Remove the existing object ARN conditions and use only the bucket's ARN.
choices.explanation: This removes a condition required for previously encrypted objects and prevents continued reads of existing data.

choices.text: Keep only the object ARN conditions and specify a different Region for the bucket in PutObject.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the change in encryption context to the bucket ARN.

source.label: S3バケットキーと暗号化コンテキスト

learning.reason: With S3 Bucket Keys, the bucket ARN is used in the encryption context.
learning.concept: Account for both the object ARN used for existing data and the bucket ARN used for new data.

sourceLabel: S3 Bucket Keys and encryption context

title: Reject uploads that explicitly use a different key
prompt: The audit bucket uses customer managed KMS key K for default encryption. Senders may omit the encryption headers and use the default, but writes that explicitly select a different key or encryption method must not be accepted. In addition to the bucket default, which control should be used?

choices.text: Change the bucket’s object ownership setting to Bucket owner enforced.
choices.explanation: This controls object ownership and ACLs; it does not prevent encryption settings from being overridden.

choices.text: Use a bucket policy to explicitly deny s3:PutObject unless the encryption headers are completely omitted or both the method aws:kms and the ARN for key K match.
choices.explanation: Check both the encryption method and key ARN. Sending only aws:kms could select an AWS managed key, so that combination must also be denied.

choices.text: Set K as the default encryption key and simply ignore any encryption settings sent by clients.
choices.explanation: A default does not prevent a request from overriding it with an explicit setting.

choices.text: For every PutObject request, deny it when the key ID header is Null is true.
choices.explanation: This would also reject valid writes that omit the header and use the default setting.

source.label: S3のSSE-KMSとバケットポリシー

learning.reason: Separate the conditions for using the default settings from those for a caller explicitly specifying encryption requirements.
learning.concept: Distinguish between both headers being absent, both being specified, and only one being specified.

title: An organization-wide deny takes precedence over an allowed role action
prompt: In an Organizations member account, you granted a CI role application-related creation permissions. To prevent IAM users from being created in this environment, the security team added an explicit deny for iam:CreateUser in the parent OU’s SCP. What happens if you later add an Allow for the same action to the IAM role?

choices.text: The user still cannot be created because the parent OU’s explicit SCP deny applies despite the role’s Allow.
choices.explanation: The explicit deny in the organization hierarchy applies and cannot be overridden within the member account.

choices.text: Granting service-specific permissions to the role overrides the organization’s deny because it is a general rule.
choices.explanation: The specificity of an Allow does not invalidate an explicit deny.

choices.text: Renaming the role to OrganizationAccountAccessRole automatically exempts it from the SCP.
choices.explanation: There is no rule that exempts an ordinary IAM role in a member account from an SCP based on its name.

choices.text: Pass an Allow for the same action to the session using the role; the role’s SCP restrictions will not carry over.
choices.explanation: A session policy can restrict permissions, but it cannot allow an action denied by an SCP.

source.label: AWS Organizations SCPの評価

learning.reason: An explicit organization-level deny takes precedence over identity-based permissions in a member account.
learning.concept: If the organization is to allow an action, check both the applicable policy ceiling and the permissions granted to the role.

title: Cache a secret briefly without embedding it in the function
prompt: A Lambda function reads a Secrets Manager database secret on every request, and the retrieval call adds latency. The existing handler can call a general-purpose HTTP client. You want to keep the secret out of the ZIP package and environment variables, and briefly cache the retrieved value only within the execution environment using an official extension. What should you configure?

choices.text: Add the AWS Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension, allow the execution role to retrieve the secret, and use the extension’s local endpoint.
choices.explanation: This uses a cache within the execution environment without including the secret in the deployment artifact.

choices.text: Read the secret at build time and include a plaintext JSON file in a Lambda layer.
choices.explanation: This stores the secret in the artifact and requires redeployment when the secret changes.

choices.text: Set the secret value as a function environment variable.
choices.explanation: This stores the secret’s contents in an environment variable, which does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Add the secret value as a response header in the API Gateway integration and pass it to Lambda.
choices.explanation: This moves the value through an unnecessary path and does not provide caching within the execution environment.

source.label: LambdaのSecrets Manager利用

learning.reason: The extension retrieves the value using the execution role and caches it within the execution environment.
learning.concept: Configure the TTL to balance how long an old value can be used after rotation against retrieval latency.

title: Restrict access to one file by expiration and source network
prompt: A training company has a fixed IPv4 range for its dedicated-line egress. You want to provide a URL for a single CloudFront file for just 10 minutes. The URL will be issued to users by an application, and knowing the URL alone must not allow retrieval from outside the company’s range. Which method should you use?

choices.text: Create a signed URL with a canned policy and state the permitted CIDR in the application’s explanatory text.
choices.explanation: The canned policy enforces an expiration, but this approach does not check the source network.

choices.text: Restrict origin access to CloudFront only and issue unsigned distribution URLs.
choices.explanation: This does not restrict the viewer’s expiration or source network when accessing CloudFront.

choices.text: Add the viewer’s country code to the CloudFront cache key.
choices.explanation: Separating the cache does not control access based on the company’s IPv4 network.

choices.text: Set the target file as the resource and create a signed URL with a custom policy containing an expiration and an IpAddress condition.
choices.explanation: CloudFront checks the viewer’s IPv4 range and can deny use from outside that range.

source.label: CloudFrontのカスタムポリシー付き署名URL

learning.reason: A CloudFront custom signed policy can enforce both an expiration and an IPv4 source address.
learning.concept: The versioned URL, expiration, and permitted network can all be included in the signed policy.

sourceLabel: CloudFront signed URLs with custom policies

title: Narrow an existing role’s broad permissions using observed activity
prompt: An existing Lambda function has broad AWS permissions, and CloudTrail contains records of its planned normal operations. As an initial review proposal, you want to create an IAM policy based on the operations this role recently used, then separately validate an unexecuted failure-recovery path. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Use the IAM policy simulator to put every operation currently allowed by the permissions into a new policy.
choices.explanation: Listing allowed operations does not narrow them to operations that were actually used.

choices.text: Specify the target role and a CloudTrail activity period in IAM Access Analyzer policy generation, then review the generated candidate.
choices.explanation: This produces a policy template based on observed AWS activity.

choices.text: Retrieve the Lambda Invocations metric from CloudWatch and reduce permissions based on its invocation count.
choices.explanation: A total invocation count does not identify downstream service API actions.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer policy validation to inspect the current policy as is.
choices.explanation: It can report syntax issues and best-practice findings, but it does not extract operations that were executed.

source.label: IAM Access Analyzerのポリシー生成

learning.reason: A candidate least-privilege policy can be generated from CloudTrail activity.
learning.concept: This does not cover tasks that were not performed during the audit period; validation and supplementation are required.

title: Attribute actions across shared roles to the originating user
prompt: A user signs in through the corporate identity system and assumes an IAM role, then switches to a shared role in another account. For auditing, you want to associate the immutable ID of the originally authenticated user with actions under both roles, rather than relying only on a shared session name. The identity system has a trusted ID. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Write the ID of the last user who acted to each resource as a tag.
choices.explanation: Concurrent actions can overwrite the tag, and it cannot attribute individual CloudTrail actions.

choices.text: Use the same fixed name, production, for the RoleSessionName in each AssumeRole call.
choices.explanation: This identifies an environment, not an individual user.

choices.text: Record the user ID in the first Lambda function’s CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: It does not carry the session identity into subsequent actions in the other account.

choices.text: Set and require SourceIdentity on the initial role, allow sts:SetSourceIdentity in the trust for the chained role, and verify it in CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: The source identity for actions is retained in the session after the role switch.

source.label: IAMロールのソースIDと監査

learning.reason: SourceIdentity set with AssumeRole persists through subsequent role chaining.
learning.concept: The auditing ID should be guaranteed by the trust policy and identity system, and distinguished from a freely entered name.

sourceLabel: IAM role source identity and auditing

title: Protect post-connection application actions with a separate authorization boundary
prompt: With an API Gateway WebSocket API, users are authenticated when they connect, and messages are then allowed on a per-destination-channel basis. Channel permissions can also be revoked while a connection is active. What should you do instead of attaching a custom Lambda authorizer to every message route?

choices.text: Authenticate at $connect, associate the user with the connection ID, and have the message integration check channel permissions at the time of each action.
choices.explanation: This separates identity at connection time from business authorization that can change dynamically.

choices.text: Add the sender’s ID to the message body without verifying its association with the connection ID.
choices.explanation: Input in the message body alone does not verify that the action came from the user authenticated on the connection.

choices.text: Register the same Lambda authorizer on each custom route and remove the permission check from the integration.
choices.explanation: A WebSocket API Lambda authorizer cannot be applied to individual messages in this way.

choices.text: Use the channel list allowed at $connect and never reread permissions after that point.
choices.explanation: This cannot reject actions after a user loses permission while connected.

source.label: API Gateway WebSocketのLambdaオーソライザー

learning.reason: A WebSocket Lambda authorizer can be used only at connection time.
learning.concept: Separate connection authentication from authorization for individual business actions during the connection.

title: Correct the IAM connection ARN so it identifies the actual DB
prompt: IAM database authentication is enabled for RDS PostgreSQL, and the required database-side configuration for the DB user reporting is complete. After generating a token, a connection using the same user is denied. The rds-db:connect ARN contains the DB instance name shown in the management console. What should you correct?

choices.text: Change the service name in the IAM policy to rds and allow rds:DescribeDBInstances.
choices.explanation: Being able to view DB information does not grant database connection permission.

choices.text: Use DbiResourceId and reporting in the dbuser resource for rds-db:connect.
choices.explanation: These match the internal RDS resource ID and DB user checked for connection permission.

choices.text: Set the application IAM role name as the dbuser in the ARN.
choices.explanation: The final component is the PostgreSQL login user name, not the IAM role name.

choices.text: Keep the DB instance name and change only the TCP port when generating the token.
choices.explanation: The resource ARN checked by IAM remains unchanged, and using a different port also breaks the connection settings.

source.label: RDS IAMデータベース認証のポリシー

learning.reason: The ARN for IAM database connection uses the immutable DB resource ID and DB user name.
learning.concept: The display instance identifier, endpoint, and DbiResourceId are different values.

title: Preventing unintended public access when saving a policy
prompt: An organization deploys resource policies for Secrets Manager. Sharing with specified roles outside the organization is required by an existing process, but the update operation itself must reject policies that grant broad public access, such as through a wildcard. What should be added?

choices.text: Verify the specific principals being granted access and set BlockPublicPolicy to true in PutResourcePolicy.
choices.explanation: This checks the scope of public access during the update and prevents a broadly permissive policy from being saved.

choices.text: Move all secrets to a different KMS key and skip policy validation.
choices.explanation: Selecting an encryption key does not prevent a broadly permissive resource policy from being registered.

choices.text: Configure CloudTrail to notify administrators about PutResourcePolicy and have them search the logs the next day.
choices.explanation: This helps detect the change, but a policy with broad access could remain effective temporarily.

choices.text: Shorten the automatic rotation interval in Secrets Manager and register the public policy as is.
choices.explanation: Rotating credentials does not change the scope of the access permissions.

source.label: Secrets Managerのリソースポリシー

learning.reason: BlockPublicPolicy can reject a resource policy that grants broad access.
learning.concept: Evaluate sharing with explicitly permitted roles separately from grants whose scope is too broad.

title: Processing only the intended function from a queue in another account
prompt: A Lambda function in account A processes an unencrypted SQS queue in account B in the same Region as an event source. The function's execution role in A is allowed to call ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage, and GetQueueAttributes on the target queue. What additional permission must B add?

choices.text: In B's queue policy, allow A's execution role to perform the required operations on the target queue.
choices.explanation: With permissions on both the execution role and the SQS resource, the event source can process the queue.

choices.text: Remove every Allow statement from B's queue policy and rely only on the execution role in A.
choices.explanation: A cross-account request would then lack the required permission on the SQS side.

choices.text: Grant lambda:InvokeFunction to A's function ARN in B's queue policy.
choices.explanation: Adding that permission to the queue policy does not grant A permission to read from SQS.

choices.text: Allow only the SQS service principal to invoke A's function.
choices.explanation: With this event source, Lambda reads the queue; SQS is not configured to invoke the function directly.

source.label: LambdaのSQSイベントソースマッピング

learning.reason: Cross-account access to SQS also requires permission on the queue itself.
learning.concept: When Lambda polls a queue, that differs from granting SQS permission to invoke the function directly.

title: Allowing only an internal batch to update data in a public schema
prompt: An internal AppSync API uses Cognito to authenticate users who read data. AWS_IAM is already configured as an additional authorization mode. A batch process has an IAM execution role and should be allowed to call only a specific Mutation. Keep the existing read access for regular users, and do not allow the batch role to access other API fields. Which settings are appropriate? Select TWO.

choices.text: Store a shared Cognito user password for the batch process and allow it to access every field.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the field-level least-privilege requirement or the requirement to use the batch process's existing IAM role.

choices.text: Grant the role only appsync:StartSchemaCreation.
choices.explanation: This operation is for schema creation; it does not authorize GraphQL Mutation execution.

choices.text: Authorize the target Mutation with @aws_iam in the schema, and apply the same authorization to the fields needed in the returned type.
choices.explanation: The IAM-signed request can access the target field and the required values in its return type.

choices.text: Restrict the execution role's appsync:GraphQL permission to the ARN of the target Mutation field.
choices.explanation: This limits the GraphQL operations available to the role to only the fields it needs.

choices.text: Change the default authorization mode to API_KEY and give the same key to the batch process and all users.
choices.explanation: This would not preserve existing user authentication or limit the batch process's access.

source.label: AppSyncの認証と認可

learning.reason: Combine an additional authorization mode with schema-level authorization scope and IAM permissions for API fields.
learning.concept: Adding IAM authorization to an API still allows the role's permissions to be limited to specific fields.

title: Isolating a sensitive child path in a shared settings tree
prompt: An application needs permission to recursively retrieve parameters under /app/team in Parameter Store. It must not receive settings under /app/team/secret that are used by another system.
