In a test combining GetParametersByPath permission on the parent path with a denial on the child path, recursively retrieving from the parent enumerated the child parameters. What design should be used instead?

choices.text: Keep recursive retrieval on the parent path allowed and explicitly deny only GetParameter on the child path.
choices.explanation: This does not change the scope of parameters available through GetParametersByPath on the parent path.

choices.text: Require the application to set WithDecryption to false and give it the same IAM permissions.
choices.explanation: This relies on the caller rather than path-based authorization and does not protect secret names or unencrypted values.

choices.text: Change SecureString parameters to String to simplify encryption settings.
choices.explanation: Changing the data type does not change the recursive path scope and removes encryption protection.

choices.text: Move application settings and sensitive settings to separate paths that are not ancestors or descendants of each other, and allow the application to recursively retrieve only from its dedicated path.
choices.explanation: Sensitive parameters are then outside the scope expanded by recursive retrieval.

source.label: Parameter Storeの階層アクセス制御

learning.reason: Do not place sensitive parameters that the application must not retrieve beneath a parent path it can retrieve recursively.
learning.concept: Separate the hierarchies for accessible and sensitive settings, and grant recursive retrieval only from the intended root path.

title: Pin the Code and Configuration Used for QA
prompt: A Lambda function’s $LATEST version is shared, and the operations team publishes it after QA approval. While QA is in progress, another developer may update the code or environment variables, causing the production version to differ from what was approved. Pin the version used at the start of QA so that production points to that version only when it is published. What should you do?

choices.text: Do not publish a version until QA is complete; after approval, publish the current configuration for the first time.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent the version being published from changing during QA.

choices.text: Point both QA and production to the unqualified function ARN, then use the current $LATEST after approval.
choices.explanation: A separate deployment can change $LATEST, so it cannot guarantee a match with the approved content.

choices.text: Publish a version before QA, test using that version’s ARN, and after approval update the production alias to the same version number.
choices.explanation: This directs production to the exact code and configuration that were tested.

choices.text: Pin only the Lambda layer version at the start of QA, and test the function code from $LATEST.
choices.explanation: Pinning the layer does not prevent the function code or configuration from changing.

source.label: Lambdaの関数バージョン

learning.reason: A published version pins the code being tested and its version-specific configuration.
learning.concept: Use mutable $LATEST for development and a production alias that is explicitly promoted.

title: Trigger Only for Pull Requests Targeting a Specific Branch
prompt: You want CodeBuild integrated with GitHub to run automated tests only when a pull request targeting main is created or updated. It must not run for a direct push to main or for a pull request targeting any other branch. What should you configure in the webhook?

choices.text: Set EVENT to PUSH only, and filter HEAD_REF to main.
choices.explanation: This targets direct pushes; it does not cover pull request creation or updates.

choices.text: Set the pull request events and ^refs/heads/main$ for HEAD_REF in the same group.
choices.explanation: HEAD_REF is the pull request’s source branch, so it cannot specify that the target is main.

choices.text: In the same filter group, set EVENT to PULL_REQUEST_CREATED and PULL_REQUEST_UPDATED, and set BASE_REF to ^refs/heads/main$.
choices.explanation: This runs tests for pull request creation and updates only when the base branch is main.

choices.text: Put the pull request events and the BASE_REF condition in separate filter groups.
choices.explanation: The build starts if either group matches, so this cannot require both conditions.

source.label: CodeBuildのGitHubウェブフックイベント

learning.reason: Evaluate the pull request’s target branch with BASE_REF and combine it with the event types in the same filter group.
learning.concept: The source branch and the pull request target are independent conditions.

title: Pass Artifacts to an Action in Another Region in the Same Pipeline
prompt: A CodePipeline pipeline in Tokyo builds an application, then runs a corresponding deployment action in Osaka in the same account. The pipeline uses only an artifact store in Tokyo. What changes are required to pass the build artifact to Osaka within the same pipeline? Select two.

choices.text: Create an artifact S3 bucket in Osaka in the same account, and register it as the Osaka entry in artifactStores.
choices.explanation: This defines the Region-specific store for artifacts passed to the action.

choices.text: Configure only one artifactStore in Tokyo, and set both actions’ Region to Tokyo.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to run the action in Osaka.

choices.text: Create an S3 bucket with the same name in Osaka, but do not register it in artifactStores.
choices.explanation: CodePipeline does not infer an unconfigured cross-Region store from its name.

choices.text: Set the Osaka Region in the definition of the action that runs there.
choices.explanation: CodePipeline then runs that action in a Region different from the one where the build runs.

choices.text: Make the Tokyo artifact bucket public and point the Osaka action configuration to its URL.
choices.explanation: This does not meet CodePipeline’s Region-specific store configuration requirement and exposes the artifact.

source.label: CodePipelineのクロスリージョンアクション

learning.reason: The pipeline uses an artifact store in each Region where an action runs.
learning.concept: Match the action’s execution Region with the Region of its input artifact store.

title: Reproduce a Specific Commit Without Moving the Branch Head
prompt: A CodePipeline pipeline normally uses the latest commit on main. To investigate an issue from a few days ago, you want to manually run the pipeline once with a specific commit from the existing CodeCommit source action, without moving the Git branch head. What should you specify?

choices.text: In StartPipelineExecution, specify the source action name, revisionType of COMMIT_ID, and the actual commit ID in sourceRevisions.
choices.explanation: This explicitly selects the revision that the source action retrieves for this execution.

choices.text: After the CodeBuild action completes, change the deployment tag name to the commit ID.
choices.explanation: Changing the tag does not change the contents of a build artifact created from a different commit.

choices.text: Give the execution the same name as before, omit the source revision, and assume that the same artifact will be retrieved.
choices.explanation: The default source follows the current configuration; it does not retrieve a past commit based on the execution name.

choices.text: Set the pipeline execution ID to the same string as the Git commit ID, then retrieve main as usual.
choices.explanation: The execution ID is not associated with the source revision that is retrieved.

source.label: CodePipelineのソース改訂の指定

learning.reason: Specifying the source revision at execution time lets you select a commit without moving a mutable repository reference.
learning.concept: The pipeline execution ID, source action name, and Git commit ID are different values.

title: Wait until every launched instance finishes initialization
prompt: Create a new Auto Scaling group with two EC2 instances in CloudFormation. After the group is created, each instance's User Data continues installing dependent packages. The stack must not be marked complete until both instances are initialized, and it must fail if the deadline is exceeded. Which combination should you use? Select TWO.

choices.text: Add a fixed sleep to User Data and do not use a CreationPolicy.
choices.explanation: The stack does not use the end of a fixed wait or actual initialization success as its completion condition.

choices.text: After initialization has a definite result on each instance, send that result to the group with cfn-signal.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation can receive the actual initialization result.

choices.text: Use CloudFormation DependsOn to create the group after a separate S3 bucket is created.
choices.explanation: This specifies only resource creation order; it does not check each instance's initialization result.

choices.text: Attach a CreationPolicy with ResourceSignal to the Auto Scaling group, set the required count to 2, and set the timeout to the operational limit.
choices.explanation: The number of successful signals can be made a condition for completing resource creation.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy to Retain for failures.
choices.explanation: This controls deletion behavior and does not evaluate the number of successful initializations.

source.label: CloudFormation CreationPolicy

learning.reason: Infrastructure creation state and successful application initialization must be checked separately.
learning.concept: Define the required number of ResourceSignal signals and the wait time, then let initialization processes report success.

title: Check for manual changes before deployment
prompt: You have been told that a stack you inherited includes console changes made during operations. Before the next deployment, you want to see whether explicitly specified properties on resources supported by CloudFormation match the live environment. What should you run without changing any resources?

choices.text: Filter CloudTrail for UpdateStack events only, and conclude that there were no manual changes if none are recorded.
choices.explanation: A console change that directly calls a resource's own API is not recorded as UpdateStack.

choices.text: Start drift detection, then, when it completes, compare the actual and expected values for drifted resources.
choices.explanation: This lets you investigate differences from the definition for managed resources without applying changes.

choices.text: Validate the current template to check only whether the template itself is valid.
choices.explanation: Template validation does not inspect the live values of running resources.

choices.text: Create another stack from the current template in a test account and treat successful creation as proof that the original environment matches.
choices.explanation: Successful creation in a different environment reveals nothing about the actual values in the original environment.

source.label: CloudFormationのドリフト検出

learning.reason: Differences between live resources and the current stack definition should be examined separately from a change set against the next version.
learning.concept: Drift detection covers supported resource types and properties whose values are specified in the definition.

title: Verify HTTP method and Lambda event routing locally
prompt: Send GET and POST requests from the frontend's actual HTTP client to a local API defined with SAM. You want to verify, without deploying to the cloud, that each route reaches the correct Lambda function and is converted into an HTTP response. Which tool should you use?

choices.text: If you can run sam local invoke directly on each handler, use that instead of testing the routes over HTTP.
choices.explanation: A direct invocation cannot verify which function receives an HTTP request from the frontend.

choices.text: Run sam validate and treat a parseable template as confirmation that the client can communicate with the API.
choices.explanation: Template validation does not execute requests and responses.

choices.text: Run sam package to put the artifacts in S3, then send GET and POST requests to the S3 object URLs.
choices.explanation: The artifact storage location does not provide API Gateway-compatible routing for the local API.

choices.text: Start the app with the API defined in the SAM template by running sam local start-api, then send requests from the client to each local URL.
choices.explanation: The SAM CLI provides HTTP endpoints and invokes the functions mapped to the routes.

source.label: SAM CLIのローカルAPIサーバー

learning.reason: The local HTTP server connects the SAM API definition to Lambda.
learning.concept: Distinguish checking a single function invocation from testing through multiple HTTP routes.

title: Separate release files and internal diagnostics from one build
prompt: CodeBuild generates a binary and internal debug symbols. Downstream CodePipeline actions must validate and deploy only the distribution binary, while a separate downstream action stores the debug symbols internally. Which configuration passes them as two separately named artifacts without rerunning the build?

choices.text: Register both filenames as environment variables and have downstream actions reference the CodeBuild working directory directly.
choices.explanation: Files are not automatically carried over to a separate execution environment.

choices.text: Save both files in the CodeBuild cache and specify their names in the downstream deployment process.
choices.explanation: The cache is for speeding up builds; it does not create named pipeline artifacts.

choices.text: Put both files in one ZIP and specify the same artifact for each downstream action.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to deploy and store them as two independent artifacts.

choices.text: Use secondary-artifacts in the buildspec to specify an identifier and files for each set, and match the CodePipeline output artifact names.
choices.explanation: This passes each downstream process its required build artifacts independently.

source.label: CodeBuildの成果物とsecondary-artifacts

learning.reason: One build can assign its generated files to different artifact sets.
learning.concept: Align each build artifact identifier with the artifact name passed as input to the downstream action.

title: Use a different endpoint only for CI with the same environment variable
prompt: The shared buildspec sets APP_STAGE=test. A dedicated CodeBuild project sets APP_STAGE=preprod, and for this run only, APP_STAGE=staging was supplied as an override through the StartBuild API. The shell does not set the same variable again. Which value will this run's command read?

choices.text: preprod. The project is defined outside the source, so it takes precedence over the API override.
choices.explanation: The project definition takes precedence over the buildspec, but not over the StartBuild override.

choices.text: staging. The StartBuild override has the highest precedence.
choices.explanation: The value specified for this particular run is used.

choices.text: All three values are concatenated with a delimiter, and the application chooses one.
choices.explanation: There is no rule for combining values of the same environment variable; one value is selected.

choices.text: test. The buildspec is read after the environment is set up, so it always takes precedence.
choices.explanation: A definition in the buildspec's env section has lower precedence than a project value or a value supplied at start time.

source.label: CodeBuildの環境変数の優先順位

learning.reason: An override supplied when a build starts takes precedence over both the project definition and the buildspec.
learning.concept: Treat per-run overrides, project settings, and file defaults as separate layers.

title: Notify an existing change log when configuration deployment completes
prompt: A feature configuration is deployed gradually with AppConfig. The existing change log should record the environment ID and deployment ID only when the deployment finishes, not during the test phase or when it starts. The application that reads the configuration values must remain unchanged. Which combination should you use?

choices.text: Add the change log update URL to the configuration's JSON Schema validator.
choices.explanation: Schema validation does not notify you when a deployment completes.

choices.text: Record deployment completion when the configuration is committed to the code repository.
choices.explanation: A commit does not prove that the AppConfig gradual deployment has finished.

choices.text: Detect successful GetLatestConfiguration calls in each application instance and write to the same log each time.
choices.explanation: A client fetching configuration does not mean the deployment is complete. This would also require modifying the application and could create duplicate records.

choices.text: Associate an AppConfig extension that calls a log-update Lambda at the ON_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETE action point.
choices.explanation: This hooks into the completion lifecycle and records the deployment without depending on the application fetching the configuration.

source.label: AWS AppConfigの拡張機能

learning.reason: The configuration deployment lifecycle has an action point for handling deployment completion.
learning.concept: Configuration retrieval by an application can be separated from deployment-completion notifications for operational workflows.

title: Resolve a conflict between an existing unmanaged file and a deployed file
prompt: During an EC2 in-place deployment with CodeDeploy, a configuration file left by a previous manual installation is present on the deployment target. From now on, the files in the revision are authoritative, and an existing file with the same name should be replaced during deployment. Which setting should you add to the AppSpec?

choices.text: Set RETAIN for file_exists_behavior in the AppSpec.
choices.explanation: This retains the conflicting existing file, which contradicts the requirement to make the new revision authoritative.

choices.text: Set DISALLOW for file_exists_behavior in the AppSpec.
choices.explanation: The deployment fails if the existing file is present, so it does not replace the file.

choices.text: Set OVERWRITE for file_exists_behavior in the AppSpec.
choices.explanation: When a deployed file conflicts with an existing file, this replaces the existing file with the file from the deployment revision.

choices.text: Enable rollback for the deployment group so the previous configuration is restored when a conflict occurs.
choices.explanation: This setting rolls back after a failed deployment; it does not make the new file authoritative or overwrite the existing one.

source.label: CodeDeploy AppSpecのfile_exists_behavior

learning.reason: You can specify how to handle a conflict with an existing file that was not managed by a previous deployment.
learning.concept: The deployment definition can distinguish files owned by the revision from files maintained separately and outside its scope.

title: Ensure deployment uses the verified image even if the tag moves
prompt: In ECS, a development team updates the same latest tag. The image digest was recorded during quality verification. After approval, you want replacement tasks to reliably use the verified image even if latest points to a different image. What should you specify in the task definition?

choices.text: Set the image tag to the commit message used for the build.
choices.explanation: There is no guarantee that an image can be referenced by that name, and it does not identify an immutable image content value.

choices.text: Use latest and restart the tasks multiple times to vary when they download the image.
choices.explanation: There is no guarantee that the content the tag points to later is the correct one.

choices.text: Set image to the ECR repository URI followed by @ and the verified sha256 digest.
choices.explanation: Even if the tag moves, the manifest referenced by the task definition does not change.

choices.text: Keep latest in image and increment only the task definition revision number.
choices.explanation: Pinning the task definition revision does not pin the contents of the mutable tag it references.

source.label: ECSタスク定義のコンテナイメージ

learning.reason: You can specify build contents by image digest.
learning.concept: A deployment that resolves the current tag value and one that explicitly specifies verified content have different guarantees.

title: Deploy the same template to each environment
prompt: The team wants to use the same SAM template for development, testing, and production, and reproduce each environment’s stack name, Region, and parameters consistently. They want to reduce the work of entering values manually and specify the target environment as an input to the deployment job. Which method should they use?

choices.text: Copy the SAM template for each environment and manually apply changes to shared resources.
choices.explanation: This creates divergent configurations and no longer meets the requirement to use the same template.

choices.text: Pass the same stack name and fixed parameters to all three environments, then adjust them in the console after deployment.
choices.explanation: The actual environment would depend on changes made outside the template, reducing reproducibility.

choices.text: Define environment-specific deploy parameters in samconfig.toml and explicitly select one with sam deploy --config-env.
choices.explanation: This allows deployments from the same template with reproducible options for each environment.

choices.text: Embed credentials and parameter values for every environment in the function build artifact.
choices.explanation: This makes an artifact unrelated to target selection depend on the environment and stores credentials unnecessarily.

source.label: SAM CLI設定ファイルの環境

learning.reason: SAM CLI configuration files can store command options by named environment.
learning.concept: Share the template and select only the environment-specific deployment parameters when deploying.

title: Specify a database restore source only in production
prompt: Use CloudFormation to create the production database for the first time from an existing snapshot. The testing environment starts with an empty database. Use the same template, and ensure that the DBSnapshotIdentifier property itself is not sent in the testing environment. Which expression should you use?

choices.text: Use Fn::If to return the string null in the testing environment.
choices.explanation: The string is passed as a value, so the property is not omitted.

choices.text: Use Fn::If to return the snapshot ID in production and AWS::NoValue in testing.
choices.explanation: This removes the property from the definition in the environment where the condition does not apply.

choices.text: Attach a production-only Condition to the entire resource.
choices.explanation: The empty database would not be created in the testing environment.

choices.text: Return an empty table name as the default value for DBSnapshotIdentifier.
choices.explanation: This leaves the property in place and supplies a name for a different kind of resource.

source.label: CloudFormation AWS::NoValue

learning.reason: A condition can remove a property itself, rather than only changing its value.
learning.concept: Distinguish between sending an empty string and not sending the property to the service at all.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Prevent p99 alarms from flapping during quiet periods
prompt: A CloudWatch alarm monitors the p99 of API calls. Its state changes based on a single request in the middle of the night, but it should still detect p99 degradation when there are enough requests. How can you keep the threshold and preserve the current state during periods when there are too few samples for a reliable statistic?

choices.text: Set the evaluation period to 1 so that the alarm always enters ALARM when a single observation exceeds the threshold.
choices.explanation: This leaves the cause of evaluating a small sample in place.

choices.text: Set EvaluateLowSampleCountPercentile to ignore for the percentile alarm.
choices.explanation: This can suppress state changes during periods when the sample count is too low for a statistically meaningful evaluation.

choices.text: Set TreatMissingData to notBreaching only.
choices.explanation: A period with a value reported from one request is not treated as missing data.

choices.text: Change p99 to Average and keep the same threshold.
choices.explanation: This no longer monitors upper-tail latency as p99, even when there are enough requests.

source.label: CloudWatchの低サンプル数とパーセンタイル

learning.reason: Distinguish between a missing data point and a percentile calculated from only a few samples.
learning.concept: Disabling evaluation at low sample counts prevents the alarm from changing state during those periods.

sourceLabel: CloudWatch low sample counts and percentiles

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Monitor only newly arriving log lines after deployment
prompt: For 30 minutes after starting a production deployment, an operator wants to display newly arriving ERROR events from multiple CloudWatch Logs log groups on one screen. They do not want to set up an aggregation of historical logs or a persistent destination, and will close the monitoring session when the work is done. Which feature should they use?

choices.text: Display only the total from CloudWatch metric filters instead of using Live Tail for each log group.
choices.explanation: This can measure the count, but it does not display the log lines themselves.

choices.text: Open a CloudWatch Logs Live Tail session and specify the target log groups and an ERROR filter pattern.
choices.explanation: Matching logs ingested from then on can be sent to the session while the operator works.

choices.text: Call GetLogEvents once for an old log stream name and display the output without refreshing it.
choices.explanation: This cannot continuously monitor later logs or multiple log groups.

choices.text: Change the log retention period to one day and export all logs, including older ones, each time.
choices.explanation: Changing retention does not provide a live display of newly arriving logs.

source.label: CloudWatch Logs Live Tail

learning.reason: A live session can follow newly ingested logs only while an investigation is in progress.
learning.concept: This serves a different purpose from searching over a time range or configuring a subscription that continuously delivers logs.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: The age of the oldest message alone cannot determine whether a backlog is stuck
prompt: In a standard SQS queue, the same message repeatedly fails processing each time it is received. It has not yet met the condition for moving to a DLQ. Even after ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage decreases, the application logs still show the same processing error. How should you interpret this metric while troubleshooting the error?

choices.text: Convert the displayed number of seconds into a receive count and use it as the individual message's ReceiveCount.
choices.explanation: Time and receive count are different quantities, and the metric does not identify an individual message.

choices.text: Assume processing became faster by the amount of time the metric decreased, and treat the same error as an old, lingering log entry.
choices.explanation: A decrease in the metric alone does not prove that the failing message was processed.

choices.text: Conclude from the age of the oldest message that the first message must have been processed in FIFO order.
choices.explanation: Standard queues do not guarantee strict ordering, and this interpretation does not account for redelivery behavior.

choices.text: Consider that an unprocessable message may be redelivered and no longer reflected in the metric; check receive and failure records and the DLQ state.
choices.explanation: The metric can reflect another message's age even while an older failed message remains in the queue.

source.label: SQSの最古メッセージ経過時間

learning.reason: In a standard queue, an unprocessable message that has been received several times may be moved toward the back of the queue.
learning.concept: A decrease in the metric is not evidence that this particular message was successfully processed and deleted.

sourceLabel: Age of the oldest SQS message

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: An environment variable is not expanded only in the task's health check
prompt: A health check in an ECS task definition uses CMD form. It fails because the same command uses the environment variable APP_PORT, which a shell must interpret, and a logical operator. The container has a shell and curl, and manually running the same operation in a shell succeeds. How should you modify the task definition?

choices.text: Change the task definition's health check to CMD-SHELL form.
choices.explanation: The shell in the container can interpret the environment variable and operator.

choices.text: Keep CMD form and only increase the number of retries.
choices.explanation: Repeating a command that is not interpreted by a shell does not expand the environment variable.

choices.text: Add a HEALTHCHECK in the Docker image using the same CMD form and leave the task definition unchanged.
choices.explanation: The health check in the ECS task definition is used, so the existing incorrect form remains.

choices.text: Extend the start period and wait for CMD to expand the environment variable.
choices.explanation: The start period controls when failures begin to count; it does not change how the command is evaluated.

source.label: ECSのコンテナヘルスチェック

learning.reason: CMD runs a command directly, whereas CMD-SHELL evaluates it through a shell.
learning.concept: Use a form that invokes a shell when the command relies on environment variable expansion or logical operators.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Lambda succeeds, but the REST client receives a 502
prompt: With a REST API Lambda proxy integration, the invoked function raises no exception, and its logs show that it returned JSON business data. The client receives a 502. In the latest change, the function began returning only the business data object directly as its output. Where should you make a correction?

choices.text: Only double the function timeout and return the same object.
choices.explanation: Execution completes, and the 502 will remain if the return value's format is not changed.

choices.text: Add statusCode only when the business data is empty, and return ordinary objects as they are.
choices.explanation: The valid proxy response format is required when returning ordinary business data as well.

choices.text: Return a numeric statusCode at the top level and put the business data in body as a JSON string.
choices.explanation: This matches the REST API proxy response format and lets the gateway construct the HTTP response.

choices.text: Enable API Gateway data caching and keep using an older response that succeeded.
choices.explanation: This does not fix the invalid format returned by new invocations, which will still fail on a cache miss.

source.label: API Gateway Lambdaプロキシ統合の出力形式

learning.reason: A REST proxy integration defines how the response must be wrapped.
learning.concept: Even when Lambda completes successfully, an output the gateway cannot interpret results in a failure.

sourceLabel: API Gateway Lambda proxy integration output format

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: A cached error is returned even after the origin recovers
prompt: An object deployment to an S3 origin behind CloudFront is delayed, and some edge locations receive a 404. Even after the object becomes available from S3, the same URL continues to return 404 for a while. Where should you adjust the configuration to shorten how long future 404s are retained while preserving the TTL for successful responses?

choices.text: Only configure a custom error response that returns 200 to users for 404s.
choices.explanation: Changing the status shown to users does not change the setting that controls how long the error is retained.

choices.text: Disable CloudFront compression to immediately invalidate only cached 404 responses.
choices.explanation: Compression affects content transfer format; it does not adjust error retention time.

choices.text: Lower Error Caching Minimum TTL in the custom error response for 404s, and also check the error cache duration specified by the origin.
choices.explanation: This can shorten the 404 cache duration without changing the normal TTL for 200 responses.

choices.text: Always set only the Default TTL in the successful-response cache policy to 0.
choices.explanation: This discards caching for successful files and does not directly configure retention for 404s.

source.label: CloudFrontのエラー応答のキャッシュ有効期間

learning.reason: The cache duration for error responses can be managed separately from the settings for successful objects.
learning.concept: Also account for the effect of cache headers returned by the origin and the 1-second minimum for an S3 origin.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Find the keys driving throttling without adding values to application logs
prompt: There are signs that writes are concentrated on a subset of keys in a DynamoDB base table, but you can see only the total number of throttled requests for the table. You want to identify the most frequently accessed or throttled keys without adding every primary key to application logs. What should you enable?

choices.text: Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery and restore the latest table.
choices.explanation: This feature restores data; it does not aggregate access patterns by key.

choices.text: Enable CloudWatch Contributor Insights for the table and review reports on frequently accessed and throttled keys.
choices.explanation: This helps isolate suspected hot keys without adding processing details to the application.

choices.text: Immediately add ReturnItemCollectionMetrics to every SDK call.
choices.explanation: This setting provides item collection metrics; it does not rank throttled keys.

choices.text: Display the Sum of ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits in CloudWatch and treat the time of the peak as the key string.
choices.explanation: Table-level consumption cannot identify an individual key.

source.label: DynamoDBのCloudWatch Contributor Insights

learning.reason: Table-level totals do not show which keys are driving the load.
learning.concept: Contributor Insights rules let you review key-level rankings for the target resource.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: New Fargate tasks cannot be placed despite available CPU quota
prompt: After scaling out an ECS Fargate service, new tasks that were using the same image successfully until just before now fail to start. The service events report that the target subnet has no available IP addresses for network interfaces. The account has ample CPU quota. How should you restore service within the same VPC?

choices.text: Add another subnet in the same VPC that has available IP addresses, and include it as a placement option in the service's network configuration.
choices.explanation: This provides IP addresses to assign to the new tasks' ENIs.

choices.text: Increase only the account's Fargate vCPU quota.
choices.explanation: Increasing the vCPU quota does not increase the number of available IP addresses in a subnet.

choices.text: Change the network mode to bridge and deploy on the existing Fargate capacity.
choices.explanation: Fargate requires awsvpc; switching to bridge cannot resolve this.

choices.text: Keep the same subnet and halve the task CPU.
choices.explanation: If the number of tasks does not change, they still need the same number of IP addresses for their ENIs.

source.label: ECS Fargateのawsvpcネットワーク

learning.reason: Each Fargate task uses a network interface and a private IP address.
learning.concept: CPU, container images, and subnet address capacity are consumed independently.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Investigate shard reads for a lagging consumer
prompt: You operate a Kinesis consumer that uses shared throughput. GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds continues to rise, and ReadProvisionedThroughputExceeded increases on some shards during the same period. PutRecord-related operations succeed, and application processing time has not changed. What cause should you investigate first?

choices.text: The writer is exceeding the PutRecord limit, and records that have not yet been ingested are being included in the age metric.
choices.explanation: The capacity exceeded in the scenario is on the read side, and records that have not been ingested cannot be read.

choices.text: CPU load on the consumer has increased, causing Kinesis to emit ReadProvisionedThroughputExceeded.
choices.explanation: This metric represents requests rejected by the stream's read limit; it does not measure reader CPU load.

choices.text: The data retention period is too short, so GetRecords is repeatedly reading records that have already expired.
choices.explanation: Expired records do not remain available for retrieval, and this would not explain the read throttling metric.

choices.text: Shared read capacity throttling on the affected shards is preventing the consumer from keeping up with new records.
choices.explanation: This explains both the increase in failed read requests and the rise in the age of the records retrieved.

source.label: Kinesis Data StreamsのCloudWatchメトリクス

learning.reason: Correlate record age with read-side capacity exceedances on the same shard and at the same time.
learning.concept: This distinguishes a lag caused by read throughput from failures to write records.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Measure latency only for the content served from the same bucket
prompt: An S3 bucket contains assets/ for static content delivery and private/ for internal documents. Operations staff want to track FirstByteLatency and 5xxErrors in CloudWatch only for requests to assets/. They do not want to incur additional charges for detailed metrics on internal documents. What should they configure?

choices.text: Filter S3 Inventory to assets/ and calculate response times and 5xx errors for each request from the inventory.
choices.explanation: Inventory lists objects and related information; it does not record per-request latency or response codes.

choices.text: Use CloudWatch's daily bucket-size metrics to find days when responses from assets/ were slow.
choices.explanation: BucketSizeBytes measures data volume; it does not measure time to first byte for the target requests.

choices.text: Use a prefix filter for assets/ in the request metrics configuration.
choices.explanation: This classifies requests for matching keys and aggregates the target latency and errors.

choices.text: Enable request metrics for the entire bucket and display the same aggregate as metrics for assets/.
choices.explanation: Requests for internal documents would also be included and charged, and the symptoms affecting assets/ could not be isolated.

source.label: S3リクエストメトリクスの設定

learning.reason: S3 request metrics can be scoped to a prefix or another filter.
learning.concept: Daily storage volume is a different metric from request counts and time to first byte.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Smooth out throttling caused by bursts of concurrent generation
prompt: An application uses on-demand inference with the same model in a single AWS Region on Amazon Bedrock. It receives a ThrottlingException only when many long requests arrive within a short time; the request and response contents are valid. Immediate synchronous responses are not required. How should the application continue processing within the quotas without changing the model or serving Region?

choices.text: Immediately retry every throttled request and send inputs of the same size in parallel.
choices.explanation: The original requests may overlap with the retries, making throttling more likely to continue.

choices.text: Lower only maxTokens for each request while keeping the input token count and concurrency unchanged.
choices.explanation: This can reduce output-token consumption, but it does not address bursts of long inputs or request-rate limits.

choices.text: Adjust queue draining and concurrency to match the model quotas, and retry throttled requests with exponential backoff and jitter.
choices.explanation: This can smooth bursts in token usage and request volume.

choices.text: Increase only the network timeout while keeping the send rate unchanged.
choices.explanation: Extending the client wait time does not make requests pass when the service rejects them for exceeding a quota.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockの推論クォータ

learning.reason: Check the request-rate and token quotas for the model and invocation path, then smooth the workload.
learning.concept: Avoid retrying large numbers of requests at once; distribute processing with a queue and varied wait times.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Handler is fast, but extension cleanup adds time at invocation end
prompt: After adding a monitoring extension, the Lambda handler duration is unchanged, but the time until the invocation ends has increased. You want to use a function's CloudWatch metrics to measure whether the extension is doing more work after the runtime signals that it has finished. Which metric should you use?

choices.text: Check Throttles.
choices.explanation: This counts rejected invocations; it does not measure post-runtime processing time for accepted invocations.

choices.text: Extend the CloudWatch Logs retention period to keep more records.
choices.explanation: This retains historical logs, but it does not configure a measurement of the time an extension spends at invocation end.

choices.text: Check Errors.
choices.explanation: This reports the number of errors, not post-runtime processing time during successful invocations.

choices.text: Check PostRuntimeExtensionsDuration.
choices.explanation: This metric measures the time extensions run after the runtime has completed.

source.label: Lambdaのパフォーマンスメトリクス

learning.reason: A metric is available to observe the interval between runtime completion and extension completion.
learning.concept: Distinguish initialization, handler execution, and extension cleanup when diagnosing duration.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Keep a small number of traces at low volume and control peaks
prompt: An API that uses X-Ray sampling rules receives 0–3 requests per second during normal operation and several thousand requests per second at peak. You want to guarantee the first request in each second when there is traffic, then trace only 5% of additional requests. Which rule should you specify?

choices.text: Set Reservoir size to 1 and Fixed rate to 1.0.
choices.explanation: This samples all requests, including those beyond the fixed quota.

choices.text: Set Reservoir size to 0 and Fixed rate to 0.05.
choices.explanation: This applies only a percentage to all requests and cannot ensure the first request in a low-volume second.

choices.text: Set Reservoir size to 5 and Fixed rate to 0.0.
choices.explanation: This captures up to the first five requests as a fixed quota and does not apply a 5% rate to additional requests.

choices.text: Set the sampling rule's Reservoir size to 1 and Fixed rate to 0.05.
choices.explanation: This reserves the fixed quota for each second and samples 5% of requests beyond it.

source.label: X-Rayのサンプリングルール

learning.reason: Use the fixed quota for each second first, then apply the percentage to requests beyond that quota.
learning.concept: Combining a fixed quota with an additional sampling rate can provide useful coverage at both low and high traffic volumes.

category: トラブルシューティングと最適化
examDomain: トラブルシューティングと最適化
title: Investigate slow searches by shard-level search processing
prompt: Some searches in Amazon OpenSearch Service are slow. You want to record in CloudWatch Logs which index and shard had long search processing time when a threshold is exceeded. Audit logs are configured, but they do not contain records of slow queries. What should you add? Select TWO.

choices.text: Enable publishing of search slow logs from the domain to CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: This provides a path for receiving search slow logs generated by the domain.

choices.text: Enable only indexing slow logs and interpret write time as search time.
choices.explanation: These measure indexing delays, not the time spent on search queries or fetches.

choices.text: Set the required Query and Fetch thresholds for search slow logs on the target index.
choices.explanation: This records shard-side search phases when they exceed the configured thresholds.

choices.text: Aggregate the domain-wide duration returned by the search API and infer the slow shard name from the total.
choices.explanation: A total duration alone cannot identify an individual shard in a target index.

choices.text: Only extend audit log retention and treat access timestamps as search duration.
